title: agent0 Code Review
abstract: agent0 is a single-user, local-first agent: a FastAPI web UI and a CLI around a multi-step tool loop on local Ollama models, with local speech in and out, conversation memory in SQLite, a stop button, context pruning and a small skill system. This page covers the repository at commit `d0bacbe` plus the changes up to 22 Oct 2026 (commit `c1338f9` and the uncommitted working tree); 317 tests pass.

Approvals, secrets, error handling, file backups, the secret-file rules and conversation storage are in reasonable shape. The open problems are in newer code: a stopped request can still be saved as a turn, tool results can still overflow the context window, and a symlink can lead the file tools outside the project. Several chat shortcuts still take over messages meant for the model, and `edit_file`'s `<script>` guard refuses some Python edits.

Skills work with the general model once the local-first prompt lists them, but the code model did not load the one skill it needed in two runs, so any rule that protects data should stay in the system prompt.

priorities.title: A stopped request is still stored
priorities.text: After Stop, the next request is sent the question with an error as its answer. The docs say it is not stored.

priorities.title: Tool results can still overflow the context window
priorities.text: Two newest results are never pruned and can each fill half the budget, and per-file caps are undone by a second cap, which can drop a whole file from the prompt.

priorities.title: The agent can read and write outside the project through a symlink
priorities.text: A symlink in the project that points outside is accepted; reads need no approval. The permissions doc says symlinks are covered.

priorities.title: The agent's own safety checks misfire
priorities.text: `verify_app` reports OK for broken Python, and the `<script>` check refuses every edit to some Python files.

priorities.title: Shortcuts take over ordinary messages
priorities.text: "Play chess with me" never reaches the model, a sentence about a meeting with a time can create an event without approval, and some ordinary questions are treated as file tasks.

priorities.title: The launchers still listen on the network or hardcode paths
priorities.text: The Windows launcher binds `0.0.0.0`; the fish launcher and systemd units bind localhost.

findings.title: Exceptions from tools and from Ollama are not caught: the stream aborts silently, the CLI crashes, and the model never sees the error
findings.detail: execute_tool calls func(**args) without try/except, and so does query_llm (lines 145, 226). Only the tools in tools/files.py and player.py accept **kwargs. Reproduced: read_calendar with {"month": "october"} raises TypeError out of stream_agent. Other realistic cases: get_news with {} (its registry description lists no arguments, but the signature requires `country`) raises TypeError. create_calendar_event with start 'tomorrow 12:00' raises ValueError from _parse_datetime, which only knows strptime formats. Ollama down or a timeout raises ConnectionError or ReadTimeout. A model returning a list as `action` also crashes at line 257 (TOOLS.get(list) raises TypeError: unhashable). Effects: /ask_stream has already sent 200, so the connection just drops. There is no error event, and chat.js leaves the spinner and last status ('Executing tool: ...') up forever. The CLI `__main__` loop (line 413) has no try and exits. The error is never fed back, so the model can't fix its argument names.
findings.suggestion: Wrap execute_tool in try/except and add `Result: ERROR <Type>: <msg>. Signature: <inspect.signature(func)>` to the context, then continue the loop. Wrap query_llm and yield {event: 'error'}. Check that `action` is a str before the TOOLS lookup. Add a try/except around run_agent in the CLI loop.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and reproduced the bug in memory, with log_event patched to a no-op so nothing was written.

- agent.py:121-128 (execute_tool) calls func(**args) with no try. The call at agent.py:309 is outside the try/except at 288-302, which only covers request_permission. query_llm at agent.py:145 and 226 is also unguarded, and core/llm.py:38-39 calls requests.post and raise_for_status with no handling.
- Nothing upstream stops these inputs. The read_calendar tool is low risk with no RULES entry, and get_news and verify_app are "auto" in config/settings.py, so request_permission auto-approves all three. Execution happens inside the stream.

Reproduced by driving stream_agent with a mocked query_llm:
- read_calendar with {"month":"october"} raised TypeError "unexpected keyword argument 'month'". The last event yielded was {'event':'status','message':'Executing tool: read_calendar'} and no error event was emitted.
- get_news with {} raised TypeError "missing 1 required positional argument: 'country'" (tools/web.py:59).
- verify_app with {"path":...} raised TypeError.
- An action given as a list raised "TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'" at the TOOLS.get call on line 257.
- query_llm raising requests.ConnectionError propagated straight out.
- _parse_datetime("tomorrow 12:00") raises ValueError, as claimed.

Effect on the web: /ask_stream (core/agent_routes.py:191-195) has no try around stream_agent. Starlette sends http.response.start before it iterates the body, so uvicorn can only close the connection. In static/chat.js:77-79, reader.read() then rejects, which is an unhandled rejection in the submit handler. handleStreamEvent never receives an error event, so the thinking image and the last status stay on screen.

Effect on the CLI: the __main__ loop (agent.py:389-413) has no try, so it exits with a traceback.

In every case the error is never added to context, so the model cannot correct its arguments.

No test covers any of this: grep of tests/ finds no exception or error-event case for the agent loop.

Minor corrections, none of which change the verdict:
1. Not every function in tools/files.py takes **kwargs. get_project_structure() (tools/files.py:41) takes no arguments and is "auto" in RULES, so any arguments the model passes also raise TypeError mid-stream. This widens the bug.
2. create_calendar_event is "ask" in RULES. On the web it only runs after approval, and the permission card posts to the non-streaming /ask route. There the outer `except Exception` in core/agent_routes.py:147 catches the ValueError and renders it as an error. So that example does not cause the silent stream drop; it does crash the CLI, and the model still never sees the error.
3. More generally, /ask catches all exceptions. The silent hang is specific to /ask_stream, which is the default chat path, and to the CLI.

Severity high is reasonable: Ollama being down or a zero-argument tool receiving guessed arguments are both realistic.
findings.status_note: Tool exceptions go back to the model as an ERROR result with the tool's signature, so it can correct itself. Ollama errors become an error event, and the stream turns any other exception into an error event.

findings.title: The duplicate-call check blocks the re-verify and re-read steps that the prompt and tools ask for
findings.detail: `attempted` is never cleared, so a second identical call is refused for the rest of the run, even after the files changed. Reproduced: verify_app returns FAILED, edit_file runs, then verify_app is refused with 'You already ran this exact action... Do not repeat it'. That contradicts SYSTEM_PROMPT ('If it reports FAILED, fix the problem before finishing'). Likewise edit_file's own error tells the model to 'read the file again and copy the exact text' (tools/files.py:410), but read_files with the same path is refused, so the model has to edit from stale content.
findings.suggestion: Clear `attempted` after any successful mutating tool (write_file, edit_file, extract_inline_scripts, create_calendar_event), or include a 'state version' that each mutation increments in the signature.
findings.verification_note:
Traced agent.py:_run_steps. `attempted = set()` is created once at line 203, before the loop. Each call's signature is `action + json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)` (line 276), and it is added at line 284. Nothing ever removes entries, and no mutating tool clears the set. verify_app takes no arguments, so every call to it has the same signature, `verify_app:{}`. That means the second call is always refused, whatever happened in between. No tests cover this (grep for 'attempted' or 'already ran' in tests/ finds nothing).

I reproduced it without writing anything. I monkeypatched agent.log_event, try_local_answer, planned_first_decision, request_permission and execute_tool, and scripted query_llm to return this sequence: read_files, edit_file (fails with 'not found'), verify_app (returns FAILED), edit_file (succeeds), verify_app, read_files (same path), none. Only ['read_files', 'edit_file', 'verify_app', 'edit_file'] actually ran. The second verify_app and the second read_files were both refused with 'You already ran this exact action... Do not repeat it' (lines 278-283). So after a fix, the model can only see the stale FAILED result. This contradicts config/system_prompt.py:41-42 ('If it reports FAILED, fix the problem before finishing'). Each refusal also uses up one of the 8 steps (MAX_STEPS, line 208).

One detail is overstated. When edit_file fails with 'old_text not found in file - read the file again...' (tools/files.py:410), the file has not changed. So the earlier read_files result in context is still accurate, and the refused re-read costs a wasted step and a contradictory instruction rather than stale content. The content is only stale when a successful write_file, edit_file or extract_inline_scripts ran between the first read and the refused re-read. The verify_app case alone is enough to confirm the bug as reported (medium severity, agent.py:277). The suggested fix also holds up: clear `attempted` after a successful mutating tool, or put a state version in the signature.
findings.status_note: The repeat guard starts over after a high-risk tool (write_file, edit_file, extract_inline_scripts) runs, so verify_app and read_files can run again after an edit.

findings.title: `parse_decision` still breaks on code fences, in the fallback for calls written as JSON text
findings.detail:
If ``` appears anywhere in the text, the text is split on ``` before json.loads is tried. Reproduced: json.dumps({action: 'write_file', arguments: {path: 'NOTES.md', content: '# Setup
```bash
pip install x
```'}}) gives None, with or without a surrounding ```json fence. So writing or editing any Markdown or README content that contains a code block is impossible. The loop spends both JSON retries, and then line 246 returns the raw write_file JSON to the user as the final answer.
findings.suggestion: Try json.loads(text) first. Only strip a fence when the whole reply is wrapped in one (anchored regex `^```(?:json)?\s*(.*)```\s*$`, DOTALL). Otherwise use json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode from the first '{'. The real fix is Ollama `format`/structured outputs (see the native tool-calling improvement).
findings.verification_note:
I traced it in agent.py:69-89. When the raw reply contains ``` anywhere, line 70 splits the whole text on ```. The first fragment that starts with '{' replaces `text` (lines 74-76). For a JSON object whose string value contains ```, that fragment is the object cut off in the middle of the string, e.g. '{"action": "write_file", ..., "content": "# Setup\n'. json.loads fails on it. The fallback at lines 82-89 then searches that same cut-off text and finds no closing '}', so the function returns None.

I reproduced this read-only with the venv. parse_decision(json.dumps({'action':'write_file','arguments':{'path':'NOTES.md','content':'# Setup\n```bash\npip install x\n```'}})) returns None, with or without a ```json fence around it. An edit_file decision with ``` in `new` also returns None.

Nothing upstream prevents this. core/llm.py query_llm sends no Ollama `format`/schema parameter, so the reply is free text. No test covers parse_decision at all: grep finds no reference in tests/, and test_agent_flow.py never exercises backticks.

In the loop, a None decision uses up json_retries_left (2) at lines 237-244. After that, line 246 returns the raw JSON string as the final answer, so the write never runs.

The reviewer understated the scope. It also breaks any {"action":"none","response":"...```python...```"} final answer, which I reproduced as returning None. In the tool loop, that means any final answer that contains a code block comes back to the user as raw JSON. In try_local_answer (line 148), a direct answer with a code block (e.g. "how do I write a for loop in Python") parses as None. That answer is thrown away, and the request is escalated to the much slower qwen3-coder tool loop. The location, mechanism, failure scenario and suggested fix (try json.loads first, strip a fence only when it wraps the whole reply, then raw_decode from the first '{') are all accurate. Medium severity is reasonable.
findings.status_note:
Tool calls no longer go through parse_decision. It remains only as a fallback for calls written as JSON text, where the fence bug still applies.

Originally reported as: parse_decision fails on valid JSON whenever a string value contains ``` (Markdown code blocks)

findings.title: The step history leaves out the tool arguments, so the model can't tell which file or query each result belongs to
findings.detail: context += 'Action: {action}\nResult: {result}', without the args. read_files with a single path returns the bare file content with no filename. Scenario: 'move function X from a.py to b.py' runs read_files(a.py) and then read_files(b.py). The prompt shows two 'Action: read_files' blocks with no paths, so the model has to guess which content is which before calling edit_file(path, old_text). The dedupe message 'its result is above' points at a result the model can't identify. Results that are lists or dicts are also added as Python repr, not JSON.
findings.suggestion: Record `Action: {action} {json.dumps(args)}` and serialise results with json.dumps(result, default=str, ensure_ascii=False) when they aren't str. With /api/chat this becomes an assistant tool_call message followed by a tool message.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and reproduced it. At agent.py:339 each step is added to the context as `f"
Step {step}:
Action: {action}
Result: {result}
"`. `args` is never written there, and neither is the raw decision JSON. It is only used for the dedupe signature at line 276 and for log_event at lines 317-323. When read_files (tools/files.py:113-141) gets a single path it returns the bare file content, and a missing file returns just "File not found" with no name.

The repeat guard at agent.py:278-282 adds "its result is above" under another bare "Action: read_files", so it cannot say which earlier block it means. A list of paths returns a dict (files.py:119), and the f-string writes it into the prompt as a Python repr: single quotes, with newlines turned into literal `
` text.

No guard elsewhere adds the args, and no test checks the context format. tests/test_agent_flow.py only stubs query_llm.

I reproduced it read-only by monkeypatching query_llm, request_permission, needs_tools and log_event, then sending read_files(tools/registry.py), read_files(config/settings.py), read_files(paths=[README.md, CLAUDE.md]), read_files(nope.py) and a repeat. The last prompt contained:
- 'Step 0:
Action: read_files
Result: TOOLS = {...'
- 'Step 1:
Action: read_files
Result: # rules, flags...'
- "Step 2:
Action: read_files
Result: {'README.md': '# agent0\n\nA local-first...'"
- 'Step 3:
Action: read_files
Result: File not found'
- 'Step 4:
Action: read_files
Result: You already ran this exact ac...'

None of these blocks names a path. The model can only guess from the step order, and its own earlier decision isn't in the context to confirm that order.

Location, mechanism and severity (medium: it hurts multi-file edit tasks but doesn't crash) all hold. One caveat on the suggested fix: `json.dumps` on the dict result still escapes newlines to `
`, so file contents would still be one long escaped line. Rendering a dict result as per-file sections such as `=== path ===
<content>`, plus recording `Action: {action} {json.dumps(args)}`, would read better. Moving to /api/chat tool messages would change core/llm.py's contract. Just adding the args at line 339 changes nothing outside agent.py.
findings.status_note: The loop keeps a chat history: each tool call with its arguments, followed by its result.

findings.title: Neither prompt gives today's date, so relative dates either crash or become wrong-year events
findings.detail: SYSTEM_PROMPT and LOCAL_ONLY_PROMPT (agent.py:24-41) have no current date or time. create_calendar_event needs a date _parse_datetime can read (strptime formats only; 'tomorrow 12:00' raises ValueError, which then aborts the stream as described in the exception finding). The model either passes the relative phrase through (crash) or makes up an absolute date from its training period (an event in the wrong year). Local-first answers to 'what's today's date' or 'how long until Christmas' are also wrong. Example: 'put lunch with Kari on my calendar tomorrow at noon' once the view-shortcut hijack is fixed.
findings.suggestion: Add 'Current date/time: {datetime.now():%A %Y-%m-%d %H:%M}' to both prompts at call time, and state the date format create_calendar_event expects (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM).
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and could not refute it. Neither prompt has a date: SYSTEM_PROMPT (config/system_prompt.py:3-62) and LOCAL_ONLY_PROMPT (agent.py:24-41) contain no date, time or 'today', and _run_steps (agent.py:217-224) adds only the tool list and context. query_llm (core/llm.py:27-44) sends a bare /api/generate payload with no system or date field, so no date is added anywhere else.

_parse_datetime (features/calendar/calendar.py:27-81) only uses strptime and fromisoformat. 'tomorrow 12:00', 'tomorrow at noon' and 'next friday 12:00' all raise ValueError. create_event (calendar.py:169) calls it without a guard. execute_tool (agent.py:120-127) runs at agent.py:303 with no try/except, so the ValueError escapes the generator.

Today's shortcuts do not catch a request like this. For 'add a meeting with Kari tomorrow at 12', parse_create_command returns None because CREATE_SINGLE_RE needs 'on <date> at'. is_calendar_request is False, and needs_tools is False. So the request goes local-first and then to the tool loop.

I reproduced the crash read-only, with query_llm and log_event mocked and permission set to approved. The stream goes through 'Executing tool: create_calendar_event' and then the generator raises 'ValueError: Unable to parse date/time: tomorrow 12:00'. Where that lands: /ask_stream's event_stream (core/agent_routes.py:191-193) has no handler, so the NDJSON stream aborts. /ask's outer except shows the error text. The CLI's __main__ loop crashes.

No test covers relative dates or prompt date context. tests/test_calendar.py only uses absolute 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' strings, and test_agent_flow.py mocks create_event.

Two small caveats, neither of which refutes the finding:
- The reviewer's example ('put lunch with Kari on my calendar tomorrow at noon') currently contains 'my calendar', so is_calendar_request catches it and only shows the calendar view, as the reviewer says. 'add a meeting with Kari tomorrow at 12' reaches the bug today.
- RULES['create_calendar_event'] = 'ask' (config/settings.py:9) shows the made-up start value on the permission card before anything is written, so the wrong-year case is visible to the user before approval. Approving the relative-phrase args always crashes.

What the model outputs varies from run to run, but the missing date and the crash path are certain.
findings.status_note: The system message includes the current date and time, and the prompt gives the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM format for calendar events.

findings.title: An empty Ollama response comes back as the whole JSON body, which then shows up as a blank answer
findings.detail: `body.get('response') or body.get('text') or json.dumps(body)`: when response is '' (for example the model spent its output on thinking, or hit its length limit), query_llm returns the Ollama metadata dict as JSON. parse_decision accepts it as a dict, and try_local_answer returns decision.get('response', raw), which is ''. Reproduced with a fake body {response: '', thinking: '...', done: true}: stream_agent yields final_response ''. chat.js hides the card when response is falsy, so the user sees nothing. In the tool loop the same body becomes "no tool called 'None'".
findings.suggestion: Return body.get('response', ''). Treat an empty string as a failure (raise, or return None and escalate), and log done_reason. Set `think` explicitly for the JSON-only calls.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the path and reproduced it with read-only snippets that monkeypatch requests.post.

- **Where it starts:** `core/llm.py:43` runs `body.get("response") or body.get("text") or json.dumps(body)`. An empty string is falsy, so when Ollama returns an empty `response` the whole metadata body is serialised to JSON and returned.
- **Local path:** `parse_decision` (`agent.py:58-91`) accepts that JSON because it is a dict. It has no "action" key, so `try_local_answer` (`agent.py:156-158`) treats it as action None and returns `decision.get("response", raw)`, which is `''`. Because the result is `''` and not None, `_run_steps` (`agent.py:195-198`) emits `{'event': 'final_response', 'response': ''}` and does not escalate.
  - Reproduced with body `{response:'', thinking:'hmm...', done:True, done_reason:'stop'}`: `query_llm` returned the JSON string, `try_local_answer` returned `''`, and the last event of `_run_steps` was `final_response` with `''`.
  - `static/chat.js:109-114` hides `streamCard` when `event.response` is falsy, so the user sees nothing.
  - The fallback makes this worse than having none. If `query_llm` had returned `''` itself, `parse_decision('')` would give None, `try_local_answer` would return None, and the request would correctly go on to the tool loop.
- **Tool loop:** reproduced with body `{response:'', done_reason:'length'}`. The output was "LLM chose action: None", then "No such tool 'None', retrying..." twice, then `{'event': 'error', 'message': 'Unknown action: None'}` (`agent.py:249-271`).
- **No guard or test:** nothing elsewhere catches this. `tests/test_llm.py` only covers a non-empty `response` and streaming.
- **Can it happen in practice?** Yes, but I haven't seen it yet:
  - Ollama is 0.34.4, and `query_llm` never sets `think` or `num_predict`.
  - The logged qwen3:8b outputs contain no `<think>` tags, so thinking text is going into a separate field. A reply that spends everything on thinking, or stops early, would therefore leave `response` empty.
  - None of the 1449 logged `llm_raw_decision` entries in `local_storage/logs.txt` contains `done_reason`, and none has an empty raw value.
  - So the bug is real but has not happened in recorded use. Low severity is right.

The suggested fix is appropriate: use `body.get('response', '')`, treat an empty response as a failure so the request escalates, log `done_reason`, and set `think` explicitly for the JSON-only calls.
findings.status_note: Resolved: query_llm was removed. chat() returns the message or raises LLMError.

findings.title: Use Ollama /api/chat with native tools, or at least `format` structured outputs, instead of hand-written JSON over /api/generate
findings.detail: The loop rebuilds one flat prompt string each step and parses free text with heuristics (fence splitting, outer-brace fallback, five argument key aliases, two retry budgets). The logs show the cost: invented actions such as 'write_response', 'final_response', 'ask_stream', 'handle_audio_file', and a reply that copied the agent's own {"event": "error"} JSON. Registry descriptions mostly don't list parameters (get_news needs `country`; read_files/search_files/search_web parameter names aren't given). decision_args also silently drops `arguments` sent as a JSON string, which is common in OpenAI-style output.
findings.suggestion: Add a `parameters` JSON schema to each registry entry, or derive one from inspect.signature. Call /api/chat with messages=[system, user, assistant tool_calls, tool results] and tools=<schemas>; qwen3-coder supports native tool calls. Alternatively, pass format=<JSON schema with action enum = TOOLS + 'none'> to /api/generate. This removes parse_decision's guessing, both retry paths, the fence bug and invented tool names. Set think=false for the decision calls.
findings.verification_note:
The main claim holds up. core/llm.py:27-44 sends one flat prompt to /api/generate with no `format`, `tools` or `think`, and agent.py:210-226 rebuilds that prompt string on every step. agent.py:58-91 does the parsing with heuristics: it splits on fences, then falls back to the span from the first `{` to the last `}`. agent.py:113 tries five argument keys, and agent.py:204-205 keeps two separate retry counters. I checked each failure mode against the code:
(a) Fence bug. parse_decision(json.dumps({"action":"write_file","arguments":{"path":"x.md","content":"```bash\nls\n```"}})) returns None, because split("```") cuts through the JSON string.
(b) decision_args({"arguments":"{\"path\":\"agent.py\"}"}) returns {}.
(c) A real qwen3-coder reply at local_storage/logs.txt line 1121 (2026-09-25) contained two JSON objects, and the outer-brace fallback could not parse it.
(d) get_news(country) at tools/web.py:59 requires `country`, but tools/registry.py:38-42 never mentions it. read_files, search_files and search_web also don't name their parameters. Calling get_news with {} raises TypeError in execute_tool (agent.py:309), and nothing catches it.
The suggestion is technically sound. Ollama 0.34.4 is installed, and `ollama show qwen3-coder:30b` lists the capabilities completion and tools.

Several details are wrong, though.
1. The log evidence is stale. 'write_response' (line 33), 'handle_audio_file' (366), 'final_response' (367), 'ask_stream' (398) and the copied {"event":"error"} reply (399) all date from 2026-09-02 to 09-04. That is before commit 3f29418 (2026-09-24), which switched the tool loop to qwen3-coder:30b, removed read_email and rewrote agent.py. I parsed every llm_raw_decision logged after that commit: no action falls outside TOOLS. The parse failures listed above are real; invented tool names are not a current symptom.
2. "Set think=false for the decision calls" is aimed at the wrong call. qwen3-coder:30b has no thinking capability, so it changes nothing for the tool-loop decisions. It does matter for try_local_answer (agent.py:145), which uses OLLAMA_MODEL=qwen3:8b. That model's thinking capability defaults to true, and the logs contain no <think> text, so the thinking tokens are generated (costing CPU time) but query_llm discards them.
3. This changes a contract. The tests monkeypatch query_llm(prompt, model=None) at tests/test_agent_flow.py:13/35/58/87/105/142 and tests/test_llm.py. OLLAMA_URL (core/llm.py:5) includes the /api/generate path, so moving to /api/chat changes what that environment variable means.
findings.corrected:
core/llm.py:27 and agent.py:58-118, 204-226: the tool loop sends hand-written JSON over Ollama /api/generate without `format` or native `tools`. The parser fails in ways I verified:
- A JSON string value containing ``` (for example write_file content holding Markdown code blocks) makes parse_decision return None, so the loop retries and finally returns the raw JSON as the answer.
- A reply with two JSON objects cannot be parsed (logs.txt line 1121, qwen3-coder, 2026-09-25).
- decision_args silently drops `arguments` when it arrives as a JSON string.
The registry descriptions also leave out required parameters. get_news(country) is described only as "Get latest news headlines", so a call with {} raises an uncaught TypeError from execute_tool (agent.py:309). read_files, search_files and search_web don't name their parameters either.

Suggested fix: add a parameter schema to each registry entry, then either call /api/chat with tools= (installed qwen3-coder:30b reports the `tools` capability) or pass format=<JSON schema with an action enum> to /api/generate.

This is a design change. It alters the query_llm contract that the tests mock, the registry entry shape, and the meaning of the OLLAMA_URL environment variable.

Corrections to the original finding:
- The invented-action and copied-error-event examples all come from logs dated 2026-09-02 to 09-04. That predates the qwen3-coder switch and loop rewrite in commit 3f29418. I found no invented actions after it.
- think=false does nothing for qwen3-coder, which has no thinking capability. It belongs on the qwen3:8b local-first call in try_local_answer (agent.py:145), where thinking is on by default and quietly costs CPU time.
findings.status_note: The tool loop uses /api/chat with Ollama's built-in tool calling, still fully local. Schemas live in tools/registry.py. The local-first check uses structured output. Fallbacks read calls the model writes into its text (qwen3-coder markup or JSON).

findings.title: Two newest tool results are exempt from pruning and can each fill half the context budget
findings.detail: MAX_READ_CHARS = 100000 chars (tools/files.py:10), roughly 25k+ tokens, while OLLAMA_NUM_CTX = 16384. Reading 3 files (README.md, text_to_speech.py, tts.js) is already 40k chars. Results are appended for up to 8 steps with no cap, and the prompt order puts SYSTEM_PROMPT, the tool list and the user request at the START. That is the part Ollama truncates first, which is the failure the comment in core/llm.py:18-20 describes.
findings.suggestion: Limit each result added to the context (e.g. about 8-12k chars, with an explicit '[truncated - use read_files with a narrower target]' note). Shrink older results to one-line summaries once a step is done. Repeat the user request and the JSON contract at the end of the prompt. Optionally estimate tokens (chars/3.5) and raise num_ctx or summarise when close to the limit.
findings.verification_note:
I checked the premise against the code and it holds.

- **No limit on the context.** agent.py:202 starts `context` with the user request. Line 339 appends the full `Result: {result}` after every tool call, and lines 239, 262 and 278 append retry and correction notes. Nothing ever trims or summarises it.
- **Instructions come first.** The prompt at lines 211-218 is SYSTEM_PROMPT (1838 chars), then the tool list (1520 chars), then `context`. The user request sits at the start of `context`, so all the instructions are at the front.
- **The loop and the limits.** MAX_STEPS is 8 (line 208). core/llm.py:21 sets num_ctx to 16384 and sends it with every request. tools/files.py:10 allows MAX_READ_CHARS = 100000 per file.
- **No limit across several files.** Given a list of paths, `read_files` returns a dict of up to 100k chars per file (files.py:118-119). tools/web.py:38 caps each URL at 20k chars, but there is no limit on how many URLs.
- **The 40k figure.** README.md + features/audio/text_to_speech.py + features/audio/static/tts.js come to 5277 + 19247 + 14501 = 39,025 chars. That is about 11-13k tokens before the ~3.4k-char prompt and the model's own output, so it is close to 16384.
- **A single read can overflow.** No source file in the repo is over 19k chars. But `_safe_path` only blocks paths outside the project, so `read_files('local_storage/logs.txt')` works. That file is 640KB and returns 100k chars, roughly 25-30k tokens, well over num_ctx. Files under venv/ can be read the same way.
- **What Ollama does on overflow.** The Ollama journal on this machine (version 0.34.4) shows `n_ctx_slot = 16384, n_keep = 4` and a `truncated` field on each slot. When a prompt is too long, it keeps only the first 4 tokens and drops from the front. That removes SYSTEM_PROMPT, the tool list and the user request first, which is exactly what the comment at core/llm.py:18-20 warns about. The journal still on disk shows no actual overflow yet (largest prompt was 3642 tokens), so this is a real structural risk rather than something observed.

**Caveats on the suggestion (they don't refute the finding):**
- `read_files` has no line or offset parameter, so a "[truncated - use read_files with a narrower target]" note gives the model nothing it can act on. A range parameter would need to be added, or the note should point to search_files.
- A hard cap of 8-12k chars per result would cut text_to_speech.py (19k) in the middle.
- Shrinking older results to one-line summaries could break edit_file flows that need the exact old text from an earlier read.
- A total budget for the whole context, which shrinks the oldest results first, plus repeating the user request and the JSON contract at the end of the prompt, is safer.
- There is already a "do NOT write this back" truncation note at files.py:136-139, and it should be kept.
findings.status_note: core/context.py now caps one oversized result and stubs older ones before each model call. See the new findings for the gaps that remain. Originally reported as: The context has no size limit; one file read can exceed num_ctx, and Ollama drops the instructions first

findings.title: No conversation memory: every request starts fresh
findings.detail: _run_steps starts with only 'User request: ...'. Follow-ups such as 'what about Friday?' or 'ok, apply that change' get no context; the only state kept between turns is player._last_candidates. The system prompt's '3. Then propose changes' step ends the run with a proposal the user can't approve without retyping the whole task.
findings.suggestion: Keep a short history of recent user and assistant turns per session (in memory or local_storage), included as chat messages. This fits naturally with the /api/chat migration.
findings.verification_note: The premise holds. In agent.py, _run_steps starts at line 163, and its tool-loop context is built at line 202 as `context = f"User request: {user_input}\n"`. Nothing earlier is added to it. core/llm.py:query_llm sends one stateless `prompt` to /api/generate: there is no `messages` array and Ollama's returned `context` tokens are not reused. The local-first step (try_local_answer, LOCAL_ONLY_PROMPT) also formats only the current user_input. core/agent_routes.py (/ask and /ask_stream) and static/chat.js send only the current `input` field. A grep for history, conversation and messages in .py/.js/.html files finds nothing; request.session is used only for auth (core/auth.py). The only conversation state between turns is features/audio/player._last_candidates, as the finding says. One concrete case: agent.py:181 and core/agent_routes.py's shortcut_text_response both end a calendar create with "Would you like to see your calendar?". A reply of "yes" fails is_calendar_request (it requires "calendar" in the text), so it reaches the local model with no context. The '3. Then propose changes' point is in config/system_prompt.py:21-25. Whether the model stops with an action:"none" proposal depends on the model, but nothing in the code would carry that proposal into the next turn. Adding per-session history would not break any existing contract. SessionMiddleware is already mounted (core/ui.py), so a session key is available on the web side. Minor nit: line 163 is the function definition; the fresh-start context line is 202. Severity low / improvement is appropriate.
findings.status_note: Conversations are stored in SQLite and the newest turns are sent with each question (core/conversations.py, storage/); search_history reaches earlier sessions.

findings.title: 'Max steps reached' throws away what already happened
findings.detail: A denial ends the task immediately, so the model can't choose an alternative or explain. Hitting MAX_STEPS returns a fixed string even if files were already written or edited, and the user isn't told which.
findings.suggestion: Add the denial to the context as 'Result: user denied this action' and continue. On max steps, return a summary of the actions run (from the log or the attempted list), or ask the model for one final summary with tools disabled.
findings.verification_note:
I checked the finding against the code and it holds. In agent.py:304-306, `if not approved:` yields `{"event": "final_response", "response": "Action denied"}` and returns. The denial is never added to `context`, so the model gets no chance to pick another action or explain. After the loop, agent.py:341 yields the fixed string "Max steps reached without conclusion." run_agent repeats the same default at agent.py:355. By then, earlier iterations may already have run execute_tool, for example write_file or edit_file (agent.py:309). Those runs are recorded only in `context`, in log_event (tool_execution) and in `attempted`, and none of these reach the final response. The only place the user sees tool names is the transient "Executing tool: X" status events. In the web UI each new status overwrites the last (static/chat.js:15-19 showStatus), and the plain /ask route only prints them to server stdout. So the user is never told which tools ran. Neither behavior is handled anywhere else, and no test references either string, so changing them breaks no tests. Low severity is reasonable.

There is one caveat for the denial suggestion; it complicates the fix but doesn't make it wrong. After a denial on the web, the browser posts back to /ask with a single decision (templates/components/permission_card.html, core/agent_routes.py:27-34), and _run_steps replays from scratch. Decisions are keyed by action name only (core/permission.py:26-27). That causes two problems if the loop continues after a denial. First, every later call to the denied tool is denied automatically, even with different args, which can burn steps until MAX_STEPS unless the context message says the tool is off-limits. Second, if the model then requests a different gated tool, the next round trip carries only that new decision, so the earlier denial is forgotten and the user can be asked again about the action they rejected. This statelessness already hurts multi-approval runs today, so it isn't new, but the fix should account for it. The CLI path (decisions=None, input() prompt) has no such problem.
findings.corrected: The finding is accurate as stated (agent.py:304-306 and 341, plus the duplicate default at agent.py:355). One addition: on the web, continuing after a denial interacts with the stateless replay that keeps only one decision per round trip (core/agent_routes.py:27-34, core/permission.py:26-27). The context note for a denial should say the tool is off-limits for this request, not just that one call was denied.
findings.status_note:
A denial now goes back to the model, which finishes with an answer. 'Max steps reached' still throws away the work.

Originally reported as: 'Action denied' and 'Max steps reached' throw away what already happened

findings.title: Several test modules still write to the real local_storage/logs.txt
findings.detail: test_llm_direct_answer returns prose, so try_local_answer returns None, and the result only comes back after 2 JSON retries. Verified: 4 LLM calls, 3 to qwen3-coder:30b. The local-first success path ({action: none}) is never tested. There are no tests for tool exceptions, multi-approval resume, dedupe after a mutation, parse_decision edge cases (fences inside strings), or the unknown-action retry. log_event isn't patched, so every pytest run appends to local_storage/logs.txt: 601 'Team sync' and 341 'largest mountain' entries out of 2145 lines.
findings.suggestion: Add tests/conftest.py with an autouse fixture that points core.logger.LOG_FILE at tmp_path. Make the direct-answer test return {"action":"none","response":...} and assert a single LLM call. Add regression tests for each bug above.
findings.verification_note:
I checked each claim against the code and by running it.

(1) `test_llm_direct_answer` (`tests/test_agent_flow.py:12-17`) stubs `query_llm` to return plain prose. Because the prose has no JSON in it, `parse_decision` returns None, so `try_local_answer` (`agent.py:148-154`) returns None. The agent then enters the tool loop and uses both JSON retries (`agent.py:237-244`). The prose only comes back through the fallback at `agent.py:246`. I ran this scenario with a call-counting stub. It made 4 calls, with models `[None, 'qwen3-coder:30b', 'qwen3-coder:30b', 'qwen3-coder:30b']`, and returned the prose. So the test passes, but only through the fallback path.

(2) No test exercises the success path where the local model answers directly (`{"action": "none"}` on the first call). Every other test either starts with `{"action":"needs_tools"}`, returns a tool action (so `try_local_answer` returns None), or skips the LLM through the calendar/play shortcuts. I searched `tests/` for `try_local_answer`, `parse_decision`, `needs_tools`, `planned_first_decision`, and for tests of a tool raising an exception, an unknown action, or the dedupe of repeated calls. None of these is tested. The only other agent-related tests are the calendar shortcut tests in `test_calendar.py`, which don't reach the loop.

(3) There is no `tests/conftest.py`, and no test patches `log_event` or `LOG_FILE`. `core/logger.py:5` sets `LOG_FILE = "local_storage/logs.txt"` as a path relative to the working directory, and `log_event` reads that module global each time it's called. So every pytest run appends to the real log. I grepped the log (I didn't read it in full) and found entries matching the exact test payloads, such as the `search_web` 'largest mountain' result with the Wikipedia URL and the `create_calendar_event` 'Team sync' entry dated 2026-09-10 10:00. The counts are now 701 'Team sync' and 349 'largest mountain' out of 2221 lines. They have grown since the reviewer counted (601/341 of 2145) because other test runs have happened since; that growth is more evidence of the problem.

The suggested fix is safe. `LOG_FILE` is referenced only in `core/logger.py` (lines 5, 11 and 18), no test reads the log, and `log_event` resolves the global at call time. So an autouse fixture that monkeypatches `core.logger.LOG_FILE` to a path under `tmp_path` works without side effects. Changing the direct-answer stub to `{"action":"none","response":...}` and asserting a single LLM call would correctly cover the local-first success path. This only changes tests, so it is not a design change.
findings.status_note:
The direct-answer test now makes one structured-output call, and the risky agent paths have tests. Other test modules still write to the real local_storage/logs.txt.

Originally reported as: Tests miss the risky paths, the 'direct answer' test passes through a fallback, and pytest writes to the real log

findings.title: Hardcoded session secret lets anyone forge a logged-in session
findings.detail: SessionMiddleware uses secret_key="THIS_SECRET", and that value is in the repo. Starlette sessions are just itsdangerous-signed base64 JSON. I signed {"authenticated": true} with TimestampSigner("THIS_SECRET") and sent it as the `session` cookie with no login. GET / returned 200 with the chat UI, and GET /tts/files returned the user's file list. desktop/start_agent_ui.fish:17 and desktop/start_agent_ui.bat:9 start uvicorn with --host 0.0.0.0, so anyone on the local network can do this. They then have the whole agent, including approving write_file/edit_file, because approvals are just form fields.
findings.suggestion: Read the secret from an env var (e.g. SESSION_SECRET, loaded through the existing load_dotenv) and refuse to start if it is missing. Alternatively, generate secrets.token_urlsafe(32) on each start, which logs everyone out on restart. Also document it in README, and think about binding the launchers to 127.0.0.1.
findings.verification_note:
I reproduced it and could not refute it.

- **The secret is a constant.** core/ui.py:32-35 sets up SessionMiddleware with secret_key="THIS_SECRET". It has been there since commit a885819 and is pushed to origin github.com/hmstautland/agent0.
- **The cookie can be forged.** Starlette 1.6.0's SessionMiddleware only signs the cookie with itsdangerous.TimestampSigner(secret) over base64 JSON. Anyone who knows the key can make a valid cookie.
- **Auth checks nothing else.** The only check is core/auth.py:11-14, `request.session.get("authenticated") == True`. It is the dependency on agent_router, speech_router, audio_router, calendar_router and logout_router. There is no server-side session store and no check bound to the password.
- **I ran the exploit read-only with TestClient against the real app.** I signed {"authenticated": true} with TimestampSigner("THIS_SECRET").
  - Without the cookie: `/` returns 303 to /login.
  - With the forged cookie: `/` returns 200 with the full index page, `GET /tts/files` returns the real list of saved audio files, and `GET /calendar/month` returns the user's real calendar events.
- **It is reachable over the LAN.** desktop/start_agent_ui.fish:17 runs `uvicorn core.ui:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`, and desktop/start_agent_ui.bat:9 does the same. desktop/agent0-ui.desktop's Exec points at the fish launcher, so the user's normal way of starting the app is LAN-exposed. The README's `uvicorn core.ui:app --reload` binds to 127.0.0.1, which limits the attack to local processes or users.
- **Approvals are just form fields.** core/agent_routes.py:27-34 (create_permission_decisions) builds them from the `permission_decision` and `permission_action` fields. config/settings.py:11-12 marks write_file and edit_file as "ask". With a forged session, an attacker can POST /ask with permission_action=write_file and permission_decision=y and approve their own write.
- **Limits on the damage.** tools/files.py:14-25 (`_safe_path`) keeps writes inside the project folder. That folder holds the app's own .py files, so overwriting them gives code execution the next time the app starts. The read tools can also read .env, which holds APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD.

No existing guard stops this. High severity is justified, even for a single-user app, because the user's real launcher binds to 0.0.0.0.

A related issue I noticed but did not count here: the `/audio` StaticFiles mount at core/ui.py:30 has no auth at all, so saved audio can be downloaded without even a forged cookie if the filename is known. Filenames are timestamp-based, e.g. tts_2026-10-09_08-48.wav.
findings.status_note: SESSION_SECRET (at least 32 characters) is required from .env. The app refuses to start without it.

findings.title: chat.js ignores HTTP status, network errors and requests still in progress
findings.detail: handleAskStream never checks res.ok or content-type and has no try/catch. (1) Session expired or logged out in another tab: core/ui.py:48-51 turns the 401 into a 303 to /login (confirmed: anonymous POST /ask_stream returns 303 to /login). fetch follows it, gets the login HTML with a 200, and every line fails JSON.parse with only console.error. The UI was just cleared, so the user sees nothing. (2) A dropped or aborted stream (see the /ask_stream error-event finding) makes reader.read() reject. The rejection is unhandled and the thinking spinner stays visible. (3) No AbortController: sending a second question (or clicking an audio 'choose' button, which also calls handleAskStream) while the first is running leaves both readers writing to the same elements. The first answer, or its permission card, then shows up under the second question.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the body in try/catch/finally and show errors in #stream-error. Check res.ok and that content-type is application/x-ndjson, and send the user to /login on redirect or 401. Keep one AbortController and abort the earlier request on each new submit. On the server, consider returning a 401 JSON for fetch requests instead of redirecting.
findings.verification_note:
I traced static/chat.js:58-102 and the server side. Most of the finding holds, but one sub-scenario is wrong.

(1) Confirmed. agent_router depends on is_logged_in (core/auth.py:11-14, core/agent_routes.py:20). core/ui.py:48-50 turns the 401 into a 303 to /login. I ran TestClient against an anonymous POST /ask_stream: it returns 303 to /login. With redirects followed, it ends as 200 text/html (the login page), and 23 of its lines fail json.loads. chat.js:63-66 never checks res.ok or content-type. The catch at chat.js:89-91 only calls console.error, and clearStreamUI() (chat.js:59) has already hidden everything, so the user sees nothing. This happens after logging out in another tab, or when the session cookie expires (SessionMiddleware's default max_age is 14 days).

(2) Confirmed, and more likely than the finding suggests. agent.py:145 and :227 call query_llm, which can raise from raise_for_status, a connection error or a timeout. Nothing catches that in _run_steps, stream_agent or event_stream (core/agent_routes.py:191-195). I patched query_llm to raise ConnectionError and drove stream_agent directly. It yields {'event':'status','message':'Trying local model...'} and then raises. Under uvicorn the chunked response is cut off after headers and that status line, so reader.read() at chat.js:78 rejects. Nothing catches it: the submit handler (chat.js:130-134) just awaits it. The thinking spinner and heading set by showStatus stay up for good. Simple ways to hit this: Ollama not running, or the model not pulled (Ollama returns 404, raise_for_status raises).

(3) Partly correct. Nothing disables the form or the input, and there is no AbortController (grep finds none), so a second typed or Enter submit while the first stream runs leaves both readers writing to the same elements. Example: a long tool-loop question, then "show my calendar". The first stream's later status and final_response events overwrite the calendar view. The claim that an audio "choose" button can start an overlapping request is wrong. Those buttons are only rendered by the final_response that ends a stream (audio-player.js:39-53), and every handleAskStream call starts with clearStreamUI(), which empties streamAudio.innerHTML (chat.js:26). So the buttons cannot be clicked while another request is running. One more detail: event_stream runs the blocking, synchronous stream_agent inside an async generator, so the second request is only served at the first stream's yield points. The two streams still interleave.

No test covers any of this. The tests are Python only, and the ask_stream tests (tests/test_agent_flow.py:191, tests/test_calendar.py:126) cover logged-in happy paths. Medium severity is about right for a single-user local app.

Note: my TestClient runs appended two "user_input" lines to the gitignored runtime log local_storage/logs.txt (stream_agent calls log_event). Nothing else was written.
findings.corrected: static/chat.js:58-102 (handleAskStream) has no try/catch/finally and checks neither res.ok nor content-type. (1) After a logout in another tab or session-cookie expiry, POST /ask_stream gets a 303 to /login (core/ui.py:48-50). fetch follows it and receives the login HTML as a 200. Every line fails JSON.parse with only console.error, and the UI has just been cleared, so the user sees nothing. (2) An exception in the agent loop, such as query_llm failing because Ollama is down or the model is missing (agent.py:145/227), propagates through stream_agent and event_stream (core/agent_routes.py:191-195) after a status event has been sent. uvicorn aborts the chunked response, reader.read() rejects without a handler, and the thinking spinner stays up indefinitely. (3) There is no AbortController and nothing disables the form, so a second typed submit while a stream is running interleaves two readers on the same elements, and the earlier request's late events overwrite the newer answer or calendar. The audio "choose" buttons cannot trigger this: they only appear at the end of a stream and are wiped by clearStreamUI at the start of each request. Fix on the client: try/catch/finally that writes to #stream-error and hides the spinner; check res.ok, res.redirected and content-type, and redirect to /login when needed; one AbortController per submit. Optionally, have the server return JSON 401 for fetch requests and catch exceptions in event_stream, emitting an error event instead.
findings.status_note: chat.js shows network errors, non-OK HTTP statuses and streams that end without a final event.

findings.title: Voice notes are saved twice and the user is never told
findings.detail: /speech already saves a note when the transcript matches parse_note_command (core/speech_routes.py:21-24) and returns note_saved. speech.js ignores note_saved and puts the transcript (e.g. 'Note buy milk.') into the input box. If the user presses Enter, as the UI invites, /ask_stream's shortcut_text_response (core/agent_routes.py:44-47) matches the same text and saves a second note file. If they don't press Enter, they never learn it was saved.
findings.suggestion: When data.note_saved is set, show 'Note saved to …' in the stream card and clear the input, or leave it filled but don't save in /speech. Pick one place to do the save.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code path and it holds up. core/speech_routes.py:20-24 runs parse_note_command on the Whisper transcript. On a match it calls save_note_text(..., source="speech") and returns {"text", "note_saved"}. The only client of /speech is static/speech.js:40-42, which reads only data.text and writes it into #input. Nothing in the repo reads note_saved: a grep across static/, features/*/static and templates/ finds it only in speech_routes.py.

When the user then presses Enter (static/chat.js:136-141 calls requestSubmit, which posts to /ask_stream), ask_stream (core/agent_routes.py:160) calls shortcut_text_response with the same text. That function runs parse_note_command again (agent_routes.py:44-47) and calls save_note_text a second time, this time with source="text". The plain /ask route at agent_routes.py:90 does the same.

I checked with a read-only snippet that typical transcripts match the pattern: 'Note buy milk.' gives 'buy milk.', 'Note: dentist at 3.' gives 'dentist at 3.', and 'Take note, call mom tomorrow.' gives ', call mom tomorrow.'. So the triggering input happens in normal use.

No guard prevents the second save: there is no dedupe and the UI doesn't clear the input. save_note_text names files with second-level timestamps (tools/notes.py:34-35), so a second file is created unless Enter is pressed within the same second. In that case the first file is overwritten, and its Source header changes from speech to text.

No test covers this. There are no note-related tests for /speech in tests/test_speech_routes.py or any other test file. If the user doesn't press Enter, the UI gives no sign the note was saved, because note_saved is never shown.

Severity medium is reasonable. The location (static/speech.js:42) and the mechanism are accurate. One minor addition: the duplicate is recorded as Source: text, so the stored note's origin metadata is also inconsistent.

findings.title: Microphone stream is never released
findings.detail: getUserMedia's MediaStream is a local variable that is never stopped. After the user clicks stop, the browser's microphone indicator stays on and the mic stays open until the tab closes. Each new recording opens another stream. Other gaps: onstop is set after mediaRecorder.stop() (works only because the event fires asynchronously). A rejected getUserMedia call is unhandled. res.json() throws when /speech returns a 500 (transcription error on an empty or corrupt blob) or the login redirect HTML.
findings.suggestion: Keep the stream and call stream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop()) in onstop. Set onstop before calling stop(). Wrap the fetch in try/catch and check res.ok.
findings.verification_note:
I traced every part of the finding in static/speech.js and the server code, and each part holds up.

(1) The stream is never stopped. At line 9 `stream` is a block-local const inside the `if (!recording)` branch. Only the MediaRecorder at line 13 keeps a reference to it, and the stop path at lines 26-48 calls only `mediaRecorder.stop()`. Stopping the recorder does not stop the source tracks. I searched templates/, static/, features/ and core/ and found no `getTracks` or `track.stop` anywhere. So the mic stays live and the browser's recording indicator stays on until the page unloads. Each new recording calls `getUserMedia` again and gets another set of live tracks.

(2) `onstop` is assigned at line 29, after `stop()` at line 27. This works only because the `stop` event is dispatched asynchronously. That is fragile, but it is not a failure today, which matches how the reviewer described it.

(3) A rejected `getUserMedia` (permission denied, no device, insecure origin) at line 9 has no try/catch. The result is an unhandled promise rejection with no feedback to the user. `recording` stays false, so nothing gets stuck, but the click silently does nothing.

(4) `res.json()` at line 40 has no `res.ok` check and no try/catch. I confirmed a concrete non-JSON path. `/speech` sits on `speech_router`, which has `dependencies=[Depends(is_logged_in)]`. When the session is unauthenticated (for example after logging out in another tab, or after the session expires), `is_logged_in` raises a 401 (core/auth.py:13). The handler at core/ui.py:48-51 turns that into a 303 redirect to /login. `fetch` follows the redirect and gets the login page HTML with status 200, so `res.json()` throws a SyntaxError inside `onstop`. The text box is not updated and there is no error message. The 500 path is also real: core/speech_routes.py `speech()` calls `transcribe_audio` with no exception handling, so any decode failure inside faster-whisper becomes a plain-text 500, which `res.json()` cannot parse. That case is less likely in practice, because without a timeslice MediaRecorder delivers its data on stop, so the blob is normally not empty.

No test covers this. tests/ has only Python tests (test_speech_routes.py tests the server side), and there are no JS tests for speech.js. One more small issue in the same function, also unguarded: `recording` is set only after the awaited `getUserMedia` resolves. A second click while the permission prompt is open starts a second `getUserMedia` and a second MediaRecorder, and the first recorder and stream are leaked.

Low severity is appropriate. This is a resource/privacy-indicator leak plus UX error handling, it is client-only, and it changes no contract.

findings.title: CLI push-to-talk: busy-wait loop, held key wipes the buffer, hardcoded device
findings.detail: `while listener.running: if recording: ...` has no sleep, so it spins a CPU core at 100% until 'r' is pressed. During that time the InputStream is not read, so the first chunks after pressing are stale buffered audio. on_press runs `audio_buffer = []` on every press event. With OS key auto-repeat, holding 'r' keeps firing on_press, so audio captured so far is thrown away and the transcript holds only the tail. device=1 (line 44) is hardcoded and breaks on any other machine. `global recording, audio_buffer` at line 41 is unused (pyflakes). The transcript is printed twice in CLI mode (lines 66 and 75).
findings.suggestion: Ignore on_press while already recording. Use an sd.InputStream callback, or a threading.Event wait, instead of polling. Default to the system input device (device=None, or an env var). Drop the unused global and the duplicate print.
findings.verification_note:
I traced each claim in core/speech_to_text.py and could not refute any of them. One is understated, and two need a caveat.

How the path is reached: in agent.py, the `__main__` block on lines 386-393 calls `listen()` in speech mode ("s"). `listen()` calls `record_push_to_talk()` at line 71. No test covers this path; tests/ has no reference to `listen`, `record_push_to_talk` or `on_press`.

Confirmed:
1. **Busy-wait.** The loop on lines 45-48, `while listener.running: if recording: ...`, has no sleep or wait. Until 'r' is pressed it spins one core at 100%. It only blocks once recording starts, inside `stream.read`.
2. **Held key wipes the buffer.** `on_press` sets `audio_buffer = []` on every 'r' press, with no "already recording" guard (lines 21-23). I ran a read-only simulation using the real `on_press`/`on_release` source loaded via `ast`. After 10 chunks were captured, one repeated press left 0 chunks while `recording` stayed True. The comment says "hold 'r' to record", so holding is the intended use. pynput's uinput backend treats `key_hold` as a press (_uinput.py:409), and Windows and macOS also send repeated key-down events. Auto-repeat at 25-30 Hz is faster than one 1024-sample read (64 ms at 16 kHz). So the final buffer holds about one chunk, not "the tail": the transcript is close to empty.
   - Caveat: pynput's xorg backend does not de-duplicate (_xorg.py:584-588). If the X server sends autorepeat as release+press pairs, the first fake release calls `on_release`, which returns False and stops the listener. Recording would then be cut off after the repeat delay instead.
3. **Hardcoded device.** `device=1` is hardcoded at line 44, and this is worse than reported. On this machine, `sd.query_devices()` shows device 1 is "HD-Audio Generic: HDMI 1 (0 in, 8 out)". `sd.check_input_settings(device=1, channels=1, samplerate=16000)` raises `PortAudioError: Invalid number of channels [-9998]`. With `device=None` (system default 12) the same check passes. So CLI speech mode raises an exception at line 44 as soon as it starts, on the author's own machine. Nothing catches it, so the CLI loop in agent.py crashes. This failure currently hides issues 1 and 2.
4. **Unused global.** `global recording, audio_buffer` on line 41 is unnecessary because the function never assigns either name. pyflakes reports the same.
5. **Duplicate print.** The transcript prints twice: once in `transcribe_audio` (line 66) and again in `listen` (line 75). Line 66 also prints on every web `/speech` request, via core/speech_routes.py:20.

Plausible but not verified: the "stale buffered audio" claim. The stream is not read while idle, so the first read after pressing 'r' may return leftover or overflowed data from the host buffer. The effect is at most a short fragment and depends on the host API, so it is minor.

Severity should be higher than "low" for the CLI speech feature, because it does not work at all on this machine (point 3).
findings.corrected:
CLI push-to-talk in core/speech_to_text.py is broken, and is untested.

(1) Line 44 hardcodes `device=1`. On this machine device 1 is an HDMI output with 0 input channels, so `sd.InputStream(channels=1, device=1)` raises `PortAudioError: Invalid number of channels`. As a result, `python -m agent` in speech mode crashes on the first `listen()` call. Fix: use `device=None` (the system default) or read the device from an env var.

(2) Once a valid device is used, holding 'r' still breaks recording. `on_press` (lines 21-23) resets `audio_buffer = []` on every press event. Key auto-repeat sends repeated presses on uinput, Windows and macOS, so the buffer is cleared about every 30-40 ms and ends up holding about one 64 ms chunk. The transcript is effectively empty. On X11, autorepeat may instead arrive as release+press pairs, and the fake release stops the listener early. Fix: ignore `on_press` while already recording, and ignore auto-repeat releases.

(3) The loop on lines 45-48 busy-waits at 100% CPU until 'r' is pressed. Fix: use a `threading.Event` or an `InputStream` callback. Minor: the first read after pressing may return stale or overflowed buffered audio.

(4) Cleanup: the `global` on line 41 is unused, and the transcript is printed twice (line 66 in `transcribe_audio`, which also runs for web `/speech`, and line 75 in `listen`).

Severity: medium for the CLI speech feature, since it cannot run as-is; low for the app overall, since the web STT path (`/speech`) is unaffected.

findings.title: Exception handler turns any non-401 FastAPI HTTPException into a 500
findings.detail: The handler is registered for fastapi.HTTPException and does `raise exc` when the status is not 401. Raising inside an exception handler surfaces as a server error. Probe: a route raising HTTPException(404) returned '500 Internal Server Error'. No route raises one today. Starlette's own 404s and 405s are a different class and still work. The first `raise HTTPException(400/404)` anyone adds to a route will return a 500.
findings.suggestion: For non-401, `return await fastapi.exception_handlers.http_exception_handler(request, exc)`.
findings.verification_note: core/ui.py:48-52 registers a handler for fastapi.HTTPException that returns a redirect only for 401 and otherwise runs `raise exc`. When an exception handler raises, the exception goes up to ServerErrorMiddleware, which returns a 500. I tested this in memory with TestClient(raise_server_exceptions=False) and wrote no files. I added a probe route raising fastapi.HTTPException(404, 'nope') and moved it ahead of the catch-all. It returned "500 Internal Server Error" instead of a 404. The other paths behave as the finding says. An unauthenticated GET /logout returns 303 to /login. PUT /login returns 405, and a missing /static file returns 404. Both of those raise starlette.exceptions.HTTPException, the parent class, so this handler never catches them. Under FastAPI 0.141.1, fastapi/routing.py imports HTTPException from starlette. That means body-parse failures also bypass the handler: a malformed multipart POST to /login correctly returned 400. The only place the project raises fastapi.HTTPException is core/auth.py:13, which uses status 401. No test covers a non-401 case. So the bug is real but latent: nothing triggers it today, and the first non-401 fastapi.HTTPException added to a route will return a 500 and log a traceback. Severity low fits. One detail for the suggested fix: fastapi.exception_handlers.http_exception_handler has the same name as the local handler, so it needs an import alias.

findings.title: Starfield animation stops for good after the window is made narrower
findings.detail: z values are drawn from [0, canvas.width]. When the window narrows, the resize handler (lines 63-66) shrinks canvas.width but keeps each star's old z. Any star with z > new width gets a negative radius = (1 - z/width)*3*..., and ctx.arc throws IndexSizeError on a negative radius. animate() then throws before requestAnimationFrame, so the animation stops on login, logout and index.
findings.suggestion: Use Math.max(0, radius), or clamp/rescale star.z when the window is resized.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code in static/starfield.js and the finding holds. makeStar() sets z = Math.random() * canvas.width (line 18), and a star that respawns gets z = canvas.width (line 38). The resize handler (lines 63-66) changes only canvas.width and canvas.height and leaves each star's z alone. After the window gets narrower, any star with z > new width gets a negative radius at line 44: (1 - z/width) * 3 * sizeMultiplier. The HTML canvas spec says arc() must throw an IndexSizeError DOMException when the radius is negative, and Chrome, Firefox and Safari all do. Nothing guards against this: there is no try/catch, no Math.max and no z clamp. Because the throw happens inside the for-loop, requestAnimationFrame(animate) on line 58 never runs again, so the animation stays frozen even if the window is widened later.

The trigger is realistic. Stars respawn at exactly the old width, so there are always a few near the top of the range. I ran a Python simulation of the same update rule (600 stars, width 1920, 1000 frames, then narrowed to 1900). It left 4 stars with a negative radius, so narrowing by just 20px is enough. Common triggers are docking DevTools to the side, snapping or tiling a window, or rotating a phone from landscape to portrait.

The script is loaded on templates/index.html:78, templates/login.html:30 and templates/logout.html:26, so all three pages are affected. No tests cover the JS. Severity is low because it is cosmetic: the background freezes, but the app keeps working. Suggested fix: clamp the radius with Math.max(0, radius), or rescale or clamp star.z in the resize handler.

findings.title: Streamed final answer that is missing or not a string shows nothing or '[object Object]'
findings.detail: agent.py:254 yields decision.get('response'), which is None when the model replies with {"action": "none"} plus 'answer' or 'message' instead of 'response'. chat.js then hides both the card and the spinner, leaving a blank screen. If the model returns an object or list, textContent shows '[object Object]'. The non-streaming /ask turns these into JSON (core/agent_routes.py:139-140), so only the streamed path is affected.
findings.suggestion: In chat.js, show typeof response === 'string' ? response : JSON.stringify(response, null, 2), with a fallback like 'The model returned no answer.' Or fall back to raw in agent.py:254.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the path and reproduced it; I could not refute it. agent.py:254 yields `decision.get("response")` without a default or type check. core/llm.py:27-44 sends no `format: "json"` to Ollama, so the model's JSON is free-form. parse_decision (agent.py:58-91) only checks that the parsed value is a dict, and nothing normalizes the "response" key. core/streaming.py serializes None as `null` and keeps dicts as JSON objects.

In static/chat.js:107-116, the "LLM chose action: none" status first makes the card visible. Then `if (event.response)` is false for null or "", so the card is hidden again (streamCard.classList.add("hidden")) and the spinner is hidden too. The result is a blank screen. For a dict, `streamOutput.textContent = event.response` shows "[object Object]".

Read-only repro: I patched agent.query_llm/log_event in memory and ran stream_agent('what is the capital of France'):
- ['needs_tools', '{"action":"none","answer":"Paris"}'] gives final_response response null.
- ['needs_tools', '{"action":"none"}'] gives null.
- ['needs_tools', '{"action":"none","response":{"temp":20}}'] gives {"temp":20}.

No guard prevents this, and no test covers it (tests/test_agent_flow.py only uses a well-formed "response" string).

Small additions to the finding. The local-first path (agent.py:158, `decision.get("response", raw)`) can also stream a non-string: a local reply of {"action":"none","response":{...}} reproduced as an object in the stream. A list would show comma-joined values (Array.toString), not "[object Object]". On /ask, a None response becomes the literal text "null" (core/agent_routes.py:139-140), not a useful message. Severity low is right: it needs the model to break the JSON contract, which is plausible with a small local model.
findings.status_note: The server always sends a string answer; an empty model reply becomes an explicit message.

findings.title: Redirect branch in home() can never run
findings.detail: is_logged_in either raises HTTPException(401) or returns the (truthy) Request, so `if not await is_logged_in(request)` is never true and the RedirectResponse on line 23 never runs. The redirect actually comes from the exception handler in core/ui.py.
findings.suggestion: Use `async def home(request: Request, _=Depends(is_logged_in))`, or just call `await is_logged_in(request)` without the if.
findings.verification_note: I confirmed this by reading the code and by running a request. core/auth.py:11-14 shows that is_logged_in can only raise HTTPException(401) or return the Request. A Starlette Request is a collections.abc.Mapping whose __len__ is len(self.scope), and a real ASGI scope is never empty. So the returned value is always truthy, `if not await is_logged_in(request)` (line 22) is never true, and the RedirectResponse on line 23 is never reached. No code makes the branch reachable. No test monkeypatches is_logged_in: tests/test_agent_flow.py, test_calendar.py and test_speech_routes.py only patch auth_mod.PASSWORD. Every other caller uses it as a dependency (core/speech_routes.py:10, core/agent_routes.py:20, features/audio/routes.py:33, features/calendar/routes.py:14, core/auth.py:55), and none of them reads a boolean result. The redirect actually comes from the HTTPException handler at core/ui.py:48-51, which turns a 401 into a 303 redirect to /login. I checked this with TestClient: an unauthenticated GET / returns 303 with Location /login, and that response comes from the handler, not from line 23. This is not an unfinished feature. The branch was written as if is_logged_in returned a bool, so it is a leftover dead branch. Severity low (no behavior impact). The suggested fix (depend on is_logged_in, or call it without the `if`) is correct and does not change any contract.

findings.title: '+' button in the chat form does nothing
findings.detail: <button type="button" class="icon-btn add-btn">+</button> has no click handler in any loaded script, and styles.css has no add-btn rule. It is a visible control that does nothing.
findings.suggestion: Decide: build it (e.g. attach a document and send it to the existing /tts/extract-text, or a file picker for the agent), or remove the button.
findings.verification_note: templates/index.html:28 has `<button type="button" class="icon-btn add-btn">+</button>` with no onclick. Searching every loaded script (static/chat.js, speech.js, starfield.js, features/calendar/static/calendar.js, features/audio/static/audio-player.js, tts.js) for "add-btn" or addBtn turns up no hits. Nothing selects it either: querySelector targets only .mic-btn, .tts-btn and .audio-choice-btn. There is also no delegated document-level click handler; the only window/document listeners are starfield's resize and a dialog backdrop check in tts.js. Because the button is type="button", it doesn't submit the form, and chat.js only listens for the form's submit event and Enter on the input, so clicking it does nothing. "add-btn" appears nowhere in CSS. It only gets the generic .icon-btn styling from static/styles.css:93, so the claim that there is "no add-btn rule" is accurate. The git log shows it was added in 482f886 ("task: update UI") as a UI placeholder that was never wired up. So it is UNFINISHED (a stub with clear intent), not dead code, and the severity is low.
findings.status_note: The '+' button starts a new conversation (templates/index.html, static/chat.js, POST /conversation/new).

findings.title: check_imports.py is a dependency-check script that nothing uses
findings.detail: The script walks every .py file, collects top-level import names, tries __import__ on each non-stdlib name, and exits 1 if any fail. That includes local packages, so `import agent` loads Whisper and pynput. Nothing references it: not README, CI, tests or CLAUDE.md. CI's pip install plus pytest, and tools/verify.py's re-import of core.ui, already catch missing dependencies.
findings.suggestion: Decide: document it in README as a setup/diagnostic step (and maybe run it in CI before pytest), or delete it as redundant.
findings.verification_note:
I checked the finding and it holds up. Nothing in the repo refers to check_imports.py. A grep that skipped venv/ and .git/ found no hits in README.md, CLAUDE.md, context.md, .github/workflows/tests.yml, .claude/, desktop/*.fish, tests/, tools/, core/, config/ or features/. `git log -S check_imports --all` finds nothing either. The script arrived alone in commit e3a9e62 ("chore: ready linux and check imports script"), and the README lines added in that same commit only cover venv activation, not this script.

What the script does matches the reviewer's description. It walks every .py file under the current directory, collects absolute top-level import names, and runs __import__ on each one that is not stdlib (lines 27-36). It exits 1 if any import fails (line 43). I re-ran the same AST collection without executing any imports. The names it would import include the local packages `agent`, `config`, `core`, `features` and `tools`, plus `pytest`. `import agent` pulls in `core.speech_to_text` (agent.py:6), which builds `WhisperModel("base", ...)` as soon as it is imported (core/speech_to_text.py:9) and imports pynput (line 3). So the reviewer is right that running it loads Whisper and pynput.

CI already covers what this script checks. tests.yml installs requirements.txt and runs pytest under xvfb, so a missing dependency would fail the build there.

One small point on how to describe it: the script is not half-built. It is a complete, working diagnostic that nothing runs and nothing documents. It also only works when started from the repo root, because it uses Path("."). That fits the reviewer's "decide: document it or delete it" suggestion, and low severity is right.

findings.title: Login fails silently when APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD is unset
findings.detail: PASSWORD = getenv('APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD') is None when the variable is unset. Every login then shows 'Invalid password', and nothing says why. README never mentions APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD or .env, so a fresh clone cannot log in. The check uses a plain == comparison, and there is no rate limit, even though the launchers expose the server to the network.
findings.suggestion: Log or raise at startup when it is unset. Compare with hmac.compare_digest. Document APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD (and the new session secret) in README's setup section.
findings.verification_note:
The main claim checks out. core/auth.py:8 sets `PASSWORD = getenv("APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD")`. core/ui.py:1-3 calls load_dotenv() before it imports core.auth, so the value can only come from the environment or a gitignored .env. No .env.example is checked in. If the variable is unset, PASSWORD is None, the check `password == PASSWORD` at core/auth.py:37 is always False, and the page shows "Invalid password" with no log line. A grep of README.md finds nothing about APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD, .env or login setup; its only "env" section covers Ollama variables. The comparison is a plain `==`, and the repo has no login rate limiter (the only `rate_limit` is in tools/web.py, for web tools). desktop/start_agent_ui.fish:17 and desktop/start_agent_ui.bat:9 start uvicorn with `--host 0.0.0.0`.

Some details are wrong, though, and part of the suggestion would break things:
1. Location: the unset variable is read at line 8. Line 37 is only the comparison.
2. "Raise at startup" would break CI and tools. The CI workflow (.github/workflows) runs pytest with no .env. The tests import core.ui and core.auth at module level (tests/test_agent_flow.py:7-9, tests/test_speech_routes.py:1-4, tests/test_calendar.py:3-4), then set the password with `monkeypatch.setattr(auth_mod, "PASSWORD", "testpass")`. verify_app also re-imports core.ui (tools/verify.py:80-82). Raising at import would fail test collection and verify_app. Logging a warning is safe. Any check must also keep reading the module-level PASSWORD when a request arrives, or the monkeypatching stops working.
3. `hmac.compare_digest` cannot take the raw values. It raises TypeError when either argument is None, or a str with non-ASCII characters (e.g. a password with æøå), and that would show up as a 500. Check for None first, then compare the UTF-8 encoded bytes.
4. A bigger related problem: core/ui.py:33-34 hardcodes `SessionMiddleware(secret_key="THIS_SECRET")` in a public repo.
