Anyone can forge a signed session cookie with `authenticated=True` and skip the password entirely, which matters more than timing attacks or rate limiting once the server listens on 0.0.0.0.
findings.corrected:
core/auth.py:8 reads APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD with getenv. When it is unset, PASSWORD is None, the `password == PASSWORD` check at core/auth.py:37 always fails, and every login shows "Invalid password" with nothing logged. README.md never mentions APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD or .env, and no .env.example is checked in (.env is gitignored), so a fresh clone cannot log in until someone reads the source. The comparison is a plain `==` with no rate limit, and desktop/start_agent_ui.fish:17 and desktop/start_agent_ui.bat:9 bind to 0.0.0.0. Severity low.

Recommended fixes:
- Log a warning when the variable is unset. Do not raise at import: CI runs pytest with no .env, the tests import core.ui and core.auth and then monkeypatch `core.auth.PASSWORD`, and verify_app re-imports core.ui.
- Keep reading the module-level PASSWORD when each request arrives.
- Compare with `PASSWORD is not None and hmac.compare_digest(password.encode(), PASSWORD.encode())`. Passing raw str or None raises TypeError for non-ASCII input or an unset password.
- Document APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD, and a session-secret variable, in README's setup section.
- Related and more serious: core/ui.py:34 hardcodes `secret_key="THIS_SECRET"`, so anyone who reads the public repo can forge an authenticated session cookie without the password.
findings.status_note:
README now documents APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD and SESSION_SECRET. A missing password still fails silently at login.

Originally reported as: Login fails silently when APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD is unset, and README doesn't mention it

findings.title: Shortcut commands are split between agent_routes.py and agent.py, so the CLI misses some
findings.detail: The web routes handle notes, calendar-create, play and show-calendar themselves (lines 37-67, 91-114, 164-189). agent.py::_run_steps separately handles calendar-create and play (agent.py:174-188). So the CLI (`python -m agent`) has no notes or show-calendar shortcut and sends 'note buy milk' to the LLM, and calendar-create/play are implemented twice. load_dotenv() is called only in core/ui.py, so `python -m agent` never reads .env. Any OLLAMA_* settings kept there would be ignored by the CLI. Notes and 'show my calendar' are web-only; docs/guide/diagrams.md and docs/features/agent-loop.md list them as shortcuts without saying so.
findings.suggestion: Move all shortcuts into _run_steps, which already yields show_calendar and audio fields. Then /ask and /ask_stream just run the agent, and the CLI gets the same behaviour. Call load_dotenv() in agent.py's __main__ as well, or in a shared config module.
findings.verification_note:
I checked the premise against the code and all of it holds:
- core/agent_routes.py:37-67 (shortcut_text_response and audio_play_result) handles notes and calendar-create. Notes are not handled anywhere else, and tools/registry.py has no notes tool.
- /ask (lines 91-114) and /ask_stream (lines 164-189) run these shortcuts, plus play and is_calendar_request, before they call the agent.
- agent.py::_run_steps (lines 174-188) handles only calendar-create (parse_create_command) and play (parse_play_command). It never calls parse_note_command or is_calendar_request.
- So the CLI sends "note buy milk" to try_local_answer, and nothing ever saves it.
- In the web flow, the routes catch calendar-create and play first, so agent.py's copies of those two branches only ever run from the CLI. They are duplicates.
- load_dotenv() appears only in core/ui.py:1-3. I imported `agent` in the venv: neither core.ui nor dotenv ends up in sys.modules. The OLLAMA_* values in core/llm.py:5-24 are read with os.getenv when the module is imported, so the CLI ignores any OLLAMA_* values kept in .env. I could not read .env to see whether any are actually there.

The suggestion, done as written, would break one thing. run_agent (agent.py:357-371) keeps only response/message and show_calendar, and drops the `audio` field. If /ask "just ran the agent", it would lose `audio_data`. features/audio/templates/audio/stream_audio.html and audio_play.html need that value to show the player or the list of choices on the plain /ask page.

There is also a smaller issue. If the show-calendar shortcut moved into _run_steps, the CLI would print the raw dict `{'show_calendar': {...}}` from run_agent. The CLI cannot draw the month grid, so "CLI gets the same behaviour" does not really apply to show-calendar.
findings.corrected: Shortcut commands are split between core/agent_routes.py (shortcut_text_response/audio_play_result at lines 37-67, used by /ask at lines 91-114 and /ask_stream at lines 164-189: notes, calendar-create, play, show-calendar) and agent.py::_run_steps (lines 174-188: calendar-create and play only). As a result, the CLI (`python -m agent`) has no notes shortcut and there is no notes tool in the registry, so "note buy milk" goes to the local model and is never saved. Calendar-create and play are written twice, and agent.py's copies only run from the CLI. load_dotenv() is called only in core/ui.py:3, and importing `agent` never imports core.ui or dotenv, so the CLI ignores any OLLAMA_* values in .env. core/llm.py reads them at import time. Suggested fix: move the notes and show-calendar shortcuts into _run_steps and remove the copies in agent_routes.py. run_agent (agent.py:357-371) must then also return the `audio` field, which it currently drops, or /ask loses `audio_data` and the plain-page audio player stops working. The CLI also needs a text fallback for show_calendar instead of printing the raw dict. Call load_dotenv() in a module both entry points import (for example at the top of core/llm.py or a shared config module) instead of only in core/ui.py.

findings.title: edit_file lenient fallback merges lines and strips indentation
findings.detail:
When the exact match fails (e.g. the model retyped ' vs "), _lenient_pattern turns every whitespace run in old_text into `\s+`, which also matches newlines. A leading indent therefore matches from the previous line's newline, and a trailing newline eats the next line's indentation. Verified on a scratch copy: file `def f():
    x = 1
    call("a")
    return x
`, edit_file(old_text="    call('a')
", new_text="    call('b')
") reports success and produces `    x = 1    call('b')
return x` (lines merged, `return` dedented, which is a SyntaxError). With a 2-space-indented old_text the same merge happens. This path fires whenever quotes differ, which is the exact case it was written for.
findings.suggestion: Map whitespace runs without a newline to `[ \t]+` and runs with newlines to `[ \t]*(?:\r?\n[ \t]*)+`. If old_text starts with whitespace, anchor with `(?m)^` and match the indent as `[ \t]*`. Match on old_text.strip() and keep the file's original surrounding whitespace. Add a regression test with the example above.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and reproduced the bug. In tools/files.py, edit_file (lines 396-419) falls back to `re.finditer(_lenient_pattern(old_text), old_content)` whenever the exact text is not found. It then splices new_text over match.start():match.end(). _lenient_pattern (line 316-320) turns every whitespace chunk, including a leading indent and a trailing "\n", into `\s+`. That pattern also matches newlines and the next line's indent.

I reproduced it in memory with the real _lenient_pattern and the same splice. No files were written.
- File `def f():\n    x = 1\n    call("a")\n    return x\n` with old_text `"    call('a')\n"` (exact count 0).
- The pattern is `\s+call\(['"]a['"]\)\s+` and it matches `'\n    call("a")\n    '`.
- The result is `"def f():\n    x = 1    call('b')\nreturn x\n"`, and compile() raises SyntaxError.
- The 2-space variant gives `x = 1  call('b')` (lines merged).

Either end is enough on its own:
- Leading whitespace only (`"    call('a')"`) merges the line into the one before it.
- A trailing newline only (`"call('a')\n"`) dedents the next line to `return x`.

Old_text with no leading or trailing whitespace splices correctly, and so do multi-line snippets that start and end with non-whitespace.

Nothing prevents the bad write:
- _script_edit_guard only checks `<script>` balance.
- The "ask" permission in config/settings.py:12 is granted before the tool runs, from the arguments alone. The diff preview is only printed to the server console.
- The tool returns "File edited: ... " as success.
- tests/ has no test for edit_file or _lenient_pattern. A grep for edit_file or lenient in tests/ finds nothing.

The triggering state is realistic. The lenient path exists for when the model retypes quotes or indentation, and old_text copied from a file often starts with indentation or ends with a newline. Two things soften the impact: _backup_and_write keeps a .bak of the previous version, and verify_app may catch a resulting SyntaxError if the model happens to run it. Even so, it silently corrupts source files, so the high severity is reasonable.
findings.status_note: The lenient fallback keeps line boundaries and indentation and refuses ambiguous matches (tools/files.py `_lenient_pattern`), with tests in tests/test_files.py.

findings.title: verify_app reports 'app imports cleanly' even when imported modules are broken
findings.detail: importlib.reload(core.ui) re-executes only core/ui.py. Its dependencies (core.agent_routes, features.calendar.calendar, tools.files, ...) are already in sys.modules in both the server and the CLI (agent.py imports them), so they are not re-imported. Verified on a scratch copy: after `import agent, core.ui`, I appended a syntax error to features/calendar/calendar.py and to core/agent_routes.py, and verify_app() still returned 'OK - 12 template(s) compile, 19 referenced asset(s) exist, app imports cleanly.' CLAUDE.md and the system prompt both rely on this check after edits.
findings.suggestion: Run the import check in a fresh interpreter, e.g. `subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'import core.ui'], cwd=BASE_DIR, capture_output=True, timeout=60)`, or py_compile every project .py file, and report stderr on failure.
findings.verification_note:
I couldn't refute this. tools/verify.py:77-84 does `import core.ui; importlib.reload(core.ui)`. That re-runs only core/ui.py. The modules it imports are already in sys.modules, so they come straight from the cache and are never re-read. Nothing else guards against this, and no test covers verify_app (grep for "verify" in tests/ finds nothing).

I reproduced it without writing any files, running Python with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. After `import agent, core.ui`, I patched SourceFileLoader.get_data so it returns source with a syntax error appended for features/calendar/calendar.py, core/agent_routes.py and tools/files.py. I also wrapped exec_module to record which modules actually run.
- verify_app() still returned "OK - 12 template(s) compile, 19 referenced asset(s) exist, app imports cleanly."
- The only modules re-run were ['encodings.unicode_escape', 'core.ui'].
- As a control, a fresh import of features.calendar.calendar with the same patch raised SyntaxError, so the simulated breakage is real.

This matters because config/system_prompt.py:41 and tools/files.py:230 tell the LLM to trust verify_app after edits, and CLAUDE.md tells humans the same thing.

One small correction to the report. In CLI mode, `import agent` does not load core.ui, core.agent_routes, core.auth, core.speech_routes or features/*/routes. So the first verify_app call in a CLI session imports those fresh and does catch errors in them. What it never re-checks are the modules agent.py already loaded: tools.files, tools.registry, features.calendar.calendar, features.audio.player, features.audio.text_to_speech, core.llm and core.permission. From the second call on, nothing below core/ui.py is re-checked. In the uvicorn server everything is already loaded, so the report holds exactly as written. The location, mechanism and medium severity are correct, and the suggested fix (run `import core.ui` in a fresh subprocess, or py_compile the project's .py files) would work.

findings.title: Script-tag balance guard refuses every edit to Python files that mention <script>
findings.detail: _script_edit_guard runs on every edit_file call, whatever the file type, and counts `<script\b` and `</script>` in the resulting file. Python source that mentions the tag in strings is permanently 'unbalanced'. Verified counts: config/system_prompt.py 1/0, tools/files.py 9/3, tools/registry.py 2/0. Unrelated edits are refused, e.g. edit_file('tools/registry.py', 'Get latest news headlines', 'Get latest news headlines for a country') returns 'Refused: that edit leaves unbalanced <script> tags...'. The model is pushed toward whole-file write_file rewrites of exactly those files, which is the riskier path.
findings.suggestion: Apply the guard only to HTML-like files (.html/.htm/.jinja/.j2). Alternatively compare the open/close counts before and after the edit instead of requiring them to be equal in the result.
findings.verification_note: I traced the code and reproduced the bug without writing anything. `edit_file` in tools/files.py (lines 370-430) calls `_script_edit_guard(old_content, content, new_text)` at line 421 on every edit, whatever the file type. Before that, the function only checks the path (`_safe_path` just keeps it inside the project), the arguments, whether the file exists, and that `old_text` matches once. `_script_edit_guard` (lines 234-263) counts `<script\b` and `</script\s*>` in the resulting file. At line 244 it refuses whenever the two counts differ. It does not check the extension, and it does not compare against the counts before the edit. I counted the tags across the whole repo, skipping venv, models, local_storage and .git. Exactly three files are unbalanced: config/system_prompt.py (1/0), tools/files.py (9/3) and tools/registry.py (2/0). These are the counts the reviewer gave. I ran a read-only python snippet with `_backup_and_write` stubbed to raise. `edit_file('tools/registry.py', 'Get latest news headlines', 'Get latest news headlines for a country')` returned 'Refused: that edit leaves unbalanced <script> tags, so the JavaScript would be orphaned in the HTML. Use extract_inline_scripts...'. So the match succeeded and the guard blocked an edit that has nothing to do with scripts. Any edit to these three files gets the same refusal unless it happens to make the counts equal. `write_file` (lines 339-367) has no such guard, so the model is pushed toward rewriting the whole file. Nothing elsewhere prevents this: `edit_file` is registered at tools/registry.py:22-23 and set to "ask" in config/settings.py:12. The user may therefore approve the edit and still get a refusal. No test in tests/ covers `_script_edit_guard` or the unbalanced case. The suggested fix holds up: limit the guard to HTML/Jinja files, or refuse only when the edit changes the balance (compare counts before and after). Medium severity is reasonable. The bug blocks the agent from making targeted edits to its own system prompt, tool registry and file tools, and the fallback is the riskier whole-file rewrite.

findings.title: extract_inline_scripts merges every block at the first block's position and also moves non-JavaScript script types
findings.detail: The link is built as `/` + the project-relative path, which is only correct under static/. Verified: dest='features/calendar/static/x.js' produces `<script src="/features/calendar/static/x.js">`. That URL is not mounted (the correct one is /static/calendar/x.js), so the request hits the catch-all redirect and the code silently stops running. verify_app doesn't catch it because URLs with an unknown prefix are skipped (tools/verify.py:69-75 has no else branch). Also, every inline block is concatenated and placed where the first block was. Verified: a body-end block that used `document.getElementById('d')` and a function from a later `<script src=/static/lib.js>` was moved into <head>, ahead of both the element and lib.js, so it would get null or a ReferenceError at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Derive the URL by inverting tools/verify.py MOUNTS (and reject a dest that isn't under a mounted directory). Only merge blocks that sit next to each other, or extract one file per block and replace each block in place. In verify_app, flag `src=` URLs whose prefix matches no mount.
findings.verification_note:
I read the code and reproduced both halves of the finding by running the real function in memory. File I/O was monkeypatched, so nothing was written.

1) Wrong URL. tools/files.py:205-206 builds the link as `/` + the project-relative path. I called extract_inline_scripts(path='templates/fake.html', dest='features/calendar/static/x.js'). It returned and wrote `<script src="/features/calendar/static/x.js">`. core/ui.py has no `/features` mount; the feature static dirs are served at /static/calendar and /static/audio. The request therefore reaches core/auth.py:48-52 (catch_all), which answers with a 303 to `/` or `/login`. The browser gets HTML back instead of the JS, so the code never runs. tools/verify.py:68-75 only checks URLs that match a MOUNTS prefix and has no else branch, so verify_app skips this URL and still reports OK.

2) Block reordering. At tools/files.py:203 and 209-217, all inline blocks are joined into one file, the first match becomes the link tag and the rest are deleted. My test page had a `<head>` block and a body-end block that called `libFn(document.getElementById('d'))` after `<script src="/static/lib.js">`. The output HTML had the single link tag in `<head>`, ahead of both `#d` and lib.js. At runtime that body-end code would get null or a ReferenceError.

Nothing guards against this:
- There are no tests (no test file mentions extract_inline_scripts or INLINE_SCRIPT_RE).
- The Jinja check at 181-187 rejects only template syntax.
- The function never checks that dest is under a served directory.

Two things limit the impact, but neither refutes the finding:
- The forced shortcut (agent.py planned_first_decision → parse_script_refactor_command) never passes a dest. The default `static/<stem>.js` maps to a correct `/static/...` URL, so the URL half only happens when the LLM picks a dest outside `static/`. That is plausible: the registry description says dest is optional, and the project's feature-folder layout puts JS in `features/<name>/static`.
- No template in TEMPLATE_DIRS has an inline script today, so both problems are latent until someone adds one.

Medium severity is reasonable for a high-risk write tool that breaks pages silently while verify_app passes.
findings.status_note: Jinja blocks and an existing destination are now refused, and the link URL comes from the destination path. Still open: all blocks merge into the first position, and application/ld+json, importmap and text/template blocks are moved into a .js file because there is no type= check. Originally reported as: extract_inline_scripts links an unserved URL and moves all blocks into the first block's position

findings.title: Web searches reach several search providers, not just DuckDuckGo
findings.detail: RULES sets search_web and get_news to 'auto', so model-composed queries, which can include user input or project content, leave the machine without a prompt. config/system_prompt.py:18 tells the model 'External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission'. tools/registry.py:42/48/54 tags these tools `"external": 1`, but nothing reads that key. It looks meant for exactly this gate, so it is unfinished rather than dead. Also, ddgs 9.16 uses backend='auto', which fans out to bing, brave, google, yandex, yahoo, mojeek and others, so the result label `"source": "duckduckgo-search"` (tools/web.py:55) is inaccurate and the privacy footprint is wider than it appears. Smaller points: the 'auto' rules for verify_app and get_news duplicate their low risk level, and the `risk == "auto"` branch in core/permission.py:21 matches no tool. No rule names a nonexistent tool. The tools without rules (read_web_content, read_calendar, play_audio_file) fall back to their risk level as intended.
findings.suggestion: Decide on a policy. Either implement the `external` flag in request_permission (e.g. external tools always ask unless the user opts in through a setting) and remove search_web/get_news from 'auto', or delete the flag and fix the system prompt to match. Pin `backend='duckduckgo'` if only DuckDuckGo is intended.
findings.verification_note: The core premise checks out against the code. config/settings.py:7-8 sets search_web and get_news to "auto". core/permission.py:17-18 returns True for "auto" before any decision or prompt, so neither tool ever asks. config/system_prompt.py:18 says "External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission". The "external": 1 key at tools/registry.py:42/48/54 (get_news, search_web, read_web_content) is never read: grep finds no reader, build_tool_prompt (agent.py:131-137) only uses description, and request_permission only gets tool["risk"] (agent.py:289). The smaller points are also correct. verify_app and get_news are both risk "low", so their "auto" rules change nothing. No tool has risk "auto", so the `risk == "auto"` branch at permission.py:21 is dead. Every RULES key exists in TOOLS. Of the tools without rules, read_web_content (medium) asks, while read_calendar and play_audio_file (low) auto-allow. The suggestion would not break the suite: tests/test_agent_flow.py:38 already passes permission_decisions={"search_web": True}. The problem is the ddgs mechanism detail. I checked the installed ddgs 9.16.0 source (venv/.../ddgs/ddgs.py:72-133, 135-223, engines/__init__.py). The bing and yandex engines are `disabled = True`, so they are never used. Enabled text engines are wikipedia (priority 2), grokipedia (1.9), then brave, duckduckgo, google, mojeek, startpage and yahoo in random order. Note that duckduckgo and yahoo both report provider "bing", and startpage reports "google". With MAX_RESULTS=5, max_workers is min(providers, ceil(5/10)+1) = 2. So it does not fan out to all engines at once. It always queries wikipedia and grokipedia first, then adds random general engines one at a time until it has 5 results, usually only one more. The README also says "Web search (DuckDuckGo)" (README.md:17, 137), so the docs carry the same inaccuracy as the result label. Pinning backend="duckduckgo" is a valid key: it posts to html.duckduckgo.com. Two smaller gaps. First, get_news is risk "low", so just removing it from "auto" would not make it ask; it needs the external gate, a higher risk or an "ask" rule. Second, the system prompt's mention of "email" points to read_email, which commit 3f29418 removed, and the calendar is local, so that prompt line is stale beyond the web case.
findings.corrected: config/settings.py:7-8 sets search_web and get_news to "auto". core/permission.py:17-18 then allows them without a prompt or a decisions check. So queries the model writes, which may include user input or project text it has read, go to remote search providers without asking. This contradicts config/system_prompt.py:18 ("External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission"). The "external": 1 key on get_news, search_web and read_web_content (tools/registry.py:42/48/54) is never read: agent.py only passes tool["risk"] to request_permission (agent.py:289). It looks like an unfinished gate, not dead code. Also, tools/web.py:49-50 calls ddgs.text() without a backend, so ddgs 9.16 uses "auto". Its enabled text engines are wikipedia, grokipedia, brave, duckduckgo (Bing-sourced), google, mojeek, startpage and yahoo; bing and yandex are disabled in this version. With max_results=5, every query goes to wikipedia and grokipedia first, then to one or more randomly chosen general engines until it has 5 results. So the `"source": "duckduckgo-search"` label (tools/web.py:55) and the README's "Web search (DuckDuckGo)" (README.md:17, 137) are inaccurate, and each query reaches about three providers, not just DuckDuckGo. Minor points: the "auto" rules for verify_app and get_news repeat their "low" risk and change nothing; no tool has risk "auto", so that part of core/permission.py:21 is dead; and the system prompt's "email" refers to a removed tool, while the calendar is local. Fix options: (a) implement `external` in request_permission, for example so external tools always ask unless a setting allows them, and drop search_web/get_news from "auto". Since get_news is risk "low", the external gate (or an explicit "ask") is needed for it. Or (b) remove the flag and rewrite the system prompt line. Pin backend="duckduckgo" if only DuckDuckGo is wanted, and handle DDGSException, since a single backend fails more often.
findings.status_note:
The external flag is wired up: external tools ask once per session. Still open: ddgs uses backend "auto", so queries reach several providers and the "duckduckgo-search" label is inaccurate.

Originally reported as: search_web/get_news are 'auto' despite the 'External access requires permission' rule; the registry 'external' flag is unused (unfinished)

findings.title: Registry descriptions omit the required parameter names of strict-signature tools
findings.detail: The model only sees the descriptions. get_news(country) takes a required `country`, but the description is just 'Get latest news headlines'. search_web(query) and read_web_content(urls) don't name their parameters either ('Search the web for information', '(list of URLs)'). get_project_structure() and read_calendar() take no arguments, but only verify_app says 'Takes no arguments'. Unlike the file tools, these have no **kwargs or alias handling, so {topic:...}, {q:...}, {url:...} or {path:'.'} raise TypeError. Verified for get_news(topic=...). This is the most likely trigger of the uncaught-exception finding.
findings.suggestion: Name the arguments in each description (e.g. 'Arguments: country (e.g. "Norway")', 'Arguments: query', 'Arguments: urls (list)', 'Takes no arguments'). Also accept the common aliases plus **kwargs the way tools/files.py does, or generate the argument list from inspect.signature in build_tool_prompt.
findings.status_note: Every registry entry has a JSON parameter schema that names its arguments, and a test checks every tool has one.

findings.title: write_file with a list path creates a junk file and reports success
findings.detail: write_file accepts `paths` and `files` aliases but, unlike read_files, doesn't handle lists. _safe_path(str(['static/app.js'])) is inside the project, so it passes. Verified: write_file(paths=['static/app.js'], content='x') creates the directory `['static` containing the file `app.js']` and returns "File created: ['static/app.js']". The model then believes static/app.js exists. edit_file(files=[...]) returns a misleading 'File not found'.
findings.suggestion: In write_file and edit_file, unwrap a single-element list and reject longer lists with a clear message. Better, make _safe_path reject non-str paths.
findings.verification_note:
The bug is real. I traced the code and reproduced it in memory with `_backup_and_write` stubbed out, so nothing was written to disk.

How it happens:
- At tools/files.py:340, `_first_arg` returns the list unchanged.
- `_safe_path` (tools/files.py:19) turns the list into a string with `str(path)`, giving `<BASE>/['static/app.js']`. That path is still inside BASE_DIR, so the check at line 22 lets it through.
- `_backup_and_write` (line 334) then runs `makedirs` and creates a directory named `['static` holding a file named `app.js']`.

What the reproduction showed:
- `_safe_path(['static/app.js'])` returns `("/home/hms/Desktop/Source/agent0/['static/app.js']", None)`.
- `write_file(paths=['static/app.js'], content='x')` returns `"File created: ['static/app.js']"`.
- A two-element list is accepted silently in the same way, producing `"File created: ['static/app.js', 'b.js']"`.
- `edit_file(files=['agent.py'], ...)` and `edit_file(file_path=['agent.py'], ...)` both return `'File not found'`, even though agent.py exists. That message is misleading.

The input can really reach this code:
- agent.py:111-128 passes the model's argument dict straight to `func(**args)`, with no normalization in between.
- `read_files` (tools/files.py:117-119) already special-cases lists, with the comment "A list of paths sometimes comes back". The logs back this up: there are 30 `read_files` calls where `paths`, `files` or `file_paths` was a list.
- The logs show no `write_file` call with a list path yet. The only 3 `write_file` entries use string paths.

Other guards and test coverage:
- The only guard is the "ask" permission rule (config/settings.py:11-12). The approval card shows the args, so a careful user might notice the brackets, but nothing in the code rejects the input.
- No test in tests/ touches `write_file`, `edit_file` or `_safe_path`.

Low severity is right: it needs a malformed tool call plus user approval, and the result is a junk file plus a misleading success message, not data loss or a path escape.

findings.title: Note shortcut hijacks ordinary requests, mangles text and can overwrite notes
findings.detail: The regex `^\s*(?:take note|note)\b` fires on any message starting with 'note'. Verified: 'Note that I want you to fix templates/index.html' is saved as a note and the agent never runs (agent_routes.shortcut_text_response runs first). sanitize_note_content strips anything shaped like a tag from a plain-text note: 'note: check if a<b and c>d' is saved as 'check if ad'. 'note - buy milk' keeps the leading '- '. Filenames have one-second resolution (`note_%Y%m%d_%H%M%S.txt`, opened with 'w'), so two notes in the same second overwrite each other. NOTE_FOLDER = Path('local_storage') depends on the working directory, unlike AUDIO_DIR, which uses BASE_DIR. Notes have no tests.
findings.suggestion: Require an explicit form ('note:', 'take note:', 'take a note'), and skip messages like 'note that ...' or anything that looks like a question or task. Drop the HTML stripping, since the template autoescapes. Use microseconds or a uniqueness suffix in the filename and open with 'x'. Anchor the folder to the project root (and maybe local_storage/notes/).
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and ran the parser read-only. Every claim holds.

1. **Hijack.** In tools/notes.py:24 the regex `^\s*(?:take note|note)\b[:\-]?\s*(.*)$` with IGNORECASE matches 'Note that I want you to fix templates/index.html' and returns 'that I want you to fix templates/index.html'. In core/agent_routes.py, `shortcut_text_response` (lines 44-47) runs before any LLM call in both POST /ask (line 91) and /ask_stream (line 164). It saves the text and returns 'Note saved to ...', so the agent never runs. 'Note, the file is broken' is also captured, as ', the file is broken'. The CLI is not affected: agent.py has no note shortcut, only calendar and play at lines 174/184.

2. **Mangling.** `parse_note_command('note: check if a<b and c>d')` returns 'check if ad', because the regex on line 15 strips `<b and c>`. `parse_note_command('note - buy milk')` returns '- buy milk': `[:\-]?` matches nothing because the space comes first, then `\s*` eats the space and the dash stays in the text. The stripping also does nothing useful. Note content is never shown back to the user (the reply is only the file path), the file is plain .txt, chat.js uses textContent, and Jinja2Templates autoescapes .html.

3. **Overwrite.** Lines 34-38 use `%Y%m%d_%H%M%S` and `open('w')`, so two notes saved in the same second write the same path and the last one wins. This is real but needs rapid or concurrent submissions.

4. **Folder path.** Line 5 is `NOTE_FOLDER = Path('local_storage')`, relative to the working directory, and line 6 runs mkdir at import time. features/audio/text_to_speech.py:12-14 anchors AUDIO_DIR to BASE_DIR instead.

5. **No tests.** Grepping tests/ for parse_note, save_note or note_saved finds nothing.

**Additional related issue (not in the original finding):** POST /speech (core/speech_routes.py:21-24) also auto-saves any transcript that starts with 'note'. static/speech.js ignores the `note_saved` field: it just puts the transcript into the input box. If the user then submits it, /ask_stream saves the same note a second time, and the user never got feedback that the first save happened.

Severity low is fair: it's a mis-routing and data-quality problem with no security impact.

findings.title: _safe_path lets a symlink inside the project point outside it, for reading and writing
findings.detail: It uses os.path.abspath rather than realpath, so symlinks are followed. For example, venv/bin/python3.12 points to /home/hms/.pyenv/versions/3.12.14/bin/python3.12, outside the project; that is binary today, but any text symlink would be readable and writable. Because read_files is 'auto', read_files('.env') returns APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD with no prompt, and agent.py:317-323 logs the first 500 characters of the result to local_storage/logs.txt. Writes into .git/hooks/ or venv/lib/.../site-packages are allowed, which means code execution; these are gated by 'ask', but see the approval-binding finding.
findings.suggestion: Use os.path.realpath on both BASE_DIR and the target before the prefix check. Add a denylist (.env*, .git/, venv/, models/) that read_files and the write tools refuse.
findings.verification_note:
The facts in the finding are correct, but the exploit story is overstated.

What I confirmed:
- tools/files.py:19 uses os.path.abspath, not realpath.
- _safe_path('.env') resolves inside BASE_DIR, and .env exists. RULES['read_files'] is 'auto' (config/settings.py:15), so request_permission returns True without asking (core/permission.py:17-18).
- agent.py:317-323 logs result_preview[:500]. The .env file is 28 bytes, so all of it would go into local_storage/logs.txt.

Why it is not a meaningful exploit:
1. Symlinks. The only symlinks that point outside the project are venv/bin/python, python3 and python3.12, which point to the pyenv interpreter. venv/lib64 points to venv/lib, and the models/ links point to blobs inside models/. Those three interpreter files are binary:
   - read_files returns the string "UnicodeDecodeError..." (it catches Exception).
   - write_file and edit_file open the file for reading first and only catch FileNotFoundError, so the UnicodeDecodeError propagates and nothing is written. I verified the decode error.
   - No tool can create a symlink, so the LLM cannot plant a new escape.
   - The one theoretical write-through is extract_inline_scripts with dest='venv/bin/python3.12' and overwrite=true. Its dest read catches UnicodeDecodeError, and _backup_and_write then opens the symlink for writing. That tool is 'ask' in RULES.
2. Reading .env. Without an attacker, the only reader is the authenticated owner (agent_router depends on is_logged_in) and the local Ollama model. logs.txt is gitignored (.gitignore:40) and sits on the same disk with the same permissions as .env, which is also gitignored. No /static, /media or /audio mount exposes local_storage/ or the repo root. Prompt injection could come in through auto tools: search_web is 'auto', and get_news is low risk and also 'auto'; both return DuckDuckGo snippets. But no auto-approved tool can send data somewhere an attacker can see it. search_web and get_news only send queries to DuckDuckGo. read_web_content, the only tool that fetches an arbitrary URL, has no RULES entry and is medium risk, so it asks.
3. Writes into .git/hooks or venv/site-packages are not an escalation. write_file and edit_file exist to edit the project's own .py files, such as core/ui.py and agent.py, and uvicorn --reload runs those. That is already code execution by design, behind the same 'ask' gate. Blocking .git/ and venv/ adds almost no security. The real weakness is the approval binding: create_permission_decisions in core/agent_routes.py:27-34 records the approval by action name only, not by the arguments shown. That is a separate finding.

Overall this is defense-in-depth hardening, not a reachable vulnerability. Two changes are worthwhile: deny .env* in read_files, which keeps the secret out of the LLM context and logs.txt and closes off a prompt-injection read, and use realpath, which is cheap. The .git/ and venv/ denylist adds little.
findings.corrected:
tools/files.py:14-25 (_safe_path) uses os.path.abspath rather than realpath, and it has no denylist. This is low severity, hardening only. Nothing currently exploits it.

Symlinks: the only symlinks leading out of the project are venv/bin/python, python3 and python3.12, all binary. read_files returns a decode-error string, and write_file/edit_file raise UnicodeDecodeError before writing. No tool can create a symlink. The single write-through path is extract_inline_scripts(dest='venv/bin/python3.12', overwrite=true), which catches the decode error on dest and writes through the link. It is gated by 'ask'.

.env: read_files('.env') is auto-approved (config/settings.py:15) and returns APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD. agent.py:317-323 then copies all 28 bytes into local_storage/logs.txt. Both files are gitignored, local, and not served over HTTP, and only the logged-in owner and local Ollama see the result. No auto-approved tool can exfiltrate it to an attacker: search_web and get_news only query DuckDuckGo, and read_web_content requires approval.

Writes to .git/hooks or venv add no capability beyond what write_file/edit_file already allow by design, since they edit project .py files that uvicorn --reload executes. The actual weak point is that approval is bound to the action name, not its arguments (core/agent_routes.py:27-34), which is a separate finding.

Recommended fix: make read_files and the write tools refuse .env*, and switch to os.path.realpath on both BASE_DIR and the target. A .git/ and venv/ denylist is optional.
findings.status_note: Sensitive names are now checked on the resolved target. The resolved path is not required to stay inside the project: a pre-existing link to an outside file is readable (read_files is auto-approved) and writable after approval. Verified by reproducing it in a scratch project. docs/features/permissions.md says symlinks are included in the sandbox. Originally reported as: _safe_path doesn't resolve symlinks or protect sensitive in-project paths

findings.title: read_web_content: unrestricted targets, follows redirects, no size or total-time limit
findings.detail: requests.get(url, timeout=10) accepts http://127.0.0.1:11434 (Ollama), http://localhost:8000, LAN router pages and so on, and follows redirects, so an approved public URL can redirect to localhost. The tool is gated by 'ask', but approvals aren't bound to arguments (see the permission finding). The whole body is loaded into memory before truncation to 20000 characters, regardless of Content-Type (PDFs and ISOs are decoded as text). The 10 s timeout applies to each read, not the whole request, so a slow-dripping server can hold the call (and the event loop) indefinitely. A string passed as `urls` returns 'urls must be a list' instead of being wrapped.
findings.suggestion: Allow only http/https. Resolve the host and reject loopback, private and link-local addresses (and re-check after redirects, or set allow_redirects=False). Use stream=True, cap bytes read (e.g. 2 MB), check that Content-Type is text/html or text/plain, and wrap a single string in a list.
findings.verification_note:
Most of the mechanics check out. tools/web.py:31 calls `requests.get(url, timeout=10)` with no host check, no `stream=True` and no Content-Type check. Requests follows redirects by default, `r.text` loads the whole body before the `[:20000]` slice, and the 10 s timeout applies to each socket read, not the whole download. The tool is reachable: `read_web_content` is listed to the LLM in tools/registry.py:50 with risk "medium" and has no `RULES` entry, so `request_permission` asks. In the web flow the approval is not tied to arguments. The card in templates/components/permission_card.html posts `input` and `permission_action` to /ask. `create_permission_decisions` (core/agent_routes.py:27) builds `{action: True}` and ignores `permission_args`. `run_agent` then reruns from scratch, so the LLM can choose different URLs, and every later `read_web_content` call in that run (up to 8 steps) runs without a new prompt.

Some details are wrong or overstated:
(1) The "allow only http/https" check is already in place. Requests raises `InvalidSchema` for file://, ftp:// and gopher:// (verified with requests 2.34.2).
(2) Reaching internal hosts gains an attacker very little. The tool can only send GET requests, and responses go only into the LLM's context. Ollama's GET endpoints only return metadata such as the model list. The app's own routes on :8000 need a session cookie, which requests does not send, and the routes that don't need one (`/static`, `/media`, `/audio`) are open to anyone on loopback anyway. LAN pages usually need their own login.
(3) The more realistic risk is something private-IP blocking would not stop. A page fetched under one approval can tell the LLM to call `read_files` (auto-allowed in config/settings.py:15, and able to read anything inside the project, including `.env` with `APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD`). It can then call `read_web_content` on a public attacker URL with the stolen data in the query string, and that call runs without a prompt. The fix belongs in how approvals are scoped (tie them to the exact arguments and to one call), not only in filtering hosts.
(4) Blocking the event loop is not specific to this tool. Both `async def ask` (core/agent_routes.py:119) and `ask_stream`'s `event_stream` (core/agent_routes.py:192) run the synchronous agent loop on the event-loop thread, so every tool call and every `query_llm` call blocks it. This tool is just the one with no overall time limit.
(5) Passing a string for `urls` does return "urls must be a list", as reported. Because `rate_limit` runs before the type check, the failed call also uses up the 5 s cooldown. A corrected retry within 5 s then gets "Rate limit exceeded" (verified). Calling it with `url=...` raises `TypeError`, and nothing catches it at agent.py:309 (`result = execute_tool(action, args)`), so the whole run crashes.

Low severity is right for a single-user local app.
findings.corrected: tools/web.py:20-42 `read_web_content`: requests.get(url, timeout=10) puts no limit on the target host, follows redirects, reads the whole body into memory without checking Content-Type, and its timeout applies to each read, not the whole request. Requests already rejects schemes other than http/https (InvalidSchema), so the scheme check is not needed. Reaching internal hosts gains little: the tool can only send GET requests and results go only to the LLM, so it can read Ollama's read-only GET endpoints and the app's unauthenticated /static, /media and /audio mounts, while the app's real routes need a session cookie. The bigger risk is how approvals work. A web approval is keyed only by action name (core/agent_routes.py:27 ignores permission_args) and covers every read_web_content call in the rerun of up to 8 steps. A fetched page can therefore direct the auto-allowed read_files (config/settings.py:15, can read project files including .env) and then read_web_content to a public attacker URL that carries the data in its query string, all without a new prompt. Blocking private IPs does not prevent this; approvals need to be tied to the exact arguments and to a single call. Event-loop blocking applies to every tool and LLM call, because /ask and /ask_stream run the synchronous agent loop inside async handlers (core/agent_routes.py:119, 192); this tool is just the one with no total time limit. Related robustness bugs: rate_limit runs before the list check, so a string `urls` uses up the 5 s cooldown and the corrected retry gets "Rate limit exceeded"; calling with `url=` raises TypeError, which is not caught at agent.py:309 and crashes the run. Suggested fix: wrap a string in a list and accept url/url aliases; check the type before rate-limiting; use stream=True with a byte cap and an overall deadline; check Content-Type; optionally block loopback, private and link-local addresses, re-checked on every redirect; tie web approvals to the exact arguments.

findings.title: A long-line file under 400 lines can still produce a ~100k-character read result
findings.detail: A single read_files result can be about 100000 characters (roughly 25-30k tokens), and a list of paths has no total cap. core/llm.py:19-22 notes that overflow is silently truncated and 'the model then loses the instructions'. Verified trigger: local_storage/logs.txt is 626 KB, so read_files returns 100000 characters, more than the whole context. No source file exceeds 20 KB today, but several reads accumulate in `context`.
findings.suggestion: Lower the per-read cap to about 30-40k characters, add a total cap for list reads, and support offset/limit (or line ranges) so large files can be paged.
findings.verification_note:
I couldn't refute this; it holds up end to end.

1. **The cap is 100k characters.** In tools/files.py:10, MAX_READ_CHARS = 100000. read_files (tools/files.py:113-141) cuts content at that many characters. A list of paths is handled at line 118-119 as `{p: read_files(p) for p in path}`, with no total cap.

2. **Nothing guards the result.** read_files is auto-approved (config/settings.py:15, "read_files": "auto"). _safe_path lets it read any file under BASE_DIR, including local_storage/ and models/. In agent.py:339, the loop appends the whole result to `context` (`context += f"...Result: {result}\n"`) with no truncation. Only the log preview is cut to 500 characters (line 322). Lines 211-218 then send SYSTEM_PROMPT, the tool list and the full `context` to query_llm, with num_ctx=16384 (core/llm.py:21,32).

3. **The trigger is real.** A read-only check showed that read_files('local_storage/logs.txt') returns 100079 characters, including the TRUNCATED marker; the file is now 640 KB. The faster-whisper tokenizer.json blob under models/ (2.2 MB) also returns 100079 characters. Passing both as paths=[...] returned two 100079-character entries, about 200k characters, so there is no total cap. The whisper BPE tokenizer was used as a stand-in for the model's tokenizer. It counts the logs read as about 45k tokens, against about 1k for the system prompt plus tool list. Qwen's tokenizer is more efficient, but fitting 16384 tokens would need about 6 characters per token, so the read alone overflows the context.

4. **Ollama really truncates silently.** The installed version is 0.34.4. I sent qwen3:4b a prompt of about 4000 tokens with num_ctx=256 (keep_alive=0, so no model stayed loaded). It returned HTTP 200 with prompt_eval_count=130 and no error, so the overflow is cut silently, as core/llm.py:18-20 warns. query_llm's raise_for_status() never fires, and the model is left with a partial prompt.

5. **No tests cover it.** Nothing under tests/ refers to read_files, MAX_READ_CHARS or truncation.

Low severity is fair: no source file is over 20 KB today (the largest is features/audio/text_to_speech.py at 19247 characters), so it takes a log, model, or data file, or many reads adding up over up to 8 steps. The reviewer's token figure is also on the low side for JSONL logs; the stand-in tokenizer counts about 45k tokens, not 25-30k, though the conclusion holds either way.

One caveat for the fix: line 95 also uses MAX_READ_CHARS as the size limit for search_files content matching. Lowering the constant would quietly shrink which files search_files can match by content. The read limit should be split into its own constant, ideally based on OLLAMA_NUM_CTX, and the fix should also cap the total size of `context` in agent.py, not only single reads.
findings.status_note: Files of 400 or more lines are now returned as an outline, and core/context.py trims oversized results for the model. Originally reported as: MAX_READ_CHARS (100k chars) exceeds the model's 16384-token context

findings.title: parse_script_refactor_command still matches loosely, though the rewrite now needs approval
findings.detail: Any message containing 'script', a .html name and a word like 'external' or 'out of' becomes a forced first extract_inline_scripts call (agent.py:100-106). Verified: 'Which scripts in index.html load external libraries?' returns {'path': 'templates/index.html'}. The user gets a permission card to rewrite index.html. Rejecting it ends the run with 'Action denied', so the question is never answered.
findings.suggestion: Require imperative phrasing (move, extract, 'no inline') and skip questions (a leading wh-word or a trailing '?'). Alternatively, on denial of a forced decision, fall through to the normal LLM loop instead of returning.
findings.verification_note: I traced the code path and reproduced it without calling the LLM or writing logs. parse_script_refactor_command (tools/files.py:266-295) only requires three things: the substring "script", one keyword from the list at lines 280-286 (it includes "external", "only loaded", "not defined", "out of" and "separate"), and a *.html token. It has no check for imperative phrasing or for questions. For 'Which scripts in index.html load external libraries?' it returns {'path': 'templates/index.html'}. The same happens for 'Does index.html have any external scripts?', 'Are the scripts in index.html only loaded once?' and 'Why is the script in index.html not defined?'. None of the earlier shortcuts catches these inputs: parse_note_command, parse_create_command, is_calendar_request and parse_play_command all return None. needs_tools() is True because of ".html", so the local-first answer is skipped. planned_first_decision (agent.py:93-108) then injects extract_inline_scripts as pending_decision, and no LLM is consulted. RULES has extract_inline_scripts set to "ask" and the registry gives it risk "high", so request_permission raises PermissionRequired. I simulated _run_steps with decisions={} and got a permission_required event with args {'path': 'templates/index.html'} and reason 'Move the inline script out to its own file and link it'. The Reject button in templates/components/permission_card.html posts to /ask with permission_decision=n, which becomes {'extract_inline_scripts': False}. That re-runs run_agent, the same forced decision comes back, request_permission returns False, and agent.py:301-303 yields final_response 'Action denied' and returns. The question is never answered. The CLI behaves the same way: answering 'n' at the input() prompt also gives 'Action denied'. No test covers parse_script_refactor_command or planned_first_decision, since grep finds neither in tests/. One detail limits the impact today: no template in templates/ or features/*/templates currently has an inline script block matching INLINE_SCRIPT_RE. So if the user approves, extract_inline_scripts returns 'No inline <script> blocks found ... nothing to move' and the LLM loop continues normally, with no rewrite. The real harm right now is a misleading high-risk permission prompt, and a dead end if the user rejects it. An actual unwanted rewrite would only happen once a template has inline scripts again. Low severity fits. The finding's location, mechanism and failure scenario are accurate.
findings.status_note: extract_inline_scripts now has the 'ask' rule, so a wrongly forced call asks first. The intent match ('move', 'external', 'out of' plus any .html name) is unchanged. Originally reported as: parse_script_refactor_command forces a file-rewriting tool on read-only questions

findings.title: get_news uses a fragile site:-OR text search; HTML-to-text leaves entities and comment fragments
findings.detail:
get_news calls text search with 'latest news X site:a OR site:b ... '. The OR precedence makes the site filter unreliable, nothing guarantees recent results, and the function shares the 5 s rate limiter with search_web, so a search_web followed by get_news inside 5 s returns 'Rate limit exceeded'. The agent's duplicate guard then blocks retrying the same call. ddgs 9.16 has DDGS().news(query, timelimit='d', max_results=...), which returns dated news items. _extract_text_from_html doesn't unescape entities: verified, '

Tom & Jerry ’s ok

' becomes 'Tom & Jerry ’s b --> ok'. requests also falls back to ISO-8859-1 for text/html served without a charset.
findings.suggestion: Use ddgs.news() with a timelimit for get_news and give it its own rate-limit key. For page text, use lxml.html (already in requirements.txt) with text_content() after removing script, style and noscript, or at least html.unescape and strip <!--...-->. Fall back to r.apparent_encoding when the header has no charset.
findings.verification_note:
I checked each claim in the code and the venv. **get_news (tools/web.py:59-64)** - Line 63 builds the query `latest news {country} site:reuters.com OR site:bbc.com OR ... {year}` and sends it to `search_web` (line 64), which runs `ddgs.text()`. - Nothing in that path limits results by date. The year keyword is the only recency signal. - `get_news` checks its own `rate_limit("get_news")` key, but it then calls `search_web`, which checks `rate_limit("search_web")` (line 45). So if `search_web` ran less than 5 s earlier, `get_news` returns "Rate limit exceeded". The reverse order fails too, because `get_news` also stamps the search_web key. **Duplicate guard (agent.py:276-284)** - The call's signature goes into `attempted` before the tool runs. A rate-limited call that the model retries with the same args is therefore answered "You already ran this exact action" and never runs again. **ddgs.news() availability** - ddgs is 9.16.0 (pinned in requirements.txt:12). - `DDGS.news()` exists (ddgs.py:233) and passes `timelimit` through `_search_sync`. - All three news engines (duckduckgo_news, bing_news, yahoo_news) use `timelimit`. **HTML-to-text (tools/web.py:9-17)** - I ran the function on the sample input. It returns `'Tom & Jerry ’s b --> ok'`, exactly as the finding says: entities are not unescaped, and `<[^>]+>` stops at the `>` inside the comment. **Encoding** - lxml==6.1.3 is in requirements.txt:31. - requests 2.34.2's `get_encoding_from_headers` returns "ISO-8859-1" for a text/* content type with no charset (utils.py:586-587). `r.text` then decodes UTF-8 pages wrongly. **Severity and nothing else affected** - Low severity fits. - Only tools/registry.py and config/settings.py RULES refer to `get_news`, by name. Its signature stays the same under the suggestion, so it is not a design change. **Caveats on the suggestion (implementation details, not a refutation)** 1. `get_news` already has its own rate-limit key. The real fix is to stop sending it through `search_web`. 2. `lxml.html` `text_content()` joins text from neighbouring block elements with no space between them. I tested it: `

Title

Some text

` gives "TitleSome text". Use `itertext()` with a separator, or add whitespace between blocks. 3. `test_read_web_content_with_mocked_requests` (tests/test_web_tools.py) uses a MockResponse that has no `headers`, `encoding` or `apparent_encoding`. The encoding fallback needs `getattr` guards, or that test needs updating.

findings.title: .bak backups are single-generation and not gitignored
findings.detail: _backup_and_write overwrites <path>.bak on every write, so a second edit (or the repeated execution from the permission rerun loop) loses the original. .gitignore ignores only `.env`, `env.bak/` and `venv.bak/`, so `*.bak` files show up as untracked and can be committed with `git add .`. A write_file to .env would leave an unignored .env.bak containing the password.
findings.suggestion: Add `*.bak` to .gitignore. Consider keeping the first backup per session or timestamped backups (e.g. <path>.<ts>.bak, with pruning).
findings.verification_note:
I checked each part of the premise against the code.

(1) Backups keep only one generation. tools/files.py:329-332 `_backup_and_write` opens `full_path + ".bak"` with mode "w" whenever old_content is non-empty. write_file (line 362), edit_file (line 428) and extract_inline_scripts (lines 224-225) all go through it, so each write overwrites the previous .bak. Nothing in the repo restores from a .bak or rotates it (grep for `.bak` finds only these lines, CLAUDE.md:41 and an unrelated test fixture).

(2) Repeated writes really happen. core/permission.py:26-27 approves by action name only (`if action in decisions`). So once write_file or edit_file is approved for a run, every later call to that action in the same `_run_steps` run (agent.py:288-309) runs without asking again. Two edit_file calls on the same file therefore leave the intermediate version in .bak, and the original is gone. The approval form (templates/components/permission_card.html:20) posts back to /ask, and `create_permission_decisions` (core/agent_routes.py:27-34) carries only one action. The whole agent loop then restarts from scratch, so a write that already ran can run again in a later approval round, overwriting .bak with the already-modified content. Whether that happens depends on what the model picks, but the path exists.

(3) .gitignore does not cover backups. `git check-ignore -v .env.bak foo.py.bak templates/index.html.bak static/x.js.bak` matched nothing (exit 1). The only related patterns are `.env` (exact name), `env.bak/` and `venv.bak/` (directories only). No .bak files are tracked or currently present.

(4) The .env scenario holds. `_safe_path` (tools/files.py:14-25) only blocks paths outside the project, so write_file or edit_file on `.env` is allowed once the user approves (RULES has "ask" for both). That writes `.env.bak` with the old contents, and the file is not ignored. core/auth.py:8 reads APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD via load_dotenv (core/ui.py:1-3), so the leaked backup would hold the login password.

The suggested fix breaks nothing. No code reads .bak files back, and ignoring them does not affect git-tracked files or tests. Severity low and location tools/files.py:329 are accurate.
findings.status_note: Backups go to local_storage/backups/<timestamp>/<path>, one per write, and local_storage/ is gitignored. Nothing prunes them, as documented.

findings.title: Still no tests for _safe_path traversal, the <script> guard and extract_inline_scripts
findings.detail: Nothing tests _safe_path traversal (../, absolute paths, sibling dirs), edit_file's 0/1/>1 and lenient branches (where the line-merge bug above would have been caught), _script_edit_guard, extract_inline_scripts, verify_app, notes.py or core/permission.py. tests/test_web_tools.py doesn't reset tools.web.last_called. A second read_web_content test in the same session within 5 s gets the string 'Rate limit exceeded', and `"https://example.com" in result` fails.
findings.suggestion: Add tests/test_files_tools.py using monkeypatch on tools.files.BASE_DIR with tmp_path, tests/test_verify.py and tests/test_permission.py. Add an autouse fixture that clears tools.web.last_called.
findings.verification_note:
Mostly accurate. The tests/ directory has 8 files (test_agent_flow, test_audio_tool, test_calendar, test_llm, test_speech_routes, test_text_to_speech, test_web_tools) and no conftest.py. None of them import tools.files, tools.verify or tools.notes. So _safe_path (tools/files.py:14), extract_inline_scripts (:156), _script_edit_guard (:234), _lenient_pattern (:312), write_file (:339), edit_file (:370), verify_app (tools/verify.py:37) and notes.py (parse_note_command and save_note_text) have no direct or indirect test coverage.

tests/test_web_tools.py:14-24 does not reset tools.web.last_called (tools/web.py:67, a module-level dict). I checked this by running read_web_content twice in one process with requests mocked. The first call returns {'https://example.com': 'hi'}. The second returns the string 'Rate limit exceeded', so `'https://example.com' in result` is False.

Two details are overstated:
(1) core/permission.py is tested indirectly, not "nothing". tests/test_agent_flow.py:102 test_ui_permission_flow runs through request_permission (agent.py:289). It covers the RULES "ask" path: with an empty decisions map it raises PermissionRequired, and it returns the decision when one is supplied. test_llm_requests_search_web_and_uses_tool also goes through the RULES "auto" path. What is missing is a direct unit test, for example of the risk-level fallback for actions not in RULES and of the CLI input() path.
(2) The rate-limit leak is latent, not a failure today. read_web_content is the only test that calls the rate limiter. test_agent_flow monkeypatches search_web, so the suite currently passes (121). The test would only fail if someone added a second read_web_content test.

The suggestion would not break anything. _safe_path reads the module global BASE_DIR when it is called, so monkeypatching tools.files.BASE_DIR to tmp_path works. An autouse fixture that clears webmod.last_called is safe.
findings.corrected:
Nothing directly tests the safety-critical file tools. None of these are exercised by any test:
- tools/files.py: _safe_path traversal handling (../, absolute paths, sibling <base>-evil dirs), edit_file's 0/1/>1 matches and lenient branches, _script_edit_guard, extract_inline_scripts and write_file
- tools/verify.py: verify_app
- tools/notes.py

core/permission.py is only covered indirectly, through tests/test_agent_flow.py: test_ui_permission_flow covers the RULES "ask" raise/approve path and test_llm_requests_search_web_and_uses_tool covers the "auto" path. Nothing unit-tests the risk-level fallback for unlisted actions or the CLI input() branch.

tests/test_web_tools.py:14 doesn't reset the module-level tools.web.last_called dict. This is a latent hazard, not a current failure, because it is the only test that hits the rate limiter (the suite passes 121/121). If a second read_web_content test runs in the same session within 5 s, the call returns the string 'Rate limit exceeded' and `"https://example.com" in result` fails.

Fix:
- Add tests/test_files_tools.py that monkeypatches tools.files.BASE_DIR to tmp_path (this works because _safe_path reads the global when called).
- Add tests/test_verify.py and direct tests for core/permission.py.
- Add an autouse fixture, in tests/conftest.py or test_web_tools.py, that clears tools.web.last_called.
findings.status_note: tests/test_files.py now covers edit_file's lenient matching, backups, line ranges, the read outline and the secret-file rules. Originally reported as: No tests for the safety-critical tool code; the web test leaks rate-limit state

findings.title: /audio StaticFiles mount serves saved audio without authentication
findings.detail: audio_router has Depends(is_logged_in), but the files themselves are served by an app-level StaticFiles mount (`app.mount("/audio", StaticFiles(directory=str(AUDIO_DIR)))`), and no router dependency or middleware applies to it. I verified with TestClient and no session: GET /audio/tts_2026-10-09_08-47.wav returns 200, audio/wav, 136844 bytes, while GET /tts/files without a session returns 303 to /login. Default names are easy to guess (tts_YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM.wav with _2/_3 suffixes, see text_to_speech.py:147-153), so anyone who can reach the server can enumerate and download every generated or converted clip. This contradicts README.md:105 ("All routes require a logged-in session"). uvicorn's default 127.0.0.1 bind limits exposure, but the login exists precisely for when it is reachable.
findings.suggestion: Replace the mount with an authenticated GET /audio/{filename} route in audio_router. It should resolve AUDIO_DIR / filename, check that resolved.parent == AUDIO_DIR.resolve() and that the suffix is in AUDIO_EXTENSIONS, and return FileResponse with the mimetype. The URL stays the same, so tts.js, audio-player.js, player.py and the templates don't change. Alternatively, wrap the StaticFiles app in a small ASGI wrapper that checks scope['session'].
findings.verification_note:
I reproduced it. core/ui.py:30 mounts `/audio` as a bare StaticFiles app. The only auth is `Depends(is_logged_in)` on the individual APIRouters (agent, speech, audio, calendar, logout). No middleware checks auth: SessionMiddleware only decodes the cookie. So nothing guards a Mount.

I ran TestClient(app) with no cookie:
- GET /audio/tts_2026-10-09_08-47.wav → 200, audio/wav, 136844 bytes
- GET /tts/files → 303 to /login
- GET /audio/ → 404 (no directory listing)
- Path traversal (`..%2f`, `../`) → 404, or normalised and caught by the catch-all

So the leak is limited to files inside local_storage/audio/, but every one of them can be downloaded.

Default names are easy to guess. `_build_filename_stem` (features/audio/text_to_speech.py:136-155) uses minute precision `tts_%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M` plus `_2`/`_3` suffixes, which is about 1440 names per day. Uploads and conversions are also predictable: `upload_{timestamp}.{ext}` and `converted_{timestamp}.{fmt}` (around lines 461/465). Uploaded originals sit in the same directory, so user-supplied audio is exposed too.

The LLM path doesn't matter here. This is plain HTTP and needs no tool or permission.

Exposure is limited because the documented runs (README.md:59, :70) use uvicorn's default 127.0.0.1 bind, so only local processes or users, or someone who rebinds to 0.0.0.0, can reach it. Medium is defensible given the login exists for exactly that case. One small wording point: README.md:105 sits under the TTS endpoint table, so it doesn't strictly promise anything about `/audio`, though the spirit matches.

There is a related, worse issue the fix must take into account. core/ui.py:34 hardcodes `SessionMiddleware(secret_key="THIS_SECRET")`. I signed `{"authenticated": true}` with itsdangerous TimestampSigner('THIS_SECRET') and got 200 on /tts/files, so anyone who has read the source can forge a session for every route. The suggested authenticated `/audio/{filename}` route is correct, but it only protects anything once the secret comes from the environment or a random per-install value.
findings.status_note: /audio/<file> is no longer a public mount. It is a route in audio_router, which requires login, and StaticFiles still serves the file (path checks and range requests). Tests cover login, range requests and path traversal.

findings.title: "play" shortcut takes over any message starting with "play" and never reaches the LLM
findings.detail: parse_play_command matches `^\s*play\b...(.*)` and returns the rest as a filename query. Both agent.py:184 (_run_steps) and core/agent_routes.py:99/170 (via audio_play_result) then return describe_play_result() unconditionally, even when the search finds nothing. Verified: "Play chess with me" -> {'query': 'chess with me'}; "Play devil's advocate: is this plan good?" -> {'query': "devil's advocate: ..."}; "play the role of a pirate and tell me a joke" -> {'query': 'role of a pirate and tell me a joke'}; "Play a song about cats" -> {'query': 'a song about cats'}. Each one answers "No saved audio file matches '...'" and the LLM is never consulted. The anchoring only guards against "please play X"; ordinary requests that start with "play" still get captured.
findings.suggestion: Only short-circuit when the shortcut actually found something. In audio_play_result and in the agent.py block, return the result when status is 'play' or 'choose', or when the query is empty or a bare number. When status is 'error' and the query is free text, return None so the request goes on to the LLM. Alternatively, tighten the regex to require an audio extension, a "number N" form, or an existing filename match. Add tests for "Play chess with me" and similar inputs.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and reproduced the bug with read-only calls; I found nothing that guards against it.
- `features/audio/player.py:140-143`: `_PLAY_RE` is `^\s*play\b(?:\s+(?:me\s+)?(?:the\s+)?(?:file\s+|track\s+|number\s+|saved\s+)*(.*))?$`, so any message that starts with the word "play" matches. `parse_play_command` (line 157) always returns `{"query": <rest>}` for these. The only thing that stops it is the word boundary: "Playing around..." returns None.
- `agent.py:184-188` (`_run_steps`, used by both the CLI's `run_agent` and the web's `stream_agent`): whenever `play_args` is not None, it yields `final_response` with `describe_play_result(result)` and returns. This happens before `needs_tools`, `try_local_answer` or the tool loop, and it does not check `result["status"]`.
- `core/agent_routes.py:57-67`: `audio_play_result` returns `play_audio_file(**play_args)` unconditionally. Its callers at line 99 (`/ask`) and line 170 (`/ask_stream`) return the shortcut response whenever the result is not None, and an error dict is never None. The `shortcut_text_response` check that runs before it only handles note and calendar-creation commands, so it doesn't catch these.
- To demonstrate, I monkeypatched `agent.query_llm` and `agent.try_local_answer` to raise if called. Running `list(agent._run_steps(s, None))` and `audio_play_result(s)` for "Play chess with me", "play the role of a pirate and tell me a joke" and "Play a song about cats" gave `final_response` "No saved audio file matches '<rest>'." with `audio={'status':'error',...}`. The LLM stubs were never called. The parse results match the reviewer's exactly, including "Play devil's advocate: is this plan good?". "play to win: tips?" is captured the same way.
- Tests: `tests/test_audio_tool.py:29-31` only checks "I want to play with the code" and "please play my-music.mp3". No test covers a free-text "Play X ..." request.

A related effect: because `_matches` matches substrings, a short free-text remainder can match real files by accident. For example, "play tts" would offer every `tts_*.wav` file. The reviewer's suggestion is sound: only short-circuit when the status is play or choose, or when the query is empty or a number, and fall through to the LLM otherwise. Medium severity is fair, because this silently breaks a common class of chat prompts without crashing anything.

findings.title: LLM-invoked play_audio_file tool can never make the UI play anything
findings.detail: The registry exposes play_audio_file to the LLM, but _run_steps (agent.py:308-338) treats only calendar event lists specially (is_calendar_event_list -> show_calendar). Any other tool result is just appended to the LLM context as text. When the LLM picks this tool, the {'status':'play','audio_url':...} or {'status':'choose',...} dict is never passed on as the `audio` field of final_response. The LLM then writes something like "Playing X" and no player or choice buttons appear. run_agent (used by /ask) also drops any audio field. This path is reachable for every play request the shortcut doesn't catch: "please play my-music.mp3" (a test even asserts this is ignored by the shortcut), "can you play ...", or non-English phrasing. A 'choose' result from this path still fills _last_candidates without ever showing the list.
findings.suggestion: Decide between implementing and removing. To implement: in _run_steps, after execute_tool, if action == 'play_audio_file' and result.get('status') in ('play','choose'), yield {'event':'final_response','response':describe_play_result(result),'audio':result} and return, mirroring the calendar branch. In run_agent, also return the audio payload so /ask can render audio_data. To remove: delete the registry entry and rely only on the shortcut, and update CLAUDE.md, which describes it as a real LLM tool.
findings.verification_note:
I checked this against the code, and the finding holds. tools/registry.py:66-70 registers play_audio_file as an LLM tool with low risk. In agent.py::_run_steps, the only special handling after execute_tool (lines 308-336) is the is_calendar_event_list -> show_calendar branch. Any other result, including play_audio_file's {'status':'play'|'choose',...} dict, is only added to the LLM context as text by `context += f"...Result: {result}\n"` (line 339). The loop then goes on until the LLM returns action 'none', and that final_response (line 254) carries only `response`, never `audio`.

The frontend shows the player or choice buttons only when the final_response event has an `audio` field (static/chat.js:119 renderAudioResult(event.audio)) or when /ask passes `audio_data` (core/agent_routes.py:103 and features/audio/templates/audio/audio_play.html). Both of those are set only by the parse_play_command shortcuts: agent.py:184-188, core/agent_routes.py:99-104 and core/agent_routes.py:170-178. run_agent (agent.py:357-371) keeps only `response`/`show_calendar` and drops `audio`. So when /ask falls through to the LLM loop, audio_data is never set.

The path is reachable. parse_play_command is anchored to a leading "play", and tests/test_audio_tool.py:31 asserts that "please play my-music.mp3" returns None. ".mp3" is also not in FILE_TASK_RE, so that input goes through try_local_answer and on to the tool loop, where the LLM can pick play_audio_file. When it does, no player appears.

One small correction: on a 'choose' result, _last_candidates is set (features/audio/player.py:122), and the candidate list does reach the LLM context as text. The LLM may repeat the numbered list in prose, and a follow-up "play number N" would then work through the shortcut. So "never showing the list" overstates it: the clickable choice UI never appears, but the list is not always lost. This does not change the core finding or its severity.

The suggested fix fits: mirror the calendar branch in _run_steps for play_audio_file results with status play/choose, and return the audio payload from run_agent so /ask can set audio_data. It is a cross-file change, because the run_agent return shape is consumed by core/agent_routes.py.

findings.title: Filename deduplication only checks .wav, so generating MP3/FLAC/OGG can silently overwrite an existing file
findings.detail: _build_filename_stem only checks `(AUDIO_DIR / f"{candidate}.wav").exists()`. The final file is written by _encode_flac (sf.write, overwrites) or by ffmpeg with `-y` (overwrites). Reproduced in a scratch dir: with an existing 'Weekly Update.flac' (no .wav), synthesize(..., output_format='flac', title='Weekly Update') returned 'Weekly Update.flac' and replaced the previous file's contents. This happens whenever the matching .wav is missing, for example after the user deletes the large leftover WAV (see the next finding) or for files copied in from elsewhere. Fixing the leftover WAV would make this overwrite happen every time. There is also a check-then-write race: two concurrent requests with the same title (or no title, in the same minute) can both pick the same stem.
findings.suggestion: Treat a stem as taken if any `stem + ext` exists for ext in OUTPUT_FORMATS (or AUDIO_EXTENSIONS). Claim the name atomically, for example by opening the final path with mode 'x' in a loop, so concurrent requests can't both pick it. Add a test: an existing 'X.mp3' plus title 'X' and format mp3 should produce 'X_2.mp3'.
findings.verification_note:
I read the code and ran it, and the bug is real. features/audio/text_to_speech.py:151 only checks whether `<candidate>.wav` exists. The stem is then used at :336 (synthesize) and :423 (synthesize_dialogue, which the finding doesn't mention but has the same problem). `_finalize_output` (:287) writes the final file with `sf.write` in `_encode_flac` (:253) or with `ffmpeg -y` (:271), and both silently overwrite an existing file. Nothing else guards against this. There is no `exists` or `'x'`-mode check anywhere, and the only test (tests/test_text_to_speech.py:197) seeds `My Title.wav`, so it never covers a non-wav sibling.

I reproduced it in the scratchpad by monkeypatching AUDIO_DIR and stubbing `_synthesize_kokoro`, so no project files were touched:
- The first flac with title 'Weekly Update' produced 'Weekly Update.flac' plus the leftover 'Weekly Update.wav'.
- The second produced 'Weekly Update_2.flac', so in normal use the leftover WAV hides the bug.
- After I removed the .wav files, a third call returned 'Weekly Update.flac', and the file's samples changed from 0.1 to 0.5. The earlier output was overwritten.

How likely it is in practice, which the finding mostly states correctly:
- The app has no delete endpoint. `/tts/files` only lists, and nothing in the repo unlinks generated WAVs. So the WAV goes missing only if someone deletes it by hand, or if files were copied into local_storage/audio. That second case is plausible, because `player.find_audio_files` plays any .wav/.mp3/.flac/.ogg found there.
- The finding is right that cleaning up the leftover intermediate WAV would make this overwrite happen on every repeated title. That makes it a real trap for whoever fixes that issue.
- The race is real but narrow. The routes call synthesize through `run_in_threadpool`, so requests do run in parallel. But the stem is picked only after synthesis finishes, right before `_write_wav`, so two requests would both have to finish synthesizing at almost the same moment.

On severity: it's a latent data-loss bug. Today it only shows up after a manual delete or with copied-in files, so "medium" is defensible but on the high side.
findings.status_note: The duplicate-name check covers every output extension and the name is claimed with an exclusive create (features/audio/text_to_speech.py `_reserve_output_path`).

findings.title: MP3/FLAC/OGG output leaves the intermediate WAV in local_storage/audio, so "play <title>" always asks you to choose
findings.detail: synthesize/synthesize_dialogue always write `<stem>.wav` into AUDIO_DIR. _finalize_output then encodes it to .flac/.mp3/.ogg next to it and never deletes the WAV. Reproduced: requesting mp3 with title 'Clip' leaves ['Clip.mp3', 'Clip.wav'], and play_audio_file(query='Clip') returns status 'choose' instead of 'play'. Every non-WAV generation therefore doubles disk use: 24 kHz 16-bit mono is about 170 MB for a 10,000-word, roughly 1-hour request. It also clutters the /tts/files search and the chat play list. The README ("Output goes to local_storage/audio/", File names section) doesn't say a second WAV is kept.
findings.suggestion: When output_format != 'wav', write the WAV to a tempfile (or AUDIO_DIR/.tmp) and unlink it after encoding, inside a try/finally so a failed ffmpeg run doesn't leave it either. Fix this together with the dedupe finding above, since the leftover WAV is currently what prevents most overwrites.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and the bug is real. Both `synthesize` (features/audio/text_to_speech.py:336-339) and `synthesize_dialogue` (:423-426) always write `AUDIO_DIR/<stem>.wav`. `_finalize_output` (:287-299) then encodes it to a sibling file: `_encode_flac` at :248-254, or `_encode_with_ffmpeg`/`_run_ffmpeg` at :268-284. Nothing in that path calls unlink or removes the WAV. features/audio/routes.py (`/tts`, `/tts/dialogue`) and features/audio/player.py don't clean it up either, and there is no delete endpoint. Two more checks found nothing that keeps the WAV on purpose. No test in tests/test_text_to_speech.py asserts the WAV is kept or removed for non-WAV formats. The README's File names section only shows `.wav` examples and never says a second copy is kept.

I ran a mocked, read-only check with no file writes. `synthesize('hello there', output_format='mp3', title='Clip')` wrote `Clip.wav`, ran ffmpeg `Clip.wav -> Clip.mp3`, and made no unlink calls. `play_audio_file` returned 'choose' for files [Clip.mp3, Clip.wav] and query 'Clip'.

It is worse than the report says.
