findings.title: CLI 'play' says 'pick one below' but prints no list, and says 'Playing X.' when nothing plays
findings.detail: In _run_steps the play shortcut yields final_response with response=describe_play_result(result) and the structured `audio` dict. run_agent (agent.py:362-363) keeps only the text. With several matches the CLI prints 'Found 3 matching files - pick one below, or say "play number 1"', but the candidate names and numbers are only in the dropped audio.candidates, so the user can't tell which number is which file. With one match it prints 'Playing my-clip.wav.' and no audio is played. The CLI has no player, even though sounddevice/soundfile are already dependencies.
findings.suggestion: In run_agent, when event.get('audio') is present, print the numbered candidates for 'choose'. For 'play', either play the file (soundfile + sounddevice) or print 'Saved at local_storage/audio/<file>' instead of 'Playing'.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and reproduced the bug. In agent.py:184-188, `_run_steps` handles "play ..." by yielding `{"event": "final_response", "response": describe_play_result(result), "audio": result}`. `run_agent` (agent.py:362-363) keeps only `event.get("response", ...)`. The only other key it checks is `show_calendar`, so `audio` is thrown away. The CLI loop at agent.py:413 just runs `print(run_agent(user_input))`.

`describe_play_result` (features/audio/player.py:129-140) builds the text "Found N matching files - pick one below, or say \"play number 1\"" for a 'choose' result, and "Playing <file>." for a 'play' result. The numbered filenames exist only in `result["candidates"]`, and the CLI drops them.

This path is only reached from the CLI. Web `/ask` (core/agent_routes.py:99) and `/ask_stream` (:170) call `audio_play_result` first and render the `audio` data themselves, so they never reach the play shortcut in `run_agent`. No guard stops the CLI case.

Test coverage: tests/test_audio_tool.py only tests `play_audio_file` and `parse_play_command` on their own, and tests/test_agent_flow.py has no play test.

Read-only reproduction (stubbed `player._list_audio_files`, no file writes):
- `run_agent('play clip')` with 3 matches returns 'Found 3 matching files - pick one below, or say "play number 1".' and lists nothing.
- `run_agent('play my-clip')` with 1 match returns 'Playing my-clip.wav.' and no sound plays. Nothing in the CLI path calls sounddevice or soundfile; they are only used in core/speech_to_text.py and features/audio/text_to_speech.py.

Candidates are sorted newest-first by modification time, so a CLI user can't work out which number is which file. The comment at agent.py:180-183 shows that ignoring `audio` in the CLI was deliberate, but the text shown to the user is still wrong. This is a UX bug that affects only the CLI. Low severity is right, and the line numbers are accurate.

findings.title: README says '401 otherwise', but unauthenticated calls get a 303 to /login, which fetch() follows silently
findings.detail: core/ui.py's exception handler turns 401 into RedirectResponse('/login', 303), and the tests assert 303. Verified: an anonymous GET /tts/voices returns 303, and following it gives 200 text/html. The browser's fetch() follows the redirect, so res.ok is true and every res.ok check is bypassed. After a session loss (logout in another tab, cookie expiry), a chat submit shows nothing: the HTML lines fail JSON.parse and only reach console.error. TTS shows a generic 'Speech generation failed.', and calendar.js's loadCalendarMonth throws an unhandled rejection. The user is never told to log in again.
findings.suggestion: For non-navigation requests (fetch, or Accept without text/html, or the API paths), return 401 JSON and redirect only HTML page loads. Have the JS redirect to /login on 401. Then the README line becomes true.
findings.verification_note:
The claim holds up. README.md:105 says "All routes require a logged-in session (401 otherwise)". But every protected router (agent_router, speech_router, audio_router, calendar_router, logout_router) depends on core/auth.py:is_logged_in, which raises HTTPException(401). The handler at core/ui.py:48-52 turns that into RedirectResponse('/login', 303), so the 401 never reaches a client. The tests check for this 303 (tests/test_speech_routes.py:98,141,201,224,277; tests/test_calendar.py:110). Nothing in the tests covers what the client does with it.

I checked it with a read-only TestClient run against core.ui.app. Without following redirects, GET /tts/voices, GET /calendar/month, POST /ask_stream, POST /tts and POST /speech each return 303 with Location /login. When the redirect is followed, as fetch() does by default, each ends at 200 text/html with history [303].

What the client does with that:
- static/chat.js:63-99 (handleAskStream) checks only res.body, which exists. Every line of the HTML fails JSON.parse and goes only to console.error. clearStreamUI has already hidden the thinking indicator and the cards, so the user sees nothing at all.
- features/audio/static/tts.js:280-301 ends in the catch block and shows the generic "Speech generation failed." The extract-text (:156) and convert (:365) calls fail the same way. loadVoices (:47) and the saved-file search (:444) fail with only a generic message or a console error.
- features/calendar/static/calendar.js:31-35 (loadCalendarMonth) has no try/catch, so res.json() throws an unhandled rejection.
- One more case the finding missed: static/speech.js:35-42 (the mic onstop handler) also throws an unhandled rejection.

No JS file checks res.redirected or res.url, and nothing sends the user back to /login.

The trigger is realistic: logging out in another tab (POST /logout clears the session), the session cookie expiring (SessionMiddleware's default max_age is 14 days), or cleared cookies. A server restart does not trigger it, because the secret key is fixed.

One small correction to the mechanism: res.ok is true after the redirect, but every JS caller runs res.json() before it checks res.ok. On an HTML body, json() throws a SyntaxError, so the res.ok / data.error branch is never reached at all. It is not simply "bypassed". The result is the same as described. This also means the suggested fix needs both parts: the server must return 401 JSON for fetch/API requests, and the JS must check for 401 before calling res.json() and then redirect to /login. Without the JS part, tts.js would still show only the generic error. Severity is low, as stated, and it is correctly marked as a cross-file contract change (the server's auth response plus every fetch caller).

findings.title: Plain /ask shows an empty audio card when play fails
findings.detail: stream_audio.html hides #stream-audio only when audio_data is falsy, but audio_play.html renders content only for status 'play' or 'choose'. When play_audio_file returns {status:'error', ...} (no match, or 'play number 9' out of range), /ask passes it as audio_data. Verified with POST /ask input='play zz-no-such-file-qq': the page has `<div id="stream-audio" class="response-card">` with empty content, an empty bordered and padded card. The streamed path (audio-player.js:22) hides the card on error, so the two renderers disagree.
findings.suggestion: Use `{% if not audio_data or audio_data.status not in ('play','choose') %} hidden{% endif %}`, or only pass audio_data from /ask when status != 'error'.
findings.verification_note:
I traced the code and reproduced the bug; it holds. In core/agent_routes.py lines 99-104, POST /ask passes `audio_data: audio_result` for any non-None result of play_audio_file, and that includes {status:'error'}. features/audio/player.py returns an error at lines 99, 102, 105 and 116 (no match, no previous list, number out of range). In features/audio/templates/audio/stream_audio.html, line 3 adds `hidden` only when audio_data is falsy, and an error dict is truthy. The template then includes audio_play.html, which has branches only for 'play' and 'choose', so the card renders with nothing inside it. static/styles.css lines 114-136 give .response-card 20px padding, a 30px top margin, a background and a border, so the empty card is visibly drawn. The streamed renderer handles this case differently: audio-player.js lines 22-25 hide #stream-audio on error. Reproduction (read-only, in the venv): I set core.auth.PASSWORD to a test value, logged in with TestClient, stubbed player._list_audio_files to return [], and sent POST /ask with input='play zz-no-such-file-qq'. It returned 200 with `
\n \n
` (no `hidden`), and the "No saved audio file matches" text appeared in the separate response card. No test covers this. test_agent_flow.py only covers the 'play' and 'choose' results on /ask, and the error tests in test_audio_tool.py check only the dicts and never render the page. How often it happens: lower than the finding suggests, which supports keeping it at low severity. static/chat.js line 130 intercepts the main chat form and sends it to /ask_stream, so in normal browser use plain /ask is reached only in these cases: - JavaScript is disabled, or someone POSTs to /ask directly. - The permission-approval form posts to /ask. Play requests never reach that form, because they skip the LLM. - The server-rendered choice buttons in audio_play.html post "play number N" to /ask. These only appear on a plain-/ask "choose" page. They return an error if _last_candidates is stale, for example after one pick has already cleared it (back button, then pick another) or after a server restart (frequent under --reload). The bug is real but cosmetic, and it only shows on the plain /ask path. The suggested fix is correct: hide the card unless status is 'play' or 'choose', or don't pass audio_data on error.

findings.title: .env is loaded only by the web app, so the CLI ignores it
findings.detail: load_dotenv() is called only in core/ui.py. core/llm.py reads OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_MODEL, OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL, OLLAMA_NUM_CTX and OLLAMA_TIMEOUT at import time, and text_to_speech.py reads TTS_DEVICE and KOKORO_CACHE_DIR. Under uvicorn they see .env values because core/ui.py loads it before importing agent. `python -m agent` never loads .env. Example: setting OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL=qwen3:8b in .env (the README's light-model tip) changes the web UI, while the CLI still calls qwen3-coder:30b and fails if that model isn't pulled.
findings.suggestion: Call load_dotenv() once in a module both entry points import first, e.g. config/__init__.py or the top of core/llm.py, or explicitly in agent.py's __main__. Say in the README that .env is supported.
findings.verification_note:
The mechanism is real. I checked it with grep and with a read-only import. `load_dotenv()` is called only in core/ui.py:1-3, and it runs before core.agent_routes imports agent, so the web app sees .env values. No other module loads dotenv: core/__init__.py and config/__init__.py don't, and neither does anything agent.py imports. Running `python -c "import sys, agent; ..."` in the venv printed `core.ui loaded: False` and `dotenv loaded: False`. The `__main__` block (agent.py:386) never loads it either. core/llm.py:5-24 reads OLLAMA_URL, OLLAMA_MODEL, OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL, OLLAMA_NUM_CTX and OLLAMA_TIMEOUT at import time. The CLI also imports features/audio/text_to_speech.py through features/audio/player.py:16, and that module reads TTS_DEVICE and KOKORO_CACHE_DIR at import time (lines 32-39). So any of these values placed in .env would be seen by uvicorn but not by `python -m agent`.

The example in the finding is wrong, though. The README's light-model tip (README.md:83) says to set a shell variable with `set -x OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL qwen3:8b`. It does not mention .env. A shell variable reaches both entry points, so following the documented tip does not cause the failure described. The README (lines 74-94) documents these variables only as environment variables and never mentions .env or python-dotenv. .env is gitignored. The only variable read from it in this repo is APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD (core/auth.py:8), and that is used only by the web app. I could not read .env (permission denied), but it is 28 bytes, which fits a single login-password line. The failure therefore needs a user to put Ollama/TTS settings in .env, which nothing documents. This is a latent inconsistency, not a break in a documented contract. Severity is nit/low.
findings.corrected: python-dotenv is loaded only in core/ui.py:3, before the import chain that pulls in agent, so only the web app reads .env. `python -m agent` (agent.py:386) never calls load_dotenv. Confirmed: importing agent leaves dotenv and core.ui out of sys.modules. core/llm.py:5-24 (OLLAMA_*) and features/audio/text_to_speech.py:32-39 (TTS_DEVICE, KOKORO_CACHE_DIR, which the CLI imports through features/audio/player.py:16) read their variables at import time. So a user who puts these settings in .env gets them in the web UI but silently not in the CLI. Example: OLLAMA_CODE_MODEL=qwen3:8b in .env changes the web tool loop, while the CLI still uses qwen3-coder:30b. The README never documents .env. Its light-model tip (README.md:83) uses a shell `set -x`, which works for both entry points, and the only variable the repo reads from .env today is the web-only APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD. This is a latent, undocumented-path inconsistency (severity nit/low), not a failure of the documented setup. Fix: call load_dotenv() in a module both entry points import first (e.g. the top of core/llm.py or config/__init__.py), or in agent.py's __main__. Optionally mention .env support in the README.

findings.title: Some storage paths depend on the working directory, others don't
findings.detail: LOG_FILE ('local_storage/logs.txt'), CALENDAR_FILE (features/calendar/calendar.py:6), NOTE_FOLDER (tools/notes.py:5), the /speech temp file (core/speech_routes.py:15), StaticFiles('static') and TEMPLATE_DIRS all depend on the working directory. AUDIO_DIR, tools/files.BASE_DIR and tools/verify.BASE_DIR are anchored to the repo. Running `python ~/Desktop/Source/agent0/agent.py` from $HOME works, because the script dir is on sys.path, but it writes calendar events and logs to ~/local_storage/, while the audio and file tools use the project. Also, local_storage/temp.wav (the last voice recording) is never deleted.
findings.suggestion: Define one PROJECT_ROOT / STORAGE_DIR (e.g. in config/settings.py) and build every storage, static and template path from it. Write /speech uploads to a tempfile and delete them after transcription.
findings.verification_note:
Checked against the code, and every part of the claim holds. core/logger.py:5 (LOG_FILE), features/calendar/calendar.py:6 (CALENDAR_FILE), tools/notes.py:5 (NOTE_FOLDER, created with mkdir when the module is imported), core/speech_routes.py:15 (temp_path), core/ui.py:25-27 (StaticFiles for static/favicon/media) and core/templates.py:5 (TEMPLATE_DIRS) all use paths relative to the working directory. AUDIO_DIR (features/audio/text_to_speech.py:12-14), tools/files.py:5 BASE_DIR and tools/verify.py:7 BASE_DIR are built from __file__, so they always point into the repo. The feature static dirs in features/*/routes.py are also anchored to __file__.

I tested the mismatch: I imported `agent` from a different working directory (a scratchpad dir) with the repo on sys.path. The import worked. LOG_FILE, CALENDAR_FILE and NOTE_FOLDER resolved to <cwd>/local_storage, and tools/notes.py created that folder on import. AUDIO_DIR and files.BASE_DIR still pointed to the repo. So storage really is split, as the finding says.

core/speech_routes.py overwrites local_storage/temp.wav on each request and never deletes it. The file is in the repo's local_storage/ now. Nothing in core/, features/, tools/ or agent.py removes it.

The suggestion would not break tests: tests/test_calendar.py:19 monkeypatches calendar_mod.CALENDAR_FILE, and that still works if the constant is built from a root path.

One small addition: core/speech_to_text.py:52, the CLI's `listen`, also leaves its NamedTemporaryFile (delete=False) behind.

Low severity is right. The web app run from another directory would fail at StaticFiles('static') rather than split storage silently; the silent split is in the CLI.

findings.title: Some comments may still not match the code
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md:22 says each feature provides `<name>/head.html`, but no head.html exists. Feature CSS is linked from body partials (tts_dashboard.html:1, calendar_card.html:1). config/system_prompt.py:35 tells the LLM 'JavaScript belongs in static/, templates in templates/', and extract_inline_scripts defaults to static/<name>.js (tools/files.py:192). Both contradict the feature-folder convention: features/<name>/static and features/<name>/templates. So LLM-driven moves of feature scripts land in the shared static/. core/llm.py:7-15 justifies the default with 'qwen3:4b' and 'a 4B model', but the default is qwen3:8b.
findings.suggestion: Fix CLAUDE.md to match the actual include pattern (or add the head.html partials), update the system prompt's layout rule to cover features/<name>/{static,templates}, and refresh the llm.py comment.
findings.verification_note:
Every factual claim checks out against the code.
(1) CLAUDE.md:22 says each feature provides `<name>/head.html`. No head.html exists anywhere in the repo, and git history shows none was ever added. The line was introduced in commit 2bb9640 alongside the index.html refactor. Feature CSS is linked from body partials: features/audio/templates/audio/tts_dashboard.html:1 links /static/audio/audio.css, and features/calendar/templates/calendar/calendar_card.html:1 links /static/calendar/calendar.css. templates/index.html <head> includes only components/favicons.html.
(2) config/system_prompt.py:34-35 says "JavaScript belongs in static/, templates in templates/". tools/files.py:192 defaults extract_inline_scripts' dest to `static/{stem}.js`, and the registry description at tools/registry.py:29 says the same. Neither mentions features/<name>/static or features/<name>/templates, which is how the audio and calendar features are actually laid out (see the MOUNTS in tools/verify.py:14-20).
(3) The core/llm.py:7-10 comment names "qwen3:4b" and line 14-15 says "a 4B model", but the default at line 11 is "qwen3:8b". README.md:52/78 also documents qwen3:8b.
Minor nuances that don't change the verdict: the default static/<stem>.js destination still works, because the /static mount serves it and verify_app would pass, so this is convention drift, not breakage. No feature template currently contains inline <script> blocks, so the misplacement is latent. The LLM can still pass an explicit dest. Low severity is appropriate.
findings.status_note:
CLAUDE.md and the system prompt describe the new loop and approvals. Other stale comments were not reviewed.

Originally reported as: CLAUDE.md, the system prompt and llm.py comments no longer match the code

findings.title: The tracked Claude Code allow-list lets `cat .env` run without a prompt despite the Read(.env) deny
findings.detail: The deny list blocks Read(.env), Read(**/*.key) and similar, but the allow list auto-approves Bash(cat:*), Bash(head:*), Bash(tail:*) and Bash(rg:*). Claude Code's Read deny rules apply to its file tools, not to Bash subprocesses, so `cat .env` (which holds APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD) or `rg . .env` runs without a prompt. That defeats the deny rule's intent.
findings.suggestion: Drop the blanket cat/head/tail/rg allows (Claude has Read/Grep tools for this), or add matching Bash deny patterns such as Bash(cat .env*), or enable the sandbox so the deny is enforced at the OS level.
findings.verification_note:
.claude/settings.json is tracked in git and does allow Bash(cat:*), head, tail, wc and rg (lines 13-17). Its deny list is lines 24-32. No sandbox is enabled and there are no Bash deny rules in ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json or the managed settings. .env exists, and core/auth.py:8 reads APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD from it.

The finding's main example is wrong, though. I tested on a public, non-secret file that the Read(**/*.pem) deny also covers (venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/certifi/cacert.pem):
- The Read tool was denied.
- `head -n 3 <that file>` and `cat <that file>` were both denied, even though Bash(head:*) and Bash(cat:*) are allow-listed.
- `head` on core.py in the same folder (not covered by any deny) worked.

So Claude Code does check file arguments of Bash read commands against Read deny rules, and a plain `cat .env`, `head .env` or `tail .env` would not run without a prompt.

The deny can still be got around, so the core concern holds:
1. Wildcard arguments slip through. `wc -c venv/.../certifi/*.pem` was auto-approved and read the denied file through the allow-listed wc. By the same route, `cat .en?` would likely be auto-approved by Bash(cat:*). I did not run it on .env.
2. Searching a whole folder slips through. `rg -c --no-ignore PATTERN certifi/` (via the rg allow) and `grep -rc PATTERN certifi/` both searched inside cacert.pem. grep is not in any allow list, so Claude Code's own auto-approval of read-only commands let it through. That means `grep -r APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD .`, or `rg -uu APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD .`, would print the password line with no prompt. (-uu is needed because .env is gitignored at .gitignore:8/35 and is a hidden file.)

The suggested fix is therefore partly wrong. Removing the cat/head/tail/rg allows would not stop recursive grep. Bash deny patterns like Bash(cat .env*) only cover the form that is already blocked, and they are easy to get around. Only the sandbox enforces the deny at the OS level.

Reachability: this concerns the Claude Code developer tool (Claude itself, or a prompt injection inside a Claude Code session). It has nothing to do with agent0's runtime, its routes, or its LLM. Low severity, close to informational, is right for a single-user local repo.
findings.corrected: The tracked .claude/settings.json Read(.env) and Read(**/.env*) denies (lines 25-28) do not fully protect .env (APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD) from Claude Code's Bash tool. However, a direct `cat .env`, `head .env` or `tail .env` is not the gap. Claude Code checks Bash file arguments against Read deny rules: cat and head on a Read(**/*.pem)-denied file were refused, even with Bash(cat:*) and Bash(head:*) allowed. Two gaps remain. First, wildcard arguments run under the allow list: `wc -c dir/*.pem` was auto-approved, so `cat .en?` would likely run through Bash(cat:*) at line 13. Second, searching a whole folder is not checked: `rg -uu APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD .` runs via Bash(rg:*) at line 17. `grep -r APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD .` needs no allow entry at all, because Claude Code auto-approves read-only commands. Either one prints the secret with no prompt. Removing the cat/head/tail/rg allows narrows this, but does not close it, and Bash deny patterns are easy to get around. The reliable fix is to enable the sandbox, which enforces deny-read at the OS level, or to accept that Read denies are best-effort. Severity: low or informational. This is about the Claude Code tool's settings, not agent0's runtime.

findings.title: The .bat launchers and agent0-ui.desktop still hardcode one machine's paths
findings.detail: Both .bat launchers `cd /d C:\AI\projects\agent0`, and agent0-ui.desktop hardcodes Exec/Icon under /home/hms/Desktop/Source/agent0, so they only work on the author's machines. The fish scripts derive the path correctly. The .desktop Comment says '(uvicorn --reload)', but the script runs without --reload and binds 0.0.0.0. README's Windows .bat snippet runs `uvicorn core.ui:app` on localhost without starting Ollama, while desktop/start_agent_ui.bat starts Ollama unconditionally and binds 0.0.0.0, so the two disagree.
findings.suggestion: Use `cd /d %~dp0..` in the .bat files, generate or document the .desktop path (or install it with a small script), bind 127.0.0.1 by default, and make the README point to the desktop/ launchers instead of a diverging inline copy.
findings.verification_note:
Every factual claim checks out. desktop/start_agent.bat:3 and desktop/start_agent_ui.bat:3 both run `cd /d C:\AI\projects\agent0`. desktop/agent0-ui.desktop:5-6 hardcodes Exec and Icon under /home/hms/Desktop/Source/agent0. desktop/start_agent_ui.fish:4-5 works out the project root from the script's own location. The .desktop Comment (line 4) says "(uvicorn --reload)", but start_agent_ui.fish:17 runs `uvicorn core.ui:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` with no --reload. README.md:64-72 has an inline .bat that runs plain `uvicorn core.ui:app` (localhost) and never starts Ollama. desktop/start_agent_ui.bat runs `start /min ollama serve` every time and binds 0.0.0.0. So the inconsistency is real and the severity is low.

Two parts of the suggestion overreach. First, "bind 127.0.0.1 by default" assumes the 0.0.0.0 bind is a mistake, and it probably isn't. The app has password and session login (core/auth.py: APP_LOGIN_PASSWORD, /login, is_logged_in on agent and speech routes, and a 401 redirect in core/ui.py:47-51). That suggests reaching the UI from another device on the LAN (for example, voice from a phone) is intended. Switching to 127.0.0.1 would break that, so it is a choice to discuss, not a fix. Second, a .desktop Exec/Icon entry has to be an absolute path, because the spec has no way to resolve a path relative to the file. The hardcoding can't be removed inside the file itself. The only real fix is the option the reviewer already lists: an install step that writes the path in, or documentation.
findings.corrected: Launchers are inconsistent and partly tied to one machine (low severity). desktop/start_agent.bat:3 and desktop/start_agent_ui.bat:3 hardcode `cd /d C:\AI\projects\agent0`. The fix is `cd /d "%~dp0.."`, which works out the path the same way the fish scripts already do. desktop/agent0-ui.desktop:5-6 hardcodes Exec/Icon under /home/hms/Desktop/Source/agent0. .desktop files need absolute paths, so the fix is a small install script that writes the path in, or a note in the README. The .desktop Comment (line 4) says "(uvicorn --reload)", but desktop/start_agent_ui.fish:17 runs without --reload; correct the comment. README.md:64-72 has its own inline .bat (localhost, no Ollama start), which has drifted from desktop/start_agent_ui.bat (starts Ollama, binds 0.0.0.0). The README should point to the desktop/ launchers instead of carrying a separate copy. The 0.0.0.0 bind looks intentional: core/auth.py adds password/session login, which points to LAN access. Keep the bind, or make the host configurable (for example an AGENT0_HOST env var) and state the exposure clearly. Don't silently change the default to 127.0.0.1, because that would break remote access from other devices.
findings.status_note: The fish launcher derives the project root and the new systemd units use %h paths. start_agent_ui.bat (C:\AI\projects\agent0) and agent0-ui.desktop (/home/hms) are unchanged. Originally reported as: Launchers hardcode one machine's paths and don't match the README

findings.title: Runs waiting for approval live in process memory
findings.detail: A run waiting for approval is kept in memory for up to 30 minutes (at most 50 at a time). A server restart, or a second worker process, loses it; the approval card then says the approval is no longer valid and the user sends the request again. Accepted for a single-user local app, as part of the 17 Oct 2026 decision to resume stored runs.
findings.suggestion: If the app ever runs with several workers or must survive restarts, keep paused runs in a small local database keyed by run id.

findings.title: An approved web tool stays approved for the whole login session
findings.detail: After the first approval, search_web, get_news or read_web_content runs without asking until logout. Later queries, which can contain project text the model has read, then go to remote search providers without a prompt. Chosen by the owner on 17 Oct 2026 (approve once per session, per tool).
findings.suggestion: Show which web tools are approved this session and let the user revoke them, or expire the approval after a while.

findings.title: The calendar shortcut also triggers on "set" and "plan"
findings.detail: To support requests like "set a meeting from 11 to 1 tomorrow", the trigger words now include "set" and "plan". Any sentence with one of the trigger words, a meeting word and "at/from <time>" creates an event directly, without the approval rule that create_calendar_event has. This slightly widens the shortcut over-matching listed under shortcomings.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before writing when the sentence is a question, or route borderline phrasings to the model.

findings.title: Tool calls written as text are still run
findings.detail: qwen3-coder sometimes writes its tool call into the reply text instead of the tool interface, so the loop also reads calls from qwen markup or JSON in the text. A model that quotes an example call in prose could therefore trigger it. The call still goes through the same approval rules. Accepted because without it the tool loop failed in live testing.
findings.suggestion: Re-check if a model update makes Ollama's own parsing reliable, and drop the fallback then.

findings.title: A stopped request is still stored as a conversation turn
findings.detail: `ndjson_response` wraps the stream in `cancel.scoped`, but the stream is already wrapped by `conversations.record`. After a stop, the closed Ollama connection raises `LLMError`, `_loop` turns it into an error event, and `record` saves the turn before `scoped` drops the event. The next request is then sent the question with '(Failed: Could not reach Ollama...)' as its answer.
findings.suggestion: Put `record` outside `scoped`, or skip saving a cancelled request. Add a test where the fake chat raises `LLMError` after the stop (tests/test_cancel.py only yields the final event). docs/features/agent-loop.md and conversation-memory.md both say a stopped request isn't stored.
findings.verification_note: Reproduced with fakes: the event was dropped but the row was stored with the failure text.

findings.title: Two newest tool results are exempt from pruning and can each fill half the context budget
findings.detail: `MAX_RESULT_CHARS` is `CONTEXT_BUDGET_TOKENS*2` (about 49k characters), and `prune_messages` never stubs the newest 2 results. Two near-cap results back to back equal the whole 24.5k-token budget before the system prompt, history and question. The estimate is characters/4, and code and JSON tokenize worse than that, so the prompt can pass the 32768 window.
findings.suggestion: Lower `MAX_RESULT_CHARS` to about a quarter of the budget, or shrink the newest results when stubbing older ones is not enough, and leave headroom for thinking tokens.
findings.verification_note: Confirmed by reading core/context.py; the overflow needs two near-cap results in a row.
findings.corrected: The newest 2 results are exempt and each can be about half the budget, so two near-cap results in a row can pass the budget and, with a chars/4 underestimate, possibly num_ctx. What Ollama then drops is unverified.

findings.title: The per-file caps from cap_each are undone by a second cap over the JSON text
findings.detail: `_run_call` caps each file with `cap_each`, turns the result into a JSON string, and `_tool_result` then runs `cap_result` over that string. JSON escaping makes it longer than the limit, so the second cap cuts the end of the JSON: a whole file's text disappears and the 'lines N-M omitted' numbers count lines of a one-line string. Reproduced with three files of about 47k characters.
findings.suggestion: Skip the second cap when `cap_each` already ran, or apply `cap_each` only inside `_tool_result`.
findings.verification_note: Reproduced: three large files gave a 58k-character string, and the cut removed the last key.

findings.title: Any prune turns off the repeat-call guard for the rest of the run
findings.detail: When `prune_messages` returns a pruned copy, `run.attempted.clear()` runs. Once history is over budget that happens every step, so a model that repeats the same call is never stopped before `MAX_STEPS`.
findings.suggestion: Remove only the signatures whose results were stubbed; `prune_messages` would need to report which.

findings.title: One long question evicts all older history, and newlines in tool arguments split the 'Tools used' line
findings.detail: Only the answer is capped (`TURN_ANSWER_CHARS`); a question over `HISTORY_CHARS` (6000) makes `history_messages` stop and drop that turn and every older one. A newline in a tool argument is not removed from the one-line action summary, so it can produce extra entries.
findings.suggestion: Cap the question length in `history_messages` and collapse newlines in action summaries.
findings.corrected: A robustness issue, not a security one: replaying the model's own earlier answer in a single-user local app crosses no new trust boundary.

findings.title: edit_file and write_file rewrite CRLF files as LF, and the backup is already converted
findings.detail: Files are read in text mode and written back with 'w', so a CRLF file ends up with LF only, and the backup is written from the converted text, so it is not byte-identical to the original.
findings.suggestion: Open with `newline=''` for reading and writing, or copy the original bytes to the backup.

findings.title: A failed conversion can leave a partial converted_* file in local_storage/audio
findings.detail: `_save_output` removes its output when it fails, but `convert_audio_file` only deletes the upload. If ffmpeg stops part way, a partly written file stays, and the player lists it because it only skips zero-byte files.
findings.suggestion: Remove `out_path` on failure, as `_save_output` does.

findings.title: Killing the server mid-generation leaves a zero-byte file that keeps its name forever
findings.detail: `_reserve_output_path` creates the final file before synthesis and cleans up only in an `except`. A kill (the 30-minute idle exit, or kill -9) leaves the empty file. It is hidden from listings but still blocks the name, and nothing removes it.
findings.suggestion: Remove empty files older than a few minutes at startup or when listing.

findings.title: purge_request does not catch OSError, so a log error in the stop path can leave the request unfinished
findings.detail: `log_event` catches OSError but `purge_request` does not. It is called from the `finally` block in core/cancel.py, so an error there (a locked file on Windows, a full disk) skips `request.done.set()` and the cleanup that follows.
findings.suggestion: Catch OSError around the rewrite and carry on.
findings.corrected: The only caller is the `finally` block in core/cancel.py, not an endpoint, so the effect is a stop that may hang or leak the request rather than a 500.

findings.title: The comment sizing history for an 8k window is out of date
findings.detail: It says the history fits the light model's 8k window. Both models now use 32768 and there is no light model; the 6000-character value itself is safe.
findings.suggestion: Update the comment.

findings.title: The code model does not load the move-code-out-of-file skill, and saves a note on its own
findings.detail: Running 'Move the function create_event out of features/calendar/calendar.py into a new file features/calendar/events.py' twice on qwen3-coder:30b, the model never called `load_skill`; it read files, tried write_file/edit_file (denied in the test) and then called `save_note` with its own answer, which the low-risk rule runs without asking. The two-line rule in the system prompt is all that guards the 'never delete code first' behaviour.
findings.suggestion: Load a skill deterministically when the request matches (as `planned_first_decision` does for the script refactor), and consider asking before `save_note` runs when the user did not ask for a note.
findings.verification_note: Reproduced twice against the real model; each time a stray note file was written and removed afterwards.

findings.title: Feature docs promise two guarantees the code doesn't keep
findings.detail: docs/features/permissions.md says file tools resolve every path inside the project 'symlinks included'; a symlink to an outside file is accepted (see the _safe_path finding). docs/features/agent-loop.md and conversation-memory.md say a stopped request isn't stored; it can be (see the stopped-request finding). The docs/ folder is otherwise consistent with the code: file paths, defaults, limits and endpoints I checked match.
findings.suggestion: Fix the code for both (small changes) or soften the two sentences.
findings.verification_note: Each claim was compared with the code and a reproduction.

findings.title: One malformed skill file crashed every tool-loop request
findings.detail: The loader split the file on '---' and unpacked three parts, so a skill with no closing '---' (or a non-UTF-8 file) raised an error inside `system_message()`, which runs on every request.
findings.suggestion: Skip unreadable or malformed skills.
findings.verification_note: Reproduced by two reviewers.
findings.status_note: `_parse` uses a line-anchored regex and skips unreadable files, files without frontmatter and files without a body (tools/skills.py). Covered by a test.

findings.title: Skills were looked up relative to the working directory
findings.detail: `SKILL_FOLDER = Path('skills')` found nothing when the server started from another directory, leaving the prompt pointing at a skill that did not exist.
findings.suggestion: Anchor the folder to the code.
findings.verification_note: Reproduced from a different directory.
findings.status_note: `SKILL_FOLDER` is now resolved from `__file__`. Covered by a test that changes directory.

findings.title: Duplicate skill names silently overwrote each other and an empty skill returned nothing
findings.detail: The later file won a duplicate name and an empty body returned an empty string.
findings.suggestion: First file wins; skip empty skills.
findings.verification_note: Reproduced.
findings.status_note: `_skills()` keeps the first file for a name and `_parse` skips empty bodies. Covered by a test.

findings.title: A request a skill covers was answered from the model's own knowledge
findings.detail: The local-first call answered 'give me a weekly report' with a generic template: it never reached the tool loop, so `load_skill` was never called. Found by running the real model.
findings.suggestion: List the skills in the local-first prompt so a matching request escalates.
findings.verification_note: Run against qwen3.6:35b before and after the change.
findings.status_note: `local_only_prompt()` adds the skill list (agent.py); the same request now loads the skill, calls search_history and list_notes, and writes the report from them.

findings.title: The local-first prompt has no current date
findings.detail: The tool-loop system prompt includes the date and time (`system_message`), but `LOCAL_ONLY_PROMPT` does not, so a direct answer about 'today' or 'this week' is unanchored.
findings.suggestion: Append the same date line when building the local-first messages.
findings.verification_note: Checked by the agent-loop reviewer against agent.py.

decisions.title: How approvals resume
decisions.options: A: store the run on the server under a run id. B: keep a running list of decisions per tool and arguments.

decisions.title: Built-in tool calling
decisions.options: Move the tool loop to /api/chat with Ollama tools.
decisions.outcome: Yes, on condition it stays offline (it does). Implemented 17 Oct 2026.

decisions.title: Session secret
decisions.options: Required .env setting, or a new one at every start.
decisions.outcome: Required, at least 32 characters. Implemented 17 Oct 2026.

decisions.title: External access and notes
decisions.options: Should external tools ask? Should notes be tools?
decisions.outcome: External tools ask once per login session, per tool; notes are tools. Implemented 17 Oct 2026.

method: Six reviewers each covered one area: agent loop, web layer, tools, audio, calendar, and a repo-wide unused-code sweep. A completeness critic then looked for what they missed. 132 agents ran in total.
Baseline at review time: `python -m pytest` passed 121 tests; pyflakes reported only two unused `global` statements.
Severity is judged for a single-user app run locally, which may be reachable on the local network.
Several bugs were reproduced with a fake LLM rather than real model output, so how often the real model hits those paths is uncertain.
When several reviewers found the same issue, it is listed once, with the other reviewers under "Also found by".
Fix statuses are set by checking each finding against the code after each change. Accepted risks were added from decisions made while fixing.

22 Oct 2026 update: three area reviewers covered commit `c1338f9` and the working tree (agent loop, tools and skills, storage/UI/desktop), and three verifiers re-checked every new finding; refuted ones were dropped. The new findings' line numbers refer to the working tree on 22 Oct; older ones refer to `d0bacbe`.

Also run: the test suite (317 passed), the real models (qwen3.6:35b for the general loop and weekly-report, qwen3-coder:30b for the code request, with every write denied), and the code from docs/BUILD_YOUR_OWN_AGENT.md against qwen3:8b, which read a file through the guide's tool loop. docs/ was compared with the code: paths, defaults and limits match, apart from the two statements in the docs finding.
Not covered: static/speech.js, core/speech_routes.py and core/speech_to_text.py were not re-read, so findings 29, 30, 32 and 94 keep their old status.

summaries.text: Verdict on agent.py: it's well organised for a small-model agent, but it falls short in a few important ways. The good parts: one `_run_steps` generator is shared by the CLI and the web entry points, and there is practical hardening for weak models (JSON pulled out of fences, separate retry budgets for bad JSON and unknown tools, a planned first decision, lenient tool signatures in tools/files.py). The serious problems: (1) Permission resume is a stateless replay of the whole task. Approval is keyed only by action name, so approved arguments are never checked against what actually runs. Any task that needs two different 'ask' actions keeps asking forever and re-runs the earlier side effect each time (I reproduced this). (2) Nothing catches exceptions from `execute_tool` or `query_llm`. A wrong argument name, an unparseable date or Ollama being down kills the stream with no error event, crashes the CLI, and the model never gets to correct itself. (3) It uses a hand-written JSON protocol over /api/generate. The context is one growing string with no size limit and it leaves out the tool arguments, instead of using Ollama's /api/chat with native tools or structured outputs. Here that means fenced code inside JSON breaks parsing, and the model can't tell which file each read result came from. (4) The duplicate-call check blocks the re-verify and re-read steps that the system prompt and the edit_file error message both ask for. (5) Special cases differ by path: when the LLM itself calls read_calendar the grid opens the month of the earliest event ever, and when the LLM calls play_audio_file the audio payload is dropped. (6) Both routes run the blocking agent inside `async def` handlers. I measured another request being held up for the full length of an LLM call. Tests cover only the happy path. The 'direct answer' test actually passes through the JSON-retry fallback (4 LLM calls, 3 of them to the 30B model), and pytest writes into the real local_storage/logs.txt. Unfinished items: the registry's `external` flag, the `query_llm(stream=True)` path, the ignored permission_args/permission_risk form fields, and read_email, which the prompts mention but which is not registered. I checked every finding below by reading the code, and reproduced most with fake-LLM simulations through the venv. I changed no files.

I checked every point below in the code, and confirmed the main ones by running the app in memory with FastAPI's TestClient and httpx. The protected routers are all wired correctly: every router except public_router uses Depends(is_logged_in), and the GET catch-all is registered last, so it hides nothing. The real problems are elsewhere. The session secret is hardcoded, so a forged cookie got full access. The `/audio` static mount has no auth, and the desktop launchers bind to 0.0.0.0, so both are reachable from the local network. The permission flow approves by tool name only and re-runs the whole agent from scratch. In a probe I approved write_file for notes.txt and it ran write_file on agent.py. A task that needs two different gated tools loops on approvals forever. /ask, /ask_stream and /speech run blocking LLM and Whisper calls inside async handlers. A 3s fake LLM call held up a separate GET /login by about 2.8s. An exception partway through /ask_stream (for example Ollama being down) ends the stream without an error event, and chat.js has no error handling, so the spinner never stops. I found no XSS: chat.js only uses textContent, Jinja autoescapes, and audio-player.js and calendar.js escape before using innerHTML. CSRF is mostly blocked by Starlette's default SameSite=lax session cookie. core/logger.py writes to local_storage/logs.txt. The tracked root logs.txt is a one-line placeholder that nothing uses. check_imports.py is a standalone script that checks whether the project's imports load, and nothing references it. Side effect: one probe run (the permission-flow one) left logging switched on, so it appended a few JSONL lines to the gitignored local_storage/logs.txt, the same thing pytest does. My other probe scripts are in the session scratchpad.

I reviewed the tools layer: tools/files.py, web.py, notes.py, verify.py, email.py, registry.py, config/settings.py, core/permission.py and tests/test_web_tools.py. I checked each finding against the code, and ran most of them on a throwaway copy of the repo in the scratchpad, which I then deleted. No project files were modified. The path-traversal guard holds: `../`, absolute paths outside the project and sibling-directory tricks are all rejected. The real problems are elsewhere. (1) The lenient fallback in edit_file merges lines and strips indentation, so it silently corrupts code whenever the model retypes quotes. (2) Web approvals are tied only to the tool name, not its arguments, and each approval reruns the agent from scratch. When a task needs two gated tools, approvals loop forever and earlier writes run again. (3) Any exception from a tool kills the streamed response with no error shown. Wrong argument names trigger this, because several registry descriptions don't name their parameters, and so does a DDGS search with no results or no network. (4) verify_app reports "app imports cleanly" even when imported modules have syntax errors. (5) The `<script>` balance guard refuses every edit to tools/files.py, tools/registry.py and config/system_prompt.py. (6) extract_inline_scripts writes broken script URLs for destinations outside static/, and merges script blocks in a way that changes when they run. (7) The duplicate-call guard stops the model from re-running verify_app after a fix. On "unused" code: vulture's tool hits (get_project_structure, search_files, write_file, edit_file, extract_inline_scripts, verify_app, read_web_content, get_news, read_calendar) are all live, called through the dotted names in tools/registry.py. The genuinely unfinished pieces are read_email, the unused `external` registry flag, and notes, which only work from the web UI and not the CLI. RULES has no stale entries and every rule names a real tool. But "auto" on search_web and get_news contradicts the system prompt's "External access requires permission", and the ddgs "auto" backend sends queries to several search engines, not just DuckDuckGo. Apart from two smoke tests for tools/web.py, the tools layer has no direct tests.

The audio feature is mostly sound. Synthesis, conversion and extraction run through run_in_threadpool, so they don't block the event loop. ffmpeg is called with an argv list on fixed whitelisted paths, so shell injection isn't possible. StaticFiles blocks path traversal on /audio (verified: a 404 for an encoded ../). TTS titles are sanitized, Jinja autoescape is on, and audio-player.js escapes filenames. All 98 audio/speech-route tests pass.

The real problems:
- **Unauthenticated `/audio`:** the mount serves saved audio without login (verified 200 with no session), although the README says every route needs one.
- **"play" shortcut too broad:** it captures every chat message that starts with "play" ("Play chess with me", "play the role of..."), so the LLM never sees them.
- **Unfinished registry tool:** when the LLM calls play_audio_file, the result never reaches the UI, so nothing plays.
- **Filename handling:** the filename check only looks at .wav, so a new file can silently overwrite an existing .mp3/.flac/.ogg with the same name. MP3/FLAC/OGG output also leaves the .wav behind, so "play <title>" always asks you to choose between two files.
- **Model cache location:** KOKORO_CACHE_DIR is ignored in the running app because huggingface_hub is imported before the override (verified: Kokoro weights exist in both ~/.cache/huggingface/hub and models/kokoro).

Lower-severity items: Kokoro pipeline setup and use have no lock; upload size caps apply only after Starlette has already written the whole upload to disk; one unescaped innerHTML in tts.js; ffmpeg runs without -nostdin or a timeout; the Markdown flattener damages snake_case words; a few edge cases in the player and dashboard JS; redundant except branches.

Issues seen outside the audio area that affect it: core/agent_routes.py runs the synchronous LLM loop directly on the event loop, both in /ask (run_agent) and in /ask_stream (stream_agent iterated in an async generator). So /tts and even /audio requests stall while the LLM is thinking. Also, core/speech_to_text.py:9 loads WhisperModel at import time, which contradicts CLAUDE.md's lazy-loading rule and is what causes the cache-dir problem.

The calendar feature is small and mostly hangs together. Nothing in features/calendar is dead code: every helper is used, `read_calendar` exists and takes no arguments, and calendar.js escapes event names and descriptions before rendering, so there is no XSS. Prev/next month navigation handles Dec->Jan correctly. The real problems are in the natural-language shortcut layer and in how tool results are handed back. (1) The time parser turns common European times like "12.30" or "14.00" into the year 1230 or 1400. (2) It doesn't carry am/pm from the end time to the start time, and a reversed or past-midnight range makes `create_event` raise, which returns a 500 on /ask_stream and crashes the CLI. (3) The create shortcut matches anywhere in the sentence, so questions and negations ("did I schedule a meeting on 4 october at 12") write events without the permission prompt that config/settings.py sets to "ask". (4) `is_calendar_request` swallows create/delete requests and code questions that mention the calendar. (5) When the LLM calls `read_calendar`, the grid opens on the month of the oldest event ever stored, the LLM never sees the events, and the CLI prints a raw dict. Storage has two weaker spots: times are written as UTC 'Z' even though they are local, and the write is a non-atomic truncate-and-rewrite. One damaged .ics file breaks every calendar entry point. tests/test_calendar.py has no tests for `parse_create_command` or `_normalize_time_token`, which is where most of these bugs live.

I swept every tracked file for unused code. Truly dead code is rare: only tools/email.py:read_email has no references, plus a few stray files (root logs.txt, desktop/__init__.py, check_imports.py, a personal .md), one unused CSS rule and the httpx2 pin. All JS functions and other templates are referenced, and every other CSS class is used; vulture's hits are FastAPI route handlers or dotted registry strings.

Per-tool verdict (13 tools; all resolve and all are listed in the prompt; nothing filters what the model sees):
- **File tools** (get_project_structure, search_files, read_files, write_file, edit_file, extract_inline_scripts): work and are used. Keep.
- **verify_app**: reachable but can falsely report OK after a broken Python edit. Keep and fix.
- **search_web, read_web_content**: work. Keep.
- **get_news**: effectively broken (required `country` arg is never described; never chosen in about 1,366 logged decisions). Finish with DDGS.news or remove.
- **create_calendar_event**: works.
- **read_calendar**: works, but the LLM path opens the wrong month.
- **play_audio_file**: works via the regex shortcut, but nothing plays when the LLM calls it. Finish.
- **notes**: not registered and write-only. Register save/list tools.
- **email**: stub that the prompts still advertise. Remove the mentions, or implement read-only IMAP.

The biggest unfinished wiring is the registry's `external` flag, which nothing reads, while web tools are auto-approved against the system prompt's promise.

agent.py's loop is reasonable, but it has real bugs:
- tool exceptions (TypeError or ValueError) kill the stream or the CLI;
- approvals are bound to the action name, not the args, and re-run already-executed tools; a task needing two approvals loops forever (reproduced);
- sync LLM calls block the event loop.

Separately: a hard-coded session secret combined with launchers binding 0.0.0.0, and auto-approved read_files can read .env.

Most of the earlier coverage holds up. These 14 findings are new; each one was checked against the code, and several were reproduced with TestClient or a direct run. The biggest are: (1) the documented bare `pytest` command fails to collect any of the 7 test modules, because nothing puts the repo root on sys.path; (2) the README promises a 'diff preview before file writes', but core/diff.py's output is only printed to the server console after approval, right before the write; (3) a streamed request can never resume after approval, because the card posts to the blocking full-page /ask, which shows no progress; (4) agent.needs_tools treats any mention of 'file', 'project', 'template' or 'node.js' as a file task, so ordinary questions skip the local answer and go to the 30B tool loop. The only test of the permission path is vacuous: one assertion matches a heading that is on every page, and the other matches any response. I reproduced the resumed run ending in 'Max steps reached' after 9 LLM calls, and the test still passes. test_speech_routes.py covers TTS, not /speech, so /speech, notes, permission.py, streaming.py and verify.py have no direct tests. There are also three README claims the code doesn't meet ('All actions logged', '401 otherwise', 'diff preview'), a CLI that says 'pick one below' and prints no list, an empty audio card on errors in /ask, a CLI that never loads .env, storage paths relative to the working directory, CLAUDE.md and prompt drift, a Claude Code allow-list that undercuts its own .env deny rule, and launchers with hardcoded machine paths. core/streaming.py, core/logger.py's write path and the CI workflow had no further real defects beyond what was already reported.

The loop keeps tool calls and results paired, resumes exactly the parked call and reports errors as events. The new problems are around stop and context size: a stopped request can be stored, and pruning leaves two results that can use the whole budget.
File safety is much better: backups, secret-file rules, a safer lenient edit. The symlink hole and the unbalanced `<script>` guard remain. The skill loader had three robustness bugs, now fixed.

SQLite use is sound, FTS queries are quoted and chat.js writes model text with textContent. The systemd units bind localhost. Remaining issues are small: stray audio files after failures and working-directory-relative paths.

changelog.title: Approvals apply to the exact call and resume the stored run
changelog.detail: A call that needs approval stores the run on the server under a single-use id owned by the login session. Approving runs exactly that call and continues the run; denying tells the model, which finishes with an answer. Nothing is replayed from the start. (Decision: option A.)

changelog.title: Tool loop uses Ollama's built-in tool calling, still offline
changelog.detail: The loop calls the local /api/chat with tool schemas from the registry and keeps a real message history. The local-first check uses structured output. Fallbacks read calls the model writes into its text.

changelog.title: Errors no longer kill the stream
changelog.detail: Tool errors go back to the model so it can correct itself, Ollama errors become an error event, and the stream turns any other exception into one. The agent runs in a worker thread, and chat.js shows network and HTTP errors.

changelog.title: Agent loop details
changelog.detail: The prompt includes today's date, the repeat guard allows re-checking after an edit, the approval card resumes over the stream, and denials are passed back to the model.

changelog.title: Session secret required
changelog.detail: SESSION_SECRET (at least 32 characters) must be set in .env, or the app refuses to start. README explains how to generate one. (Decision: required setting.)

changelog.title: Web tools ask once per session; notes are tools
changelog.detail: Tools marked external ask the first time and stay approved until logout. save_note and list_notes are registered tools. The prompts no longer mention email. (Decision: approve once per session, per tool.)

changelog.title: Unused query_llm removed
changelog.detail: query_llm and its streaming path were deleted, with their tests; chat() replaced them.

changelog.title: Saved audio requires login
changelog.detail: /audio/<file> is now a route behind login instead of a public mount, with the same URLs, path checks and range requests.

changelog.title: Calendar times, ranges and relative days
changelog.detail: The "add a meeting" shortcut reads 12.30, 14.00, 1030 and 2pm, follows a 24-hour day for ranges, understands today/tomorrow/weekdays, asks when a date without a year has passed, and opens the calendar on the new event with its day highlighted.

changelog.title: Docs and tests
changelog.detail: CLAUDE.md and README describe the new loop, approvals, the session secret and the test command. The agent loop, approvals, notes and permissions have new tests.

changelog.title: Skills added; skill loading made reliable
changelog.detail: A `skills/` folder, a low-risk `load_skill` tool and a skill index in the system prompt. The 'moving code' rules moved out of the system prompt into a skill. Running the real model showed that requests a skill covers were answered locally, so the skill list is now in the local-first prompt too. The loader skips malformed or empty skill files and finds the folder from any working directory. The weekly-report skill dropped its calendar step because read_calendar ends the run without giving the model the events.

changelog.title: Review of the changes since the last review
changelog.detail: Checked commit c1338f9 and the working tree (context pruning, stop button, conversation memory, file safety, systemd units, skills) against the code, with three area reviewers and three verifiers. Statuses of older findings were re-checked; new findings were added; docs/ was compared with the code and the guide's code was run against a real model.

tasks.title: Load a skill deterministically when a request matches it
tasks.text: qwen3-coder did not call load_skill in two runs, and the local-first path only escalates; the move-code rules then rely on a two-line prompt pointer. Match the request against skill descriptions (or keywords in the frontmatter) and add a load_skill call as the planned first step, as planned_first_decision does for the script refactor.

tasks.title: Stop must not store the turn, and add the test that would have caught it
tasks.text: Put conversations.record outside cancel.scoped, and add a test where the fake chat raises LLMError after the stop. The docs already promise this behaviour.

tasks.title: Keep tool results inside the context window
tasks.text: Lower MAX_RESULT_CHARS, shrink the newest results when pruning older ones is not enough, stop re-capping the JSON text and use a lower characters-per-token estimate. Add a test with two near-cap results.

tasks.title: Keep file tools inside the project when a path is a symlink
tasks.text: Require the resolved path to stay under BASE_DIR in _safe_path and add traversal and symlink tests; the permissions doc already claims this.

tasks.title: Anchor the database, log, notes and skills paths to the project folder
tasks.text: DB_PATH, LOG_FILE and NOTE_FOLDER are relative to the working directory, so a manual run from another directory silently starts a second empty history. SKILL_FOLDER is already anchored; do the same for the rest.

tasks.title: Make read_calendar return its events to the model
tasks.text: The tool ends the run on the calendar grid, so skills and follow-up questions can't use calendar data. Return the events to the loop and open the grid separately.
